review_text:
[h1] It definitely was an experience, though a lot less cathartic than the original. [/h1]

And I'm not talking about "I've already seen it" kinda feel. In fact, it is a very different game, enough to justify being a sequel, not a remake. It works a lot better as a game, the mechanics finally enhance the narrative and you have a much harder time to escape all the challenges it throws at you, which makes the struggle element so consistent throughout, but it lacks... a narrative punch. Yes, now people can actually die of the plague! But... it feels like they made them more bland because of that? EDIT: I checked. Yeah. It is true. Even if the kiddos from the Isidor's list die, it changes... nothing. So the game built around the idea of mortality rewards you with nothing if someone dies AND doesn't punish you if they die? That's bullshit. Honestly, I feel betrayed here.

With some characters, they did find an interesting way to re-introduce them. With others... They became less. I can't say I felt strongly about characters other than Burakh's friends and the kiddos, and even then, not to all of them. 

The music is so not present, that sometimes I forget that it's even there. There are hardly any tracks I remember right after completing it, while the original is a treasure trove of great music. A bigger focus on ambience felt fresh at first, but by the second half I was bummed out that I can't run around the town vibing to the otherworldly tunes of P1. 

The intended difficulty is a lil overtuned, I'd say. Yes, now it is the point that you can't be everywhere and help everyone. Still, I barely have any time to finish up with the important biz! And the time is starting to flow faster and faster with each passing day! The game really expects you to loot the infected/cured parts of the town to keep your balance and meds up, but howwww, whennnnn. And deaths causing permanent effects on you and the city is cool, but the way Mark talks to you after you die is so eugghhhh.

I like how they overhauled the haruspex part of the gameplay. It was soso not obvious where to look for the herbs, or how to mix them to get something decent, but here it's pretty easy to understand and it does a good job of tying the narrative of being a traditional medicine healer into the gameplay. Being chased by the entire town for cutting out organs right in front of their eyes was thrilling. And assigning separate trust levels to each region of the town is a great idea. 

And speaking about the narrative... the message it tries to convey is iffy, yeah. I may be misremembering P1, but I feel like the overarching idea of progress vs traditions was better presented there. Here, it feels wrong. The way they portray the kin is... oof. I don't wanna spoil stuff, I'll just say that I think they done them really dirty here. 

[h2] It is still a great game, and I like how they reimagined lots of things, but I can't shake off the feeling that something is very wrong at the core of it. [/h2]
 
TL;DR: Instead of "ooooh, cooooool" kinda mindfuck of P1 I got "huuuhhhhh, whyyyyy?" kinda mindfuck of P2
I think I prefer what the Marble Nest was going for than the main game.

Got the game for free with my GPU purchase back when, the RX 6800 XT.

The game went through abnormal performance issues at launch with ray tracing issues on AMD and even without then having massive stutters in menu. 

 I gave the game time to cook, some 2 years later, and performance is good. 
If you want to enable raytracing you need to enable temporal anti-ailising for it to become available. AMD & Nvidia. 
 With RX 6800XT on 1440p and FSR 2 and 3700x CPU (and 48GB RAM), I was able to run max RT settings without noticeable performance issues.

Regarding the actual game play and story, it is decent. Despite being created by former Dead Space devs, the game's atmosphere isn't that anxiety inducing / scary. The story is decent and I believe you need the DLC to conclude it, but the base game is good on its own. Combat is easy and for most part you never feel in danger / scared. 

It is only on the end game boss fight (main / base game) that you really get challenged. I still have yet to play the Final Transmission DLC that continues the story, so things might change in that.

Overall, game is decent and better priced now than at launch. If you are interested but wary, get it on sale. I got the season pass recently at roughly $2 for additional content.

So, decent game and easy enough combat with decent story. Worth it for good 20 - 25+ hours play time (excluding DLC).

review_text:
Update 12/24/21: This game uses a crap ton of system and video ram. If you have a bunch of programs running in the background you might need more than 16Gigs. the game by itself uses about 9-10. The video is another story. On low settings its eating right around 5-6 gigs of video ram. 6 gig cards are gonna notice performance issues and I wouldnt even  bother trying to play with a 4gig or less card. I've got a 3080 and once youre actually in the game (Not just the hub) Video Ram utilization is almost 9 gigs!!!! This is on high quality settings. Index controllers are still broken. 

UPDATE: December patch broke the game for index users so now its actually worse....FIX IT FIT IT FIX IT. 


Stuff I like

1. Graphics.......Textures on PC look decent not great not horrible
2. Character models look good Visually although their heads have this weird tendency to move independent of their bodies so it gives the impression its a headless body with a
Mannequin head stuck on top....the animations can be off.
3. quick reload just like arizona sunshine. (F--cked up in the latest patch so ignore) Gun mechanics are good so far of what ive unlocked.
4. interior environments are very detailed and colors pop nicely on my vive pro with and OLED screen.
5. Voice acting is serviceable and better than alot of other games

Stuff that sucks

1. No proper multiplayer game browser just a CUE...This is bad because youre forced to play with people that might be on the other side of the planet with Horrible ping times. Being this is a PEER to PEER server model this can cause the game to run like trash. I also found it hard to play specific maps because every time i joined the cue it was either skidrow or chinatown and after 15 minutes i just started a single player game on my own to play the other maps

2. Cross play is a good idea but it seems an oculus quest doesnt have the horsepower and or the option for a hardwired connection. again this uses a peer to peer model so everyone will be subject to the hosts crappy 2.4ghz connection if thats what theyre using on top possibly being on the other side of the planet and using a quest as a server. Not trying to hate on the quest since i have one and like it but 3/4s of the players seem to be oculus users and every single game ive played where an oculus user is the host has run like complete garbage.

3. Index controller problems.....there needs to be an index controller grip intensity slider added to the options....I keep unintentionally holstering and switching weapons constantly. This is insanely annoying and has gotten me killed a few times.

4. No character choice or development......I know all the characters play pretty much the same in lefft 4 dead and have no problem with that here but you should at least have the option to pick your character. They also have zero personality through their voice acting mainly because of what little they say. with the exception of the narrator character. he was actually pretty good....totally forgetable.

5. Outdoor environments are bland.....I get it ...its snow but it seems like it was just an excuse to use weather effects to limit draw distance.

6. Hands are way to sticky.......i walk by an openable door and all of a sudden my hand models are 3 feet away from my body but my physical hands are at my sides.

7. Enemy models look ok but the textures all look the same. Arizona sunshine suffered from this but this is worse. except for size they all look the same......at least mix the colors and clothes up just to give some variance.

8. please ad some kind of an auto height adjustment for the player models.....it looks so F--ckin stupid with an entire team running around looking like hunchbacks bent over.

9. No campaign.....Huge mistake.....just like back for blood i think alot of people will play it right now but in a month or 2 the player base wil shrink drastically. All of the multiplayer only VR games have followed this pattern with the exception of Pavlov and a small handful of others. But even they dont have a ton of players.

10. Snow Breed is a completely Corny name for what are basically ice zombies. Frozen Freddies would have been better.

11. No dedicated server program available for a game built mainly for multiplayer.....huge fail....Peer to peer is garbage and very unstable.....If the host leaves in the middle of a game ....guess what RIGHT BACK TO THE HUB!!!!!!



I AM MORE THAN WILLING TO CHANGE MY REVIEW TO POSITIVE IF AT LEAST SOME OF THIS IS ADDRESSED OR THE PRICE GOES DOWN A BIT.

While the story, voice actors, and environment of this game are quite good, the combat system is complete garbage. It's extremely clunky/slow, repetitive, boring, basically whatever word you can use to describe a bad combat system can be applied to this game. The combat system works well to fight off a single enemy, but when you start getting multiple enemies at once (especially enemies with mutations), the combat system just completely falls apart. It's so tedious with multiple enemies, especially when the game just eats and throws up the same enemies for the entirety of the game. Certain places where it would make sense to just skip by the enemies and not waste your time with them is impossible because the game locks the surrounding doors, forcing you to waste time fighting off enemies you really don't need to fight off.  What makes the combat system even worse is that the "manual save" function in this game doesn't actually let you save from whatever place you want, it only saves from the most recent auto save, so it's essentially useless. Not sure why you would want to go back and play any part of this horrific game ever again. The game also does a HORRIBLE job of showing you what the primary path is, and what the secondary paths are. I often times find myself back tracking halfway through one path because I realized that I'm actually on the primary path, when I want to be on a secondary path. Because of this game's very linear nature, once you progress, you can't go back very far. 

Unless you want a game with a slow story, lots of slow, repetitive combat, don't waste your time or money on this game.

review_text:
When I firsts started playing it I went "Man, this feels like playing a new Dreamcast in 2025", and it is!  But it's unfortunately for both good and bad reasons.  It has a fantastic visual style and sense of audio-visual aesthetics that makes me want to spend time in it, but totally fumbles the bag when it comes to level design and basic modern design conveniences, and will constantly get in it's own way of the fun.

The stunt and combo mechanics are fun and a meaningful improvement over it's predecessor (Jet Set Radio Future), and they make me want to just play around, but most of these future city environments feel simultaneously cavernous, empty and weirdly linear for a game about trying to combo tricks and they feel less fun to navigate.  And just when I'm getting info a flow with the game it has this bad old-school cutscene system where triggering events will yank the camera away from what you're doing just to highlight a basic level event like the cops appearing or where to go next, when they could have indicated that to me from my character's perspective like any other modern game in the last 10-15 years will do.

And then there's the janky stuff that just feels straight out of the old Jet Set Radio/Future games, like the boring police combat, bad forced camera angles during certain boss fights (big Sonic Adventure vibes here),  the awkwardly sequenced audio and the static cutscenes that don't do much to add life to the story that peaks 10 minutes in.

If you like what you see from the videos then you'll probably enjoy it and I did have fun here, I think i'm just disappointed that 22 years after Jet Set Radio Future this game doesn't feel like it makes the leap forward it should have.

review_text:
The game mechanics are pretty decent for a Left 4 Dead style VR shooter, and the optimization is pretty decent. The shooting feels nice and aiming is purposefully a little sluggish to help you stabilize shots (it's hard to explain, but it's almost like trying to aim underwater a little bit. It isn't tedious and actually helps against the jitter often seen in these VR shooters. This is a big positive). It's also one of the few games where when I throw an item, it actually goes where I intended it to go, another common issue in VR games. Returning from launch, a couple of things have changed since launch. a handful of guns were added, the grind eased up a little bit (it's still an extremely grindy and luck-dependant game, just not as much anymore), manual reloading has been improved but is still finicky and forces you to often crash your VERY expensive controllers together every so often, and horde mode was added along with one new mission and mutations to old missions that change daily.

There are still many issues, however. The AI bots are still completely worthless, won't pick up items, can't aim, and will actively protect zombies by constantly blocking your shots. Remember to mute NPC voices in your setting to protect your sanity against the AI constantly complaining their face is blocking your bullets. Because of this, you'll be subject to the games community, which is a hit or miss. There are some people who will help you along the way you'll have a great time, but most of the time people will hotmic shitty music, be on the phone, complain, pester, whine, scream, bicker, refuse to communicate, run off on their own to die, try to command your every action, and/or will not speak English. This isn't much of a fault of the game developers but god damn does it ruin the experience. Gun stats and upgrades are often extremely vague and true values hidden in patch notes, which isn't very helpful when you're trying to modify your guns to suit your needs and it's extremely frustrating when the game refuses to give you upgrades for your favorite gun, while you've managed to unlock everything for a gun you never want to use. The content in the game also gets old very quickly, and the devs seem to have a very slow pace adding new ones.

Overall, this game, even after all of the updates in the last couple of months, is STILL not even close to being worth 40 bucks. If you're someone who's fortunate enough to have 3 other friends who often play VR games and are also willing to play this game, I can see this game being an absolute blast. Unfortunately, if you're like me who's only got one friend like that, and have to choose between the horrible AI or horrible people, this game is a hard pass.

review_text:
So i feel like I'm probably a good candidate for a review as I played PSO Episodes 1+2 plus for both Xbox and GameCube, both offline and online. And I had an absolute blast playing those. I then went on to CARD and somehow even enjoyed that, followed by PSU. I've enjoyed every PSO game I've played because simply put. It's formula.  The gameplay has been historically simple and enjoyable for the most part, the elements associated with the plot and story lines have also made for pleasant and heartwarming experience. 

The reason I say this is because PSO2 and PSO2 NGS I feel are more appealing as games for previously established fans of the genre... PSO 2 took what made PSO and PSU successful and implemented those same mechanics, with an introduction of various new features.. such as a slew of more fashion oriented items, a system where you can upgrade weapons and armor and even other various features such as customizable techniques, photon arts, class leveling and more. That said, as a fan of the old stuff, these are awesome upgrades and implementations and definetely add to the richness and enjoyment level of the game and I haven't even touched upon aspects such as clans and player shops. 

NGS took what made PSO2 successful and followed that same style of formulaic upgrading, except now we got a serious graphical overhaul, an open world and a level of richness never before seen in a PSO game. In fact it's so rich that to new players it can be overwhelming! And there in lies the problem I feel new players will struggle with. 

This game seems like a game that you can just pick up and play on the surface (and it is) but there is a learning curve. In PSO2 and NGS there is more tact necessary during combat, you have to learn how things work in order to properly specialize your character, you need to learn how the armour and item systems work over time in order to properly maximize your fighting potential, as with any RPG. But once you do learn those mechanics (which can be done within 5-10 hours of gameplay easily) you really start to appreciate its charm and creativity. There's a lot of life in it, a lot of passion. You get a sense the developers really did try to make a good, enjoyable game. 

And most of all, the game is free. You can spend money on the premium set (and various other cosmetic items) and doing so really does add an even deeper level of richness into the game regarding the quality of life experience (more rewards for your time, expanded storage, access to player-based economy) but the cool thing is you can access this stuff as a free player as well in limited time usage increments, so you can get a taste for it and see if its worth it to you before electing to spend the $13 for 30 days of premium play. Often times there's also sales as well, I currently am utilizing 30 days of premium play for just $5. 

In reality, its a good game. It's free, its fun. Don't be afraid to join a clan and play the main story too. It really helps smooth things out and prep you to be at a solid level to join other players for endgame. Seasoned RPG veterans could grind through it in easily 10-15 hours. In a world where games are commonly feeling like half-finished cash grabs it does feel as if PSO has more respect for your time and wallet. And the nostalgia factor hits hard as well (in case you couldn't tell) 

All in all, I say to fans of the genre and newcomers alike. Give it a chance! It's a lot of fun!

review_text:
I am willing to change my feedback if, and will say with a big IF, Deca or whoever took ownership of this game, will change the direction of STO to what is supposed to be: a Star Trek game, with exploration, contacts, and other intriguing missions rather than a Cash Grab game.

I have 800 hours on this account, but I did play STO even before (out of Steam) when the top tier ship was the Fleet one, and I played it until the Odyssey was released for the first time as a free ship. No strange weapons combination, the meta was anti-proton damage and the ESD map was, basically, square. 

The game changed a lot during the years in what it is now considered as a cash grabbing / FOMO game. Whales are keeping the game alive without even considering they are damaging the game rather than helping it to stay alive. I understand perfectly this is the only Star Trek game worth to be considered nowadays, which other ST game allows you to create your on Character, your own Crew, and fly your own ship (from the tons you have in there) and customising the equipment? It's great in that sense, and also the graphic and visuals are outstanding.

But, similar to other games, STO is ten miles wide and one inch deep. Klingon original story campaign, as well as the Romulan and Cardassian one, have been revamped and shrunk, to align to the needs of the story of the 24xx era. Clusters have been removed and replaced with Duty Officer missions. Reputations are a tedious farm to get something small in return because, yes, the best components/weapons/ships are from the Store or from the Lockboxes, which means cash grabbing. Don't get me wrong, you can still accomplish lot's of stuff in this game without even paying a penny, but the amount of ships they are throwing at you recently on the Store, is a pathetic way to monetise. 

But funs will criticise you the moment you say something negative against this game. For them, STO is a church, something sacred that cannot be criticised. That's the current status of the game.

I love Star Trek, I used to love a lot STO and I hope it will last forever, but if things won't change, this game will be only targeted towards whales that throw money at the 100th Miranda re-skin without a second thought.

review_text:
I gotta say, I am quite enjoying this journey of going through every Yakuza game available on PC. I started off with 0, then Kiwami 1 and 2, then that *dreadful* 3, then 4 and now I am finally at this one. 

Now I gotta say from the start, unlike Yakuza 3 and 4 which took me a long, long time to actually go through them, not because they were bad, but because it was the same city over and over again. I kind of started getting a bit burnt out from Kamurocho, being the same main city in 5 other games. Not in this game however, Yakuza 5 has a fresh new concept. You get not one, not two but three new cities + kamurocho and sotenbori all in one game. While it did take me 106 hours to go through most of the content, I did enjoy the diversity and entirely new map, as well as bringing back most of the characters from Yakuza 4.

The graphics are a leap forward. This is I believe the first Yakuza that used the new engine where characters are more detailed and the environment looks better overall. I might be wrong, but I think this uses the same engine Kiwami and Yakuza 0 use. While graphics still look a bit dated, I would say it's an improvement comparing to 3 that looked like early PS3 game.

The story: The story is identical to Yakuza 4 where the entire game is split between different characters that all come up together in the end. I liked the story in Yakuza 4, and this one I felt added some more depth to it. Yeah there are still trope moments here and there, but at this point I kind of got used to it. Yakuza 0 had better story no doubt, but I would say I still enjoyed going through this story.

The gameplay: Now you have more things to do, especially how every character has a "sidestory" now. Sidestories are not to be confused with substories where it's just a side quest, sidestories are more like a special character quest where you get to experience different gameplay, for example early spoilers [spoiler] kiryu is now a taxi driver, so his sidestory involves driving a taxi car around the city [/spoiler]. This adds many hours of content, on top of new cities to explore and new things to do. Oh and no more stupid hostess club management game from Yakuza 3 and 4. Thank god, I really didn't like that game, I'd like to go back to management games from Kiwami 2 and 0. 
So on top of having ton of mini games, combat is improved. Enemy encounters are now marked with a red speech bubble, so unlike 3 and 4 where they hide in the corner and pounce on you, here you can actually recognize them from afar and avoid them if you don't want to engage in combat. However, there is still a problem where they react instantly in chasing you down, and some of them are even faster than you. Like I said in the previous games, the encounters are not a problem until the endgame where they become annoyance, and once again I can't stress how encounters are better done in 0, Kiwami and Kiwami 2. The combat itself is identical to 4, with addition to the "Climax heat" mode where characters get to do sort of a super move that does ton of damage. 
Speaking of gameplay, there is also a special character with a different gameplay. I won't spoil it, but I do have to say, I enjoyed it.

On top of all this, I am really glad how far Yakuza series have got. I really enjoyed playing this game and I only know Yakuza games get even better after this. Yakuza fans, do play this game, I really enjoyed my time with it, and I'll see you all in Ishin!

review_text:
Arrr, me hearties! Gather 'round as I spin ye a yarn about Bonelab, a game I've been itchin' to play for ages. I even went and plundered meself a VR headset just for this adventure. But alas, after sailin' the virtual seas for a mere hour, me excitement was keelhauled, and I be left feelin' more disappointed than a sailor without grog.

Let's talk about these scurvy-ridden enemies, or lack thereof. They be like the most mindless zombies ye ever did see – no different shapes, no fierce designs, just a bunch of landlubbers shufflin' towards ye. And what's worse? They can't even wield a cutlass or a pistol. Combat be as dull as a rusty cutlass in a barrel of seawater. When you spend at least half of the time wandering and thinking what to do next, its brief length makes sense - it knows when to wrap things up. Did I mention that the environments are truly alien and alienating and that the story is actually fitting that tone of overall decay.

review_text:
Valve took a simple idea — four survivors against endless hordes of zombies — and turned it into one of the most iconic co-op games ever made.

Every campaign feels like a mini action-horror movie, where teamwork is the only way to survive. The AI Director is pure genius: it changes enemy spawns, item locations, and pacing, so each run is unpredictable and intense. One moment you’re clearing a hallway together, the next you’re ambushed by a Smoker dragging your friend into the dark.

The special infected (Hunter, Boomer, Smoker, Tank, Witch) add so much personality and strategy — they’re not just enemies, they’re obstacles that force cooperation. And when the Tank theme kicks in… pure adrenaline.

Playing with friends is where the game truly shines. The panic, the laughter, the moments where someone sacrifices themselves so the team can escape — it all creates unforgettable memories. Even playing with bots, the game still has that sharp, tense atmosphere.

Pros:
✔️ Timeless co-op gameplay
✔️ AI Director keeps things fresh every time
✔️ Unique and memorable special infected
✔️ Excellent map design, feels like horror/action movies
✔️ Pure adrenaline in every campaign

Cons:
– Shorter than modern games (but endlessly replayable)
– Bots aren’t great compared to real players

Verdict:
Even after all these years, Left 4 Dead holds up as one of the best co-op shooters ever made. It’s fast, chaotic, scary, and fun in a way very few games have matched. If you love co-op, this is essential.

10/10 — still the gold standard of zombie survival.

review_text:
This is an odd one for me.
I am lucky enough to have a top-end rig, 5090 and all that, so performance-wise, I have no issues.
The game looks stunning at times, and I love its tone and look. I also find the story to be interesting. They give little bits, and I like the intrigue. The monsters are nothing extraordinary, but they do a good enough job, and I like the combination of things.
The score is excellent for this kind of game.

Now, I don't have as much time as I used to, so the games I play need to keep me entertained and interested, with some progress. If II don't, I move on. The game isn't what I'd call hard, in terms of the enemies you fight, but it's the game design itself that gets you killed.

There are too many narrow corridors where, when you turn, you cannot see anything.
A flashlight that, at times, is a joke.
Rooms with rare items to sell, but they put so many enemies in the room that by the time you kill them, it was pointless going in for the item. Yes, there are some rooms where you can do the smash and grab, but some rooms get sealed.
Mobs do not drop enough ammo. It doesn't need to be much more, but I got tired of basically running out of ammo. In some games like this with the low ammo count, as long as you pulled off head shots, you could scrape by. Some games even had a simple gun that either needed to cool down/recharge, but at least you had something, even if it was a weak gun. I died a few times. I basically had to Rocky a mob.
Aiming is a pain. To save shots, you try and hit the sweet spots but a few of them really dont like to stay still long, This is so frustrating due to the bad FOV being too-far-left, and your gun sways wildly. I thought I had aim assist on, maybe fighting it, and is why my shots were off, however, when I checked, it was actually off.

I would say its a good game, if you can deal with some bad camera angles and having to micro manage ammo. You will find that 50% of your deaths are due to game mechanics rather than your skill. However, if you have to pick and choose your games more, due to free time, the running around trying to scrap ammo together might drag and turn what stated off as good, into a chore of a game.

I would say its a buy, if its on sale, but right now its a 6/10, but with a few tweaks (dont think it will happen) this could be a 8/10.

Short, but I really liked what I got.
I'm one of those people that got this game knowing that this isn't a survival horror, but instead being more of a puzzle game. And I definitely wasn't disappointed with it.
The art style of this game was GORGEOUS! There's obviously a ton of inspiration from H.R. Giger here, but the design team nailed it here.
The puzzles themselves were pretty decent. Half of them were just "Move this thing over here", but the rest were actually challenging, but not to the point where I had to look up a guide.
The combat... It's a mixed bag for me. The weapons are serviceable at best, but switching them and reloading is *painfully* slow. There isn't a lot of enemy variety... They're mostly just grubs that hang around the environment. And you can literally hang back and wait for them to leave the area most of the time. Actually fighting these creatures isn't too bad though. And they're fairly easy to tangle with, even with just the melee weapon you get fairly early on. The combat overall is definitely at its worst near the end though, during the games one and only boss fight, which I'd best describe as a clunky mess.

Overall though, I definitely got my bang for my buck with this one. It's just a crying shame that it turned out to be so short.

review_text:
Meh... this game tries so hard to be Dead Space, it's actually pathetic... and yeah I'm aware the guy who made Dead Space made this game. EA basically stole his brain child and legal stuff happened and he lost the rights to it... yadda yadda... this is why you hire lawyers before dealing with greedy ass corporations.

All that drama and information aside... this game is just crap. It's like Dead Space except the focus is way more on melee weapons and timing attacks than it is about dismemberment and fun. The combat is also very low brow and juvenile, prison style combat where you're beating a monster to death like he was a human inmate in a prison... I mean that's the theme but honestly... they're monsters we're dealing with here... give me a break.

In Dead Space, there were a variety of weapons, if you were bored of one style, there were like 9 other weapons to choose from. Save points were in abundance and spaced out properly as well as shops / upgrade stations. This game? Absolutely ridiculous... 

You can save where ever you want to but the game forces check points upon you. You could go around collecting stuff, save your game, close it down, restart it 3 days later and be completely lost when you return. So even if you manually save (which I recommend doing) it needs to be near an auto save spot, otherwise you just lose progress and have to get your bearings again upon reload.

It's insanely linear and there are SO many points of no return it's insane. Most areas are a 50/50 path branch and if you take the wrong one (a.k.a. the right one) then you just missed out on something, so reload one of your 9 auto saves and re-do all the stuff you just did... it's a joke and takes you out of the immersion every chance it can... I hate games with missible nonsense... it's so 2007... like get over this crap already and just make a good game...

There's a ton of useless data log's to collect and yes, you can miss all of them. If you do happen to miss something (and you will without a walk through, trust me), you have to start the entire run over again if you've saved past a point of no return.

For some odd reason the developers decided to patch the game and moved around most of these data logs as well... So unless you have an up to date guide, you'll literally be scratching your head as to why the log isn't where the guide says it is. This actually happened to me and prompted me to want to make a negative review right there on the spot. I had to start the entire game over from Chapter 1 and I was in Chapter 3. 

I decided to not be so harsh and played for a few hours longer and then it really hit me how bad this game is. I was finding all kinds of loot and there were no shops a.k.a. "print stations" to locate and sell all of this junk to. You're forced to leave valuable stuff behind in favor of health items and resources like ammo, which means forget ever getting stronger unless you're half dead and used all your health items... it's piss poor design and just way too extreme.

I found 7 or 8 of these energy converter items to sell and there were ZERO shops to sell them to for days. The pacing is absolute garbage and your inventory for resource items is limited to 6 slots for half the game but there are like 9 giant slots for giant weapons, go figure. 

This game is literal hot garbage and these developers are incompetent. I heard bad things about this game's performance when it released so I didn't bother with it, my 5090 Astral OC brute forces this trash, everything maxed out at 185 FPS... so whatever... this game's not even worth a toss, it's so poorly optimized, there's no reason you should need a $4000 video card to run this trash on max settings in 4K... it's inexcusable.

The biggest offense this game committed was right when I bought it. I was missing two of the skins from the deluxe package and I had to MANUALLY create a KRAFTON (wtf even is this company?) account and link my Steam to it... so yeah great start. More security breech points to my Steam account and corporate data acquisitions, so they can steal my information and sell it... lovely... I digress. I had to make this account, link it to my Steam profile and then contact their customer support to unlock these skins that I had paid for...

This was already a red flag but I paid $15 CAD for this p.o.s. so I figured, whatever... it's $15... I mean, a fast food combo costs as much nowadays so I figured I may as well give this a go... yeah, it's awful...  should have just bought a Big Mac and ignored this garbage. 

The game play is bad, the direction is bad, the performance is probably bad as well but I'm rocking the best video card in the world on this thing so I can't exactly gauge this aspect much... either way, total dog sh|t... I'll play it through to the end to see the cliche plot unfold or whatever but my God... this is bad.

I also researched unlockable content and there isn't anything. There are no secret weapons or skins tied to finishing the game on the hardest settings... only achievements... so yeah, this game is a one and done for me... especially considering how linear and boring it is.

The true ending is locked behind the DLC as well, which is just laughable. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME FOR FULL PRICE. Wait for a sale and grab the Deluxe package for the cheapest price possible because man, this game is BAAAAD.

Also, there are cut scenes you can't skip, long winded vent crawling sections, tight narrow walls you have to wedge yourself through and door opening animations that rival the original Resident Evil for loading screen time sinks... you'll be dealing with this crap on EVERY play through... what a waste of life.

They also expect you to beat this game multiple times (just like Dead Space) and they even have a mode, just like Dead Space's Impossible mode, called Contagion mode. If you die on this mode, you have to start the entire chapter over again... which, okay, fair... it's better than the entire game (Dead Space's Impossible mode) but still, it's ridiculous. There are a lot of one shot death areas at the end of most of the chapters as well as bosses that just 1 shot murk you.

I also hate the combat, it's not smooth like it is in Dead Space, it's insanely scripted like one of those Batman Arkham games; except there are no button prompts on screen to take you out of the immersion... but also, it's insanely obvious because of the pauses between attacks. You can't just 5 hit combo an enemy, it's 3 hits, then you have to dodge or block and repeat... it's nauseating how lame this game is.

Your gravity bracer (because yes, they had to copy this from Dead Space as well), that allows you to throw enemies around and grab item boxes, is also terrible in this game. This thing runs out of juice so fast you literally have to make snap decisions and pre-plan where you're tossing these bags of meat... it's almost not even worth doing. Rather than the energy being expended per use, it's literally based on time while in use... so the bar runs out while you're holding enemies... what a garbage design.

Your gun is OP as hell once it's fully upgraded but good luck finding bullets or credits to upgrade this thing. This game is literally 80% melee and 20% ranged shooting. When you reach the final boss, your melee attacks can't damage him and you have to rely on a gun... so you can literally brick your save file if you spent too much on the baton... which you use for 80% of the game... LOLOL... this game is TRASH.

Also, the whole 3D-printing weapons and upgrades is such a 2020 phase, it really dates this game. I remember when everyone and their grandmother were 3D printing crap during covid.

Meh... 5/10 at best... combat sucks, game play sucks, design sucks, pacing sucks, balance sucks. It's not as good as Dead Space. Just go buy the remake of that, you'll have a much better time. If you must play this trash, $15 tops for all the content, other wise you got ripped off.

review_text: Hoo boy, this was definitely worth the wait. Let's just say that you will be spending a lot of time with some new characters (you might already be familiar with them if you played the friendsims). It was a good mix of fun/happy moments and scary/gut wrenching moments. I found myself shuddering whenever the underlying issues of the troll caste society strongly reflected the current and real-world political atmosphere. This game has a lot of neat life messages. For example, what a healthy relationship should and should not be. It touches on what justice may mean (is it achieving balance, revenge, or truth?). Some messages are apparent when Xefros is voicing his thoughts and Joey expresses her concern. There's some real character growth, that's for sure! I'll be waiting for Act 3 ("Hauntswitch??") when it comes out (which I suspect might be in a couple of years). The art is beautiful and charming just like in act 1. I can't get over how cute the animation reactions of the characters are. The bee mini game is so much fun and I was cackling at the blatant phoenix wright reference. Of course, the music is fantastic since it's Toby and James. 10/10 for me!!

review_text:
This was a good game, now I'm not so sure. 

Pros:
Good story with appearances from the show cast.

lots of space barbie (serious, the options to customize your capt, bridge officers, and ship is paralyzingly deep).

Many options for combat (space and ground, with many viable builds for each).

You aren't forced to a higher difficulty.

If you aren't willing to pay you can grind out even premium content, the grind is insane but can be done (at least in theory).

Good PVE.

TRIBBLES! tribbles everywhere, and you will need to do pest control of your inventory and banks slots. It's a feature.

Cons:
38+ different currencies not counting craft resources (and better believe you will need know them all).

The grind is real, all those currencies have different task needed to obtain them from the mundane and easy to those you need a guide just to learn even what it's used for, let alone how to get it.

PVP is so unbalanced it's easy to forget that it is even there.

Micro-transactions and lootboxes - lots of them, most of the good things in the game (powerful ship, nice looking outfit, etc.) someone had to buy and is reselling on the in-game market if you didn't buy it with cash (some of the ships go for equivalent of 200 usd).


Lastly, I will admit this is more a personal issue and spite on my part being the main reason I am steering people away. Guilds can be and are hijacked and support will not get involved even when the only reason you can't handle it yourself is because of the system they put in. Beware if you or your friend leave the game for a while, you may return to find some lowlife has gotten top rank and declared themselves ruler of your guild. All they have to do to make it so you can't get rid of them is have 2 or more characters (note: character not accounts they can be on the same account) at max rank, and when you try to force them out they just sign in on the other character and cancel it within 2 weeks. Your only hope of getting your guild back is hope they stop playing, you will need 2 weeks per character at max rank (for example if the have 7 at max rank that's 14 weeks uninterrupted to get your guild back). This has happened to a friend of mine, who lost countless hours in guild resources because he decided to take a break for a few months. 

With how long I've spend playing and fiscally supporting this game I want to give this game a positive review but I can't. Now my wallet is shut and I recommend you think long and hard before investing in this title.

If you choose to proceed: remember check for tribbles before and after any gathering/loot pickup operations, because unaccompanied tribbles are an environmental hazard.

review_text:
This game is the most overrated FPS in the past decade.

Every objective in this game is a fetch quest. "Gather these items," Bioshock says, "and I will give you a small snippet of plot in return." Screw you, Bioshock, integrate the plot into the gameplay! Don't make me go backtrack twenty times to explore your set piece, MAKE MORE SET PIECES.

Here is why Bioshock sucks: after 6 fetch quests in a row, with INCREDIBLY mediocre boss fights interspersed (i.e. standard enemy bigger health bar), they show you a super cool narrative twist. And you're like "Oh! Nice! Finally, this game is going to go somewhere!"

review_text:
Steam's rating system is busted and I'm a fan of this series, but I still can't recommend this behemoth of a game, that is the literal definition of quantity over quality. Obviously if you're playing through these titles in order you may still wish to subject yourself to this fifth entry. If you are a completionist, then I pray Kami-sama have mercy on your soul.
Yakuza5 has, by far, the worst story among all the entries I've played so far, which includes all of them, and this means that I have a fairly high tolerance for the shenanigans Yakuza usually pulls and I'm ready to suspend by disbelief. I know that ultimately it's about naked guys smashing each other's faces in on a rooftop. But still somehow the other entries managed a far better way to tell their contrived plotlines (I don't include Zero here, which is the only one that is truly amazing). At one point the characters literally state out loud: 'let's fight until something happens' They fight. Then something happens which is not satisfying at all. Plot 'twist' after twist follows around, with everyone betraying everyone, but nobody actually having any sort of damn plan. Fights happen and that's mostly it.
Gameplay-wise I have to say that, yes, it's better than 4 and the combat is mostly enjoyable. If you don't count the many street thugs that force you into inescapable fights when you're just trying to get someplace. Each character has their own sidestories which range from fairly enjoyable to tedious. I appreciated some of them, including the taxi missions and even Saejima's hunting. Haruka's singing was... there, I guess. I didn't hate it but it went on for too long. Same with Shinada's story. He's not unlikable but his presence doesn't justify the hours it takes to get through his story.
Aside from all this mess there is your standard Yakuza stuff, with endlessly impossible minigames, training masters and lots of other activities you'll be too burned out to engage with.
Now all of this would be forgivable if it actually mattered. Unfortunately these last 3 entries (3,4,5) feel mostly like spin-offs, because they waste so much time in superflous dialogue and fail to make the connections that matter, focusing instead on characters that simply don't matter. For example, Haruka and Akyiama know each other here, despite me remembering too well that they never met in the previous game. Instead of wasting my time with useless thug banter or dine-and-dash substories, you could've spent some time establishing their relationship.
I'm complaining about this because these characters obviously have lots of potential and you get to spend A LOT of time with them, so you kinda just want more than this nonsense.
Still, I'm happy I got through all of these entries in my long journey across the Yakuza series. But Steam is asking me to recommend it and I just can't. But make your own decision. In the grand scheme of things, looking back on my entire journey with Yakuza, I'm happy I played them all, the worst and the best. But whether that is your goal or you have the patience for that, only you know.

Loved almost everything about this game. The dialogues were fantastic and made me feel like I was reading Homestuck again. The art is really cute and I love all the unique little animations that the characters have, even all the background characters.

I don't share the complaints others have about the trial, it was a great way to show tons of different character interactions at once. I thought that and the other puzzles were easy enough without even using the hints, and the one hint I did use (during the final puzzle) was completely straightforward. If it's true that some hints were useless though then that sucks, hopefully online walkthroughs will start cropping up soon.

I didn't personally experience any bugs while playing. However it is problematic that there's no way to read the narration/dialog history, especially since this act had many more long sequences of text than the last. Sometimes you inevitably click too fast and miss something. Usually it's inconsequential and/or you can easily guess what they said from context, but I'd recommend saving often in case you accidentally miss something you think was important.

Overall this was a fantastic game, well worth the money personally. It was totally worth the wait too. (Hahaha just kidding, that wait was ridiculous.) Looking forward to Act 3 if I live long enough to see it!

As game developers, they have failed to see the core issue—they only notice Killers targeting specific Survivors without understanding why. If chasing other Survivors offered a better payoff than focusing on one, who would persistently tunnel a single player and relentlessly limit their game experience? Survivors want to win, but don't Killer players want to win too? Step by step, the game space for Killer players is being constrained. I can only say that the future of this game looks bleak. If Dead by Daylight continues to refuse to face reality, indulging in the idea that profiting from four players is better than profiting from one, thereby sacrificing the Killer player experience, this game will soon fade into obscurity, drowned in players' disappointment.

review_text:
Lost ruin is an interesting one for me. I went from liking it to hating it to liking it again. First of all I will touch on individual aspects of the game. 

COMBAT:

This game is definitely one of the more unique metroidvanias that I have played. The combat is best described as slow and methodical. The movement of your character is rather slow as well as the attacks she performs. You basically have to learn an memorise the move and attack patterns of not just bosses but every enemy in the game as well as the distance of your weapons attack to position yourself properly. Also when attacking you are locked in the attack animation, and you can move again after the attack is executed or something interrupts your attack.

The HP you have is extremely low and most enemy attacks do 1/3 or 1/2 of your hp. Combine that with a plethora of damage over time effects that those attacks inflict and you will legit die to 1 hit + the damage over time it comes with it. Hitting enemies with your attacks is also iffy as some do get staggered from getting hit and others do not, so you have to play a guessing game with each new enemy you encounter as to how you have to approach fighting it.

MAP & ART DESIGN:

The map is pretty well designed in my opinion. It is quite interconnected and you have options based on which path you want to take when going forward. Since the game does not have any new abilities the only progression barriers are keys that are scattered around the map and a few boss fights. The map is also full of environmental traps, which would not be that big of an issue, but every one of them inflicts one of those before mentioned damage over time blights which just make them a pain. Also this damage over time thing stacks, lets say you fall into spikes and now you are bleeding for 10s and right after you are hit by an enemy that also causes bleed with their attacks, yo now have a 20s bleed timer under your health bar. 

As far as the art style goes I think it i beautiful. Art is obviously subjective, but if you like pixel art you will definitely like this game. The environments feel real and are full of detail in both foreground and background segments. There are also a few clever cases of environmental story telling, but those cases are rather in-fequent.

STORY (Slight spoilers):

I was personally not that big of a fan of the story of this game. The story is just your generic Isekai plot where a what appears to be a high school girl gets thrown into a new, magical, dungeon like world. Also your character does not even have a name, nor can you name her and her personality is as complex as as a shape puzzle for toddlers. Heck she does not even have a name (nor can you name her), because amnesia. 

You are then tasked by the sorceress Beatrice to defeat the followers of the "Dark Lady" and you proceed to do just that. You meet a few non-boss npcs along the game, but each one just gives you a random quest and a bit of lore about the world. 

BUGS AND FRUSTRATING GAME DESIGN:
While playing I encountered two different bugs. One was that when you rode an elevator upwards if you jumped your character would sometimes clip trough that elevator and fall down to the bottom. A similar thing also happens when you ride an elevator and get hit by an attack. Even if you all on the elevator platform you will fall trough it to the bottom. This is nothing game breaking, but it is kinda annoying.

The second bug I encountered was that your attacks did not hit. Sometimes when your weapon clearly overlapped with the enemy they took no damage, knock back and there was just no indication that an attack landed even though it clearly did visually. On bosses that might have been just the case of them having temporary invincibility and I did not know about it but it also happened with regular enemies, bats in particular.

And now for one of the most frustrating things about this game. Your character can get knock back locked and you have no invincibility frames after you get hit. You know how in some games bosses like to hurl a barrage of attack at you and you have to dodge them, but it is kinda tricky so you will most likely get hit by at least 1 projectile. Well if that happens to you in this game the one projectile that will hit you will knock you into another projectile and that other one will hit you in another one and suddenly you are insta dead, since, like I mentioned before this game has no invincibility frames after getting hit. So if you get hit for example by  This is incredibly frustrating, especially since your only movement option in the game (besides walking) is a dodge roll, which is rather slow, you can not control the distance of how far you roll.

Overall the game is fun and rewarding. You will have to put some more effort into learning and adapting to its mechanics, and learning to deal with the frustrating bits but once you get a hang of it it can be a pretty fun and rewarding experience.

review_text:
I have been playing STO for several years now.  For a number of months I was slowly grinding my way up the power tree with my first character, banging my head against some of the campaign challenges and just not making much headway.  Fortunately I was friended by a nice fellow in Germany.  (There is a notable German playerbase.)  He helped me defeat a particularly annoying enemy and got me a fleet invitation.  From there I asked a steady stream of questions and got very useful advice on in-game economy, earning upgrade kits, and similar topics.  
My advice to new players is to ask many questions and not be afraid to ask for help.  There are a number of details that are not even mentioned in the tutorials, but despite the never-ending stream of political bad takes in the big chat hubs there are even more decent folk who will take advise a newcomer.

The real goal of STO is, of course, "Space Barbie."  Dressing your crew toons in stylish uniforms or casual wear is amusing, but the bigger draw is the starship selection.  The game IS free-to-play, and the normal level grind will give you several opportunities to earn your choice of basic ships appropriate to the Federation, Romulan, or Klingon career paths.  Additionally, there are summer and winter events in which one can earn a free ship as well as useful personal gear.
Unfortunately for people without trust funds, the most coveted ships and gear are not free.  The in-game store has a decent sale from time to time but it is clear that your money is supposed to be theirs.  I kept to the ftp ethos for years but finally decided that a purchase now and then was not fatal.  To be clear, it is a luxury, not a necessity.  If something I really wanted came along, I would buy it only if I could do without a corresponding purchase elsewhere.  Most often that meant not buying beer for a little while, so we're not talking really large sums.  

Sadly, I can no longer make purchases because Arc decided I have to go through them.  I hope they enjoy not having that little bit of revenue stream any longer.

review_text:
I was caught off guard by how many playable characters there are and how much variety each one brings. The game takes you through multiple cities, and it feels so refreshing compared to most games that stick to one location. Every area has its own charm, side stories, and life.

Now, the mini-games man, I’m a big fan of those. This game is absolutely packed with them. Each character has their own set of activities:

Kiryu gets the Taxi Missions and Taxi Races, which were my favorite. Oddly satisfying and relaxing, and when you’re racing, you can unlock soundtracks even a track from Daytona USA! Total classic Sega vibes.

Saejima has Snowball Fights, which are surprisingly fun and chaotic.

Haruka has her own rhythm and performance mini-games that feel like DDR, and they fit perfectly with her idol storyline.

Shinada has the Batting Cages, and they actually tie into his story really well.

Akiyama gets Business Missions and hostess interactions that play to his smooth, confident style.

All these mini-games make the world feel alive, and honestly, the amount of content here is insane.

The story itself, though, was a bit confusing and didn’t hit as hard emotionally for me. I still think Yakuza 0 and 3 had stronger, more memorable narratives. But the scale of Yakuza 5 is impressive, and it’s perfect for fans who love getting lost in Kamurocho and beyond.

Overall, it’s a huge, ambitious entry that delivers on gameplay and heart even if the plot stumbles a bit. And seriously… we NEED an Akiyama game already.

This is not a minor inconvenience - this is a core gameplay-breaking issue that is driving players away. Either fix the server routing properly or stop pretending the problem has been resolved.

review_text:
I have been playing this game fairly consistently for the past 8 or so years. I also lead an in-game Fleet (Guild) that has had a constant player base that has grown and shrunk over time with sometimes hundreds of people. In other words, I truly love this game and almost always have enjoyed playing it.

Which makes what I'm about to say very hard.

Over these years the game has steadily become one of the most greediest, dirtiest cash grabs in the current Free-to-Play MMO market. It takes literal months to grind (and I mean GRIND) for a free, premium ship. Even other free ships, like the summer/winter event ones, still require weeks of grinding - and it NEVER changes. They don't change these events, so every year it's the same activities. which becomes extremely dull extremely fast. 

Not to mention EVERYTHING else in the game requires a purchase. Uniforms, lockbox keys, bridge officers, playable factions, inventory slots, bank slots, ship slots, duty officers, shuttles, equipment upgrades, etc. While some fans may attack me and say that not ALL of these items are only attainable through real money purchases, it is MUCH easier to buy them than to grind for them.

Another in-game currency, Dilithium, has had a very small cap that has never changed for countless years. This currency allows you to upgrade your gear, support your Fleet, buy special equipment you unlock through Reputations (which, of course, require a little bit of grinding, but not nearly as bad as the previously mentioned gripes) and other useful items. The cap is insultingly low, and once again, some fans may say "well, you can refine a little extra from your Fleet mine!" or "If you're a lifetime member, you can refine an extra 1,000 every few days". Of course, lifetime subscriptions cost $200-$300, assuming they're on sale. Obviously a small price to pay for a little extra dilithium that can only be initiated through a certain mission on a certain planet.

This is only scratching the surface of this game's issues. A lot of the older missions have loads of bugs and are simply outdated (think Nimbus), some of the newer ones have some too, the engine has been out of date for years and they show no sign of upgrading it, and there's just so many bugs sometimes. I can recall when expansions would drop and certain missions or activities would literally cause your game to crash. I understand some of these times bugs will happen, but Cryptic never seems to truly test their new content. 

I am truly saddened and sickened by how awful the monetisation methods have become in this game. Like I said, I still do love this game, but I don't recommend new players to try it right now. I PRAY that they will eventually realize the insanity behind their practices and actually put some love and effort into this game, but until they do, you're better off playing older Star Trek games like Armada.

And now for a quick history lesson on this game: Its original American release date was in late 2002. Its first expansion pack (note that I didn't say DLC, because it had a physical release), Wacky Worlds, was released in 2003. Later that year, its second expansion pack, Time Twister, came out. Both add new scenarios, scenery with various themes, and reskins of rides that were already in the base game.

Around the same time that Time Twister released, the Combo Park Pack (as it's known in America, which is where I life), a compilation of the base RCT2 game and Wacky Worlds, came out. The following year, the Triple Thrill Pack, a compilation of the base RCT2 game and both of its expansion packs, released. This Steam release is a digital version of the Triple Thrill Pack.

Anyway, onto my pros and cons list!

PROS:
Messing with your customers, such as by raising the price of umbrellas when it starts raining or selling free (salty) French fries and overpriced drinks next door, is a lot of fun
Killing your guests on purpose is a lot of fun, though even one death at your park causes its rating to plummet (and if that death was from a ride crashing, guests will avoid it for months even if no one dies)
Playing the game how you're supposed to can also be fun

CONS:
Many of your guests are cowards
(I'd have other complaints, but that'd just be me being spoiled by what OpenRCT2 adds to the game that neither RCT2 nor RCT1 have officially, like fast forwarding, winning the scenario early if you reach the goal long before the deadline, auto-saving, online multiplayer, and more)

Overall, it's up to you if you want to get this game, though I'd recommend you pick up and play OpenRCT2 if you choose to buy this.

review_text:
I had high hopes for this game, since I really enjoyed SGW 3, despite its quirks. But I was let down oh so hard.

The mechanics feel rough like they weren't properly tested at all, the AI is not good, either they are completely unaware of you, or you get detected and literally everyone on the map knows where you are, up to your precise location. Once detected, everyone will start shooting at you with deadly accuracy, and the alarm keeps blaring in the background, also you will stay detected indefinitely, even if you hide. 

The weapons are fine, but none really stand out apart from the 50.cal that can dismember enemies. The maps feel like they weren't thought over twice since some passages are unusable and the terrain is incredibly rough. I got stuck on the dumbest things including but not limited to twigs, little rocks, bumps on the ground, etc. 

One moment I was having great fun and the other I was frustrated out of my mind, because of ALL the bugs. The autosave feature is clever but poorly executed, as it saves very infrequently, to the point where you have to play entire sections again, just because it didn't save.

If this game is going to be playable, it's going to need a HUGE overhaul, every feature needs to be re-evaluated to work more smoothly. Also, the animations are super laggy, even on a reasonable pc. So I hope they fix their game, but in the meantime, only get this dirt cheap, because it simply isn't worth the money in its current state.

review_text:
Alright, so I wanted to wait a bit before I made this review because while I was going through my first run of the game I was checking the reviews and I wanted to see if I would have a different opinion after beating the game or going through another run. I'll say that even after beating the game for the second time and now currently on witch mode, I still believe this game is just as great as during my first run. To preface this, I played the game on veteran difficulty for my first run and the second run I played was boss rush mode.

I'm going to touch on the art style just a bit, as I think it's already been said enough but it's really good and fits the whole anime style they were going for. So there's not to much to say on the end of art for the game but I will give praise for the sprites and how you're able to get a good feel for the characters. 

Now let's move onto the gameplay, which has had very polarizing out look on it. I gotta say, I haven't had as much fun with a lot of games I've been recently playing in comparison to this game which I've been having a blast on. As I mentioned earlier, I played this game on veteran mode, so it was especially challenging and it caused me to die quite a lot. Though it was really only at the beginning where I felt like some of the deaths was the games part. In the beginning of the game there are a few enemies that have attacks you just can't punish without taking damage if you didn't get the right equipment but it's pretty easy to avoid those enemies. It won't be long until you are able to come back and kill them anyway because those enemies become quite easy to beat once you get either the spells, weapons, and/or artifact to deal with them. That's where the fun comes in, I was able to play the game how I wanted. There are a bunch of kits in the game where you can cheese out the enemies but there's a lot of customization you can go through to fit your playstyle. When I came back to face those difficult enemies, I wasn't trapped using a certain kit because I had other options. Not every customization is going to be good for an area but you will never be limited to just one kit. This is reinforced with the spells in the game around the mid game you're able to get artifacts and a weapon that grants you mana, so you won't have to use mp potions as often. This means you can just go wild with certain spells and have a blast using them. You feel like one of bosses made the game into a bullet hell just use a spell and don't have to worry about the projectiles anymore or maybe you feel like the enemies ranged attacks are going to fast there's a spell for that too.  The only real issue I had with the gameplay and this is more of a personal one is the hitbox for specific weapons like the hatchet and the Cursed Scythe feel very small and inconsistent at times. This was really annoying to deal with as I would lose all my stacks and begin to take bleeding damage when I thought they were in the hitbox for the Cursed Scythe. 

The combat in the game is the reason why I wanted to make this review in the first place. It was really fun doing what I wanted to do, even if it wasn't the most optimal I could still mess around with it. Late game I had a blast using invis with full stacks on cursed scythe and just one shot most enemies. This ties in with what I believe with games like this, if I can do what I want to do and still feel pleasure in doing so then it's a great game. I recommend this game 100% and if I had to give a rating for this game I would definitely give it 4.99/5 stars.

review_text:
A fairly short, mildly challenging action-platformer, with a more tactical focus than running straight into every enemy mindlessly. 

You will be punished if you try to do this. 

I was lead to believe that this game was going to be unforgiving. My experience, even on the "Recommended" Difficulty was hardly that. I died, sure, but never enough times to want to pull my hair out or quit playing altogether. 

That said, I didn't find it as challenging or as difficult as some reviews led me to believe, but the game is not an easy one either. They warn you outright upon starting a new game that this is not meant to be a quick "run and gun" experience. 

The Heroine, swings melee weapons slowly. Timing is important. Traps are appropriately dangerous, but relatively rare. Figuring out when to dodge is likewise, very important. Nothing particularly new here. 

I found a wide variety of weapons available, mostly swords, axes, daggers, and hammers. I never encountered any spears, as far as I am aware of. 

Ranged options are mostly down to various throwing weapons (both traditional and, uniquely, some throwing bottles), a few bows, and casting spells. It took me some time to encounter a bow, so if that's your preferred playstyle, be wary of that. You may not acquire one till an hour or more in. 

I like the interactions between various mechanics. Casting a Lightning spell while soaking wet is, obviously, a bad idea, and a quick way to kill yourself. Finding means to solve these moment to moment problems is definitely a treat. 

However, I want to preface that previous statement with confirmation that you will be doing quite a bit of inventory management. If you're suffering bleed stacks, you can die quickly. So you will find yourself going into the inventory very often to resolve various issues. Casting a fire spell, while covered in Oil is likewise, a bad idea. 

Also, if you do find yourself changing your routine to fight against a boss. The Green "Angel" Checkpoints will only store whatever version of your equipment you had as you passed them. So you will have to reset your equipment should you be stuck at a boss. 

I didn't find it annoying as other people did, but I can see why it would get frustrating. So I will also mention that here. 

All in all, I found it a fun, and occationally challenging experience that lasted a handful of hours.

As a player coming from The Isle, I'm used to.... sketchy and shoddy. However, with 2 years of development, this game is neither of those things. It's worse. I played for all of 20 minutes to give it a full chance, and I just couldn't stand the gameplay. 

I started as a croc. There are no controls listed for crocs in the games control scheme, so it took me 5 minutes to figure out that after I rebound my keys to have left control on something different, that it was overriding the "submerge" keybind. Reset my keys again, and I immediately went back to choose a different animal after watching the movement of a croc. It's horrific.

Next, I tried out the Hornbill, a carno bird. This thing flies like a helicopter. I'm not even kidding. A damn helicopter. I let go of my W key, expecting to just glide, but somehow this bird starts to hover in midair in a stationary position. Glorious. Decided to figure out what would happen if I just pressed space while flying, and this damn bird lost all forward momentum and fell like a rock out of the air, but guess what? Press space again and you'll hover in mid air.

1/10 for vision.
0/10 for execution.

review_text:
TL;DR: Nothing about this game engaged me in any way. I'd sooner do my taxes than play this game, because at least then I'd be doing something productive.

It's like they got to the end of the game and realized:
"OH CRAPCRAPCRAPCRAP WE FORGOT TO PUT IN GUNS- Uh ok, ok, don't panic....ok I guess let's just throw em in there!"
"But boss how are we goin-"
"JUST DO IT!"

I'm honestly surprised this game did as well as it did. The story was honestly silly, the plot was thinly laid at best and any kind of surprise you ran across in the game wasn't built up, it was completely out of left field. They tell you details, but then tell you not to think about those details, THEN they tell you "oh but you have to FIND the pieces to the story, like a scavenger hunt!". That's not clever, it actively counteracts the story buildup because you then expect the game to give you the real buildup, only to find that it doesn't exist. THEN if you miss story pieces - well. Then you are robbed of the story, which, why would a game do that ever? It's almost comical how backwards this storytelling plan was.

Also, as soon as you pick up the grenade launcher the game difficulty immediately plummets to a level where it feels like you're playing a different game because you're so godlike powerful. And as soon as you put it down, you're back to level 2 in any MMO. Again, gun play was a complete and total afterthought in this game.

I don't even want to get started on the upgrade system, this'll be longer than A Tale of Two Cities.

I understand this is a classic to many, but I doubt I could have been more disappointed by it. Don't buy it, borrow it from a friend.

[h1] Witchfire is AWESOME!!! [/h1]

[h3] Just finished 100% achievements (Currently 30/30, Velmorne update, 59 hours total). [/h3]

Started with the Penitent class, only had a single revolver to shoot, no more than that.
The experience was difficult, specially if you don't know that the mirror quest from the begining was a MUST DO THING to obtain new weapons and upgrades.
Was about my 10th hour on the game, that i found the last mirror shard, to rebuild it.
So yeah, was on the second map already, just with a single weapon, ascended level 20+ or so.

[h2] AND THEN, the difficult spike REALLY got up... [/h2]

The monsters are much more aggressive, the new enemies just insta-killed me a hundred times..

[h2] UNTIL, something changed after dying like... 100 times or so... [/h2]

I learned to play the game the way it mean to be played.
Learned that i needed to cover, stop, breath, reload, double check my map, then rush to kill a enemy.
Learned to conserve ammo, to swap weapons on right time, engage on long and close range...

[h2] Then, after some time, it was just a breeze leveling up there. [/h2]

Got my ascended level to like 40~50.
Time to go on Velmorne..

The same loop repeated. 
Specially on the "dead" part.
Omg... It repeated a lot on this map.
SO many times i died to the elements present there that... Wow...

After that, the difficulty, in my opinion, was fine.
The Castle gates was OK. To be honest, for me, wayyy easier than Velmorne.

The Witch Mountain was a total blast when i reached there.
It was a complete different mechanic, remembering a lot of Destiny 1~2 path to incursions, with a TOP TIER fight at the end.

[h2] Really loved it!!! [/h2] 

The optional content (Wailing Tower) was brilliant.
It's awesome the way it is, hope its expanded in the future.
REALLY hard. Was about ascension level 85 my first victory there. 

[h2] Finally, Witchfire is, with no doubt, on my favorite list. [/h2] 

Hope to come back soon!

review_text:
[h1] Interesting Puzzle Game in Desperate Need of a UX Designer [/h1]

I [i] really [/i] tried to enjoy this game, and I'll keep trying, but this game is perhaps the best example of why "User Experience" designers are important. 

This game has a very barebones aesthetic in terms of UI and Storytelling, and at first it seems to work really well. There's basically no formal narrative, the story/lore is very subtle and plays out through the environment and puzzles, and no tutorial. That's not a problem, however, because piecing together what the game expects you to do is intuitive... in the first 30 minutes. 

When you first encounter an interactable object, a circle with a dash through it appears and you get an "error" SFX when you try to interact with it. Then when you encounter an item you [i]can[/i] interact with, the circle appears "filled" and has no line. The game teaches you that when you see these circles, you know whether or not you can interact. Then, when you finally solve your first major puzzle room, there's this sense of accomplishment that you were able to figure it out without any help. It's great! Then you move on to the next major puzzle room...

WELL LO AND BEHOLD, the game breaks its own rules on the second puzzle. Both circles appear on the same interactable object at varying times, but neither of them work and there's no "error" SFX when you do try to interact when you can't. So within 1 hour the user interface just starts lying to you. Then, when you finally do solve the puzzle, it opens a door that leads to...

A dead end. With nothing there. Nothing to interact with. Nowhere to progress. You're stuck in a room with nothing to do.

I'll keep playing, but something so egregiously dumb as switching what your UI means within the first hour of the game (without telling the player and leading them to think the game is broken) coupled with a cutscene of a door opening that leads nowhere is pants-on-head dumb design. 

Note for the devs: For your next game, hire someone that knows what a good user experience looks like.

review_text:
This games somehow has worse stealth mechanics than Splinter Cell: Blacklist and MGSV. How, I have no idea, but even for $5 this game isnt worth it.

-First and foremost, no manual save system is absolutely crazy for a game released in 2019.

-Poor PC optimization. Just standing around makes my FPS fluctuate, and this game *should* run well on my 3060.

-No options for silenced secondary weapons.

-Player character gets caught on every single little piece of protruding geometry, which becomes infuriating after the 5th time it happens.

-If you accidentally get discovered, even if you kill the enemy who sees you without them firing a shot, everyone on base immediately knows where you are despite the person that discovered you not making any broadcasts to others or tripping an alarm.

-Movement feels sluggish as all hell. Like, I get it, a "Ghost Warrior" cant just be running and gunning, this isnt Call of Duty, but it just feels horrible, cumbersome, and slow.

-No elevation on objective markers. Oh, there is a place where you can see a collectible or plant some c4? No way to tell on the map if its above of below you. Also, there isnt any way I can find to manually place a marker on the map. Which wouldnt really matter if you could, because the game doesnt have a compass, somehow. (???)

-Inconsistent bullet trajectories, which is awful considering that that should be the 100% most well detailed part of a SNIPING GAME. Even when no wind is present, bullets can sometimes veer off left or right midflight, which you cant correct for.

-The bug in this game are everywhere. Planting explosives or doing other things sometimes renders you as unable to hold a gun, you have to use the radial menu rather than the hotkey to switch weapons, which can get you killed at the wrong time. Wind sometimes instantly changes from one direction to another, instead of doing so gradually. Sometimes wind will just be blowing while youre indoors, affecting your shots somehow. Enemies looking for you with binoculars will sometimes give you a warning to get to cover, other times will just pick you up instantly with no chance to hide. Sniper rifle damage is also inconsistent, I had single shot kills to the chest on some basic enemies, but not others, while using the same rifle.

-A total lack of gun customization. Maybe its because I only played for 4 hours, but I only had a single Sniper Rifle and pistol that had a suppressor on it. You cant manually add a suppressor to any rifle. In a game that makes you calculate distance and wind speed/direction and adjust your rifle sights accordingly, why cant I choose to put a silencer on whatever gun I want? Also, for being a sniping sim, why are suppressors unlimited use?

-Enemies are FAR too accurate.. A soldier with an AK landing 6 shots on me from 250+ meters away is insane, especially when the designated counter-snipers the enemy has have to take time to aim and shoot.

-Minor gripe, but the markers you tag enemies with are way too hard to see. White markers against a snowy environment is needlessly annoying to keep track of.

Do not buy this game for any price. You WILL be let down.
