review_text:
Close call deciding to rate this positive or negative. I had basically been waiting for a game like this to come out ever since I saw Alien as a kid and watching my dad play Dead Space. It has everything I ever wanted in terms of aesthetic and body horror elements which is something that affects me greatly, even when it comes to small things. I'm the type of person that can get nauseous just from someone talking about blood, guts, or surgery... things of that sort, so I guess you could say I have a fear of offal. And yes, I became very, very, very, very nauseous in the late-game...

Unfortunately, all of these sentiments are held back by the sometimes rage-inducing parts of this game that highlight a staggeringly simplistic gameplay loop. The first issue I can see that ruins any fear or anxiety a player might have coming into this is the combat and limited number of enemy types. It is laughable that after fighting the first actual foe the game throws at you, you already know how to cheese the rest of the enemies in the game. How am I supposed to be scared of something once I realize I can just strafe around it in a circles while it helplessly misses every attack? Not to mention that I was pretty liberal with my heals and ammo and still had a surplus, the exact opposite of the claim that players will have to choose their battles to progress. Another issue tied with this is that the "combat" portion of the game has a significant bulk to it, and its length further exposes how bad the gunplay is. Also, the only normal "boss" the game has is one of the worst designed bosses I have ever fought, and was the only time I died during my playthrough. Thankfully so, as I have heard rumors that the save system is piss-poor so it seems my run could have been a much greater headache.

Despite all of this, for me I believe I took a net positive experience from this. I can say with satisfaction that there wasn't a moment during my run that I was bored, as every time that I wasn't directly progressing I was absorbed in the architecture and ambient sounds that the levels provide. In some weird twisted way the world almost becomes relaxing as you get used to the sights and sounds. If you still decide to pick up Scorn do so knowing that I personally only enjoyed it because I had a pre-established fascination with H.R. Giger and body horror like I said before, so gauge if this is money well spent for YOU.

Ya know, I played Jet Set Radio back in the day, and it was my favorite game for a time. I enjoyed the unique blend of hip hop radio music, stylish city settings, grinding on rails, writing graffiti, etc. It was a novelty.

Bomb Rush Cyberfunk tries to be like Jet Set Radio, but, it doesn't work for me. The music is filled with more misses than hits. The graffiti feels limited and too one note. I wish I could upload tags and pieces like in JSR, but I don't think that's a feature. The police heat star system is annoying. All of the playable characters in BRC feel the same in terms of gameplay other than having different skins and inserting sound bites of them saying "YEAH!" and "NICE!" over and over.

Even if I turn off the music and put on another playlist, the game doesn't draw me in. It's unfortunate, because I like the bare bones aspects of parts of the game. It just doesn't feel fleshed out enough to merit a thumbs up from me.

review_text:
I've beaten this game before on xbox and it quickly became one of my favorite games of all time. This is a fantastic game and the best out of the entire Arkham series. They took everything that was good about Arkham Asylum and cranked it up to 11. The open world oozes atmosphere. The combat is polished further and overhauled. The story is interesting and enjoyable with cool side missions. They even did more with the Riddler challenges by adding neat mini-puzzles throughout the world. This game feels like the devs were genuinely inspired and enthusiastic about making it and it shows. 

I have noticed some minor bugs on this port though such as an enemy snapping to a different location prior to combat, some of the multi-enemy counters not connecting, a grapple attack not connecting, and some goofy physics bugs after a double takedown. These only occurred on rare occasions but occurred more than once. It didn't affect the gameplay overall but were a little annoying. Additionally the mouse is always visible in center screen in the menu when you are playing with controller. The DLC's port also had some bugs, such as Robin's attacks and counters not connecting on occasion. The last fight didn't have any counter indicators when fighting the robots and I experienced a fatal crash at the same part. When I reloaded it didn't happen again but it was still annoying. I think the game itself is a 5/5 but the bugs in the port force me to give it a 4/5.

The gameplay in World of Goo is [i]very[/i] simple. It's triangle-building simulator with a few things tacked on, but hey, it doesn't get stale because of the themes of the different chapters, and the few added mechanics. Wouldn't say that I'd go achievement hunting for this game though.

The atmosphere in this game is great; the bright colors paired with overly industrial grays lead to this cheerful-yet-dreary feeling that's almost unique to World of Goo and other Tomorrow Company games.

Doesn't last too long (5-6 hours), but is a nice nostalgia trip.

review_text:
[h1] Tldr; Mediocre controls slapped on an otherwise great story with dull protagonists who won't shut up. [/h1] 

I was baited by the "overwhelmingly positive" reviews on Steam and it needs to be acknowledged that the story is emotional and deserves all the praise. But that's about the only positive this game has. Despite being a story-driven game, it's not justified if the game play is clunky and if the protagonists (that have 80% of dialogue) keep interrupting an otherwise smooth immersion into a heart-gripping tale. 

The puzzles are repetitive and get monotonous rather quickly as little is to be achieved from tile-inverting minigames. The pixel graphics may be good to look at, but with invisible barriers everywhere, it's a dumb click-fest just to get your character to move where he/she needs to so the story can progress. 

The protagonists are apathetic and constantly taking a jibe at the journey of the man whose dream they are supposed to be fulfilling which defeats the whole purpose of the story. The music is decent but the negatives of this game outweigh the positives which makes it impossible to recommend that someone pay money for this lackluster excuse of a video game. If you want to buy, make sure you pick it up during a sale, full price is undeserved. 

I may be in the minority in not recommending this game; I have no hesitation in paying for a 5-hour game focusing on a good story but if I had to drag myself just to get to the end and if the game itself feels like a chore, the payoff is not worth anyone's money or time no matter how good the story is.

review_text:
Blades of the Shogun has received a lot of critical acclaim; and by and large it deserves it.  However there are a pair of fundamental flaws that take a truly great game and turn it into a frustrating slog.

The positive reviews have already focussed on what's good.  The graphics, the atmosphere, and the music are all very good.  The idea behind the gameplay is excellent and everything is well put together.

I really wanted to like Blades of the Shogun. But eventually I found myself playing for completion rather than out of enjoyment.  Blades of the Shogun is a puzzle game marketted as a tactical stealth based game; which is not in and of itself a problem except in execution.

A tactical game should allow preparation before missions; should allow inventory management; and should allow a choice of team.  A puzzle game gives a set - and limited - number of items and characters up front and asks that the missions be completed using them.  AND THIS IS STILL NOT THE PROBLEM, I enjoy the idea of working with a limited loadout to solve each stage.  I enjoy the planning and stealth aspect so, please, bear with me.  I'm working up to where Blades of the Shogun goes so horribly wrong.

Blades *really* should have been a turned based game.  Or at least it should have allowed time to be paused whilst thinking.  It has one of the clumsiest, clunkiest interfaces I've played with.  Timing is incredibly important, as is being able to select a character and execute an involved command set.  What actually happens, when executing a plan, is that half way through the enemy that absolutely needed to die is slightly obscured by an invisible collision polygon for a wall two feet to the left. And Instead of throwing a shuriken the character will stop and blithely tell you he doesn't see a way to climb it.

Not being able to precisely execute commands is a huge problem.  Shadow mode exists but can't be used for anything complex, it's just there to allow two or three kill commands to be simultaneously executed.  It can't be used to tell a character to, for example: go there, wait for another character, then have both kill an enemy and run into the shadows.  Shadow mode is tragically very limited.

It is towards the later stages is that things get truly frustrating.  Huge maps with walls and cliffs everywhere cause the camera to bounce all over the place and make picking enemies or the ground even more difficult.  The camera can't be pointed straight down and must be twitched left and right to try and see.  Couple this with characters who get hooked on each other, rocks and sometimes the enemy and they're going to be dying a lot.

The path finding is bizarre too.  The nice straight, quiet line from here to there can become an epic journey as a character decides they don't want to go where you want them to.  Group selecting characters is risky in anything but the simplest maneuvers.  As mentioned they hook on each other, spaz out, do twitchy circular dances and generally fail to do what they've been told if they are too close together.  Which they will be, if group selected, because they clip right into each other when they move to the same spot.

So the player characters often die unintentionally.  A single dead character fails the mission.  And this brings me, finally, to the most fundamental flaw that Blades of the Shogun has.  Load times.  For a game where loading is ubiquitous there seems to have been little effort put into optimising it.  I have - quite literally - spent more of my play time watching the loading screen than actually playing the game.  And this is why I've given it a negative review.

For a game in which even tiny failures means death, failures that are often game flaws rather than player mistakes, to not have instantaneous load times is a slap in the face.  Again it's the huge, intricate later stages that are the problem.  Trying and reloading repeatedly whilst re-executing the same convoluted plan just sucks the fun right out of everything.  It turns Blades of the Shogun into a boring slog of quick-loading.  Every time an enemy starts shouting for guards when they should have been dead.  Every time a character twitches into a view cone that they shouldn't have.  Every time someone dies unexpectedly the stage must be reloaded.  It's horrible and frustrating and it's the first time in years that I've actually hated a game.

And it's unnecessary.  

Had the gameplay been pausable or turn based then twitching the camera to correctly select something would not have been a problem.  Had there been a better mechanism for setting up and executing plans then there would not have been a problem.  Even if neither of those could be implemented then quick loading and saving would have fixed the problem.  But none of that was done, and that leaves us with the game we have.

In summary: Blades of the Shogun is a puzzle game rather than a tactical game.  It has a poorly implemented interface, hard to focus camera and repeated, pointless long load times.  (Also Yuki has killed almost as many people as Chairman Mao but still sobs and cries, through each assassination, that she must be brave and not stupid; her voice actor makes me want to claw my ears off.)

If you're not looking to play through the whole game then buy Blades of the Shogun but realise that the late game is a frustrating let-down.

review_text:
Played on Mouse and Keyboard. Controller appear to be Broken with several inputs not registering properly. Game Officially recommends Controller

I really want to like this one, the setting is immaculate, sound design is absolutely on point. The opening hour of the game are Incredible at building tension, and the initial enemy reveal was done Beautifully. Unfortunately that's where the good stopped for me.

I don't know if I just got bad RNG. But in the 3 hours or so, I've found maybe a total of 25 bullets. Not missing a single shot its 3 charged shots to kill an enemy, but there's such a heavy artificial weapon sway that for every 3 shots I hit, one or two miss.

The combat gets in the way. I love hard, I love gritty "Every shot count" tension. One of my favorite survival shooters that does this well is is Metro 2033, which I've completion on Hardcore Ranger mode. Looting every little scrap and finding clever ways to deal with enemies to save even a single bullet, with the threat that one mistake and I die and it's over. The challenge was always exhilarating. Recently also completed Resident Evil Biohazard on Permadeath mode, as well as the recent Deadspace remake in the leadup to the release.

That balance is not found here.

I'm constantly having to Buy or Craft every piece of ammo i physically can, and still running out Every Single Encounter. I've died more in the first 3 hours than I did in the same time in Dark Souls 1.

That's just not fun. 

The oppressive tension of never having enough of anything to progress is too constant. When its all pull no push its numbing.

Enemies lost their Fear factor Very quickly due to this and instead became a headache.

Can't comment in the story, as I did not get far enough in to have much understanding of any narrative aside from Theres a Virus, I have an Anchor, looking for an Anomoly.

Got locked into an inescapable auto-save death loop and put down the game.

EDIT - I will be picking the game back up after completing some other games releasing using some tips from the folks in the comments. I REALLY want to know what happened in this world, and Everything aside from the never having any bullets is perfect. Hopefully I will have better RNG on my next run.

I'm really glad Adam had a return to form making this game. Gives a lot of the vibes WTTG2 did in a good way, while cutting down on some of the more cryptic and frustrating elements. It's definitely not as hard. 

I have two critiques. The first concerns the decision to make the Noir talk, specifically the lady. Part of what made them so creepy was their total silence. It takes away a lot of the creepiness to hear them. I understand it's to avoid some frustration with her mechanic of getting close, but you should have more faith in your players to do it, or maybe instead of her speaking she could gesture for you to come closer. 

Secondly, I feel as though there needs to be a short grace period after dealing with threats, at least in the non-nightmare modes. Multiple times now I've had to deal with female Noir on the roof, only to get shot by Lucas two seconds later without even realizing the laser was there. 

Good job on the game besides that.

review_text:
The much touted “spiritual successor” to Dead Space, but to be honest, it doesn’t hold a candle to that franchise, not even close.

The Callisto Protocol’s beginning is pretty strong and rather intriguing, at a first glance it does look like a decent spooky time is waiting for you and the first half of the game is not bad, pretty decent, it does have great action set pieces and it keeps you on your toes for new monstrosities around seemingly every corner.

Then comes the rest of the game after the mine drilling section, which then becomes a repetitive and tedious slog when the developers literally ran out of budget and start to recycle certain enemies and even some levels.

The game keeps promising an amazing payoff at the end, but once you reach said payoff… You’re left with the feeling of a rushed wet fart and one of the worst final bosses in a horror game, ever, both on a plot and mechanical standpoints.

The graphics are amazing and it runs great I guess, not a single stutter in my entire playthrough, although I did get a couple of crashes and the main menu's "continue" option completely disappeared, making me think my save was gone, but it wasn't; starting a new game and IMMEDIATELY hitting "Load Save" took me back to where I left off, or rather before the game crashed. 

Alas, good graphics and good performance can only carry you for so long; all the good will and strong narrative from the first half are completely gone by the time you’ve reached the final boss and the ending only makes it worse due to how disappointing that payoff is. I only played the base game by the way, screw that jazz about adding another ending through paid DLC, f**k that.

I guess the game is good enough if you manage to find it SUPER cheap, especially with the first half being legitimately decent, but honestly I’d recommend you buy the Dead Space remake instead, heck, buy the entire franchise and yes, including the third one. Am I implying Dead Space 3 is better than Callisto Protocol? F**K YES it is! At least that game has better combat mechanics and co-op, this one only has missed potential and disappointment waiting for you.

6/10 - Much better games out there, get as cheap as possible.

review_text:
100 hour review:

For a city builder the AI is weak. You can't control their behavior, schedule their work, restrict zones, lock gates, assign food or work policies, and can't control the villagers directly. Due to this the majority of the challenge mid to late game becomes preventing your villagers from constantly trying to wonder away from your village to pickup resources next to the enemy which is suicide. Workers can only build one thing at a time, if you have 100 units of wall sections and 100 builders you'd think it would be a quick job but no, they will ALL go towards one section and then in to a section thats furthest away.

The towers in this game are not balanced. Early game you can get by without them by picking up enemies and dropping them into a "cullis", its a building which instantly kills any thing thrown into it. Early game towers aren't necessary and late game they are pointless as mobs scale indefinitely and you don't.  When mobs scale to 15,000 health and 5x faster movement speed your tower that shoots for 30 when you first started the map is not going to do much. And one of the main utility towers called "banish tower", its projectile speed isn't even fast enough to catch the enemies passing next to it.

Strategy late game consists of 97% of you picking up enemies with 15,000 health(every single one of them and there are thousands of them each night) and dropping them into a cullis, because your 30-40 damage tower isn't going to get the job done. There are 5 type of enemies, 3 of which are susceptible to being permanently frozen, the other 2 types which are specters and fire elementals you would need to drop into a cullis and its not fun to do it few hundred times. The other 3% is remembering to recast your AOE freeze spell, don't do it too many times or your FPS will drop to single digits. Building a maze is optional, making the enemy funnel at a single point is sufficient for this strategy.

Colony sim... don't have anything negative to say about this part of the game..

So out of the 4 tags, tower defense, colony sim, city builder, & strategy only 1/4 passed.

review_text:
I wish I could recommend this game, it has a lot of charm and potential, but it still feels like an early access game, not only in bugs/flaws but features and design. As such, charging $25 USD is way too much. I could probably recommend it at half the price. For this review, I've dabbled in all of the levels and got Gold on every challenge in one of the levels (Which the gold medals in this game feel tough to meet, only ever beating time trials by milliseconds or 1-2 seconds at most), so I feel like I've played with the mechanics and systems enough to have a solid opinion.

The biggest flaw has to be the controls (It was designed for controller, so will be referencing their inputs), well specifically how you do tricks. It feels like it was ripped straight from other trick systems (Tony Hawks, SSX, etc ), you do them by being airborne, holding the North/South/West face buttons and flicking your left stick in one of the four directions. This is great for those other games where you have long hang times and can freestyle moves and chain them together before you hit the ground, but as a parkour game, you hardly have the opportunity to string moves together more than 2 at a time, if even that. What's worse, and the main reason I bring this up, is that the jump button (south face button) has one too. This game also feature variable jumping where holding the button increases distance. So often times, as I've seen in other reviews or gameplay, you will try to prep a jump by holding it just before you land, but if you press the jump button while in air, you do a trick and flail out and crash. And because it's tied in with left stick, there is often conflict between movement and tricking (Better make sure your stick returns to neutral before trying to trick). Maybe a combo system would have been better here, or trick on button release instead of press, or just not using the jump button as also a trick button (And you can't remap controls, so that's great for a fully released game in 2025).

Besides the core problem, there are a lot of minor gripes that indicate it should still be in early access, like your characters arms and legs and the camera clipping through walls and seeing inside textures. The tutorial being very bare bones and feeling like devolopment test world, and then you having to spend the next 20 mins in the menu's learning things the tutorial left out (which is a lot). There's also some inconsistencies with the zipline, both in how it functions and compared to other systems (You hold to hang zipline but not for ledges? I thought back ejects were just straight up broken until I stopped holding the button, but don't expect side ejects if you're an AC fan). Some of the environments feel very barren, flat textured walls, no ornamentation (don't expect to be hopping up window shutters or electrical boxes) though I will say the parkour gym is really nice. I also wish there was more feedback. How long am I or can I hold the jump button? Do I have enough speed to wall run? Contextual prompts would be nice, like if I hold left shoulder button, the UI should display my options instead of burying it in a menu.

Now for features, there are 6 maps each with 8 challenges. There are only 2 types of challenges, time trials (Run through rings), and trick rush (do tricks in a shrinking area for score). The medals will reward currency which can be used for cosmetics. That's the entire game. I really wish there was more variety, maybe a race to the goal any way possible, or maybe a single trick score, or maybe don't get caught by AI or run from a wall. You'd think there would be a ghost mode or something to guide players, or even better yet, design the levels so that the challenge teaches new concepts and becomes more difficult over time. The game does a horrible job teaching you anything. There is also adrenaline (boost) and the scoring system. The scoring system has a timing window that gets smaller the higher the combo. Adrenaline will pause the timing window, so at higher scores you are spam clicking Left Stick In, otherwise you'll randomly lose your combo, which does not feel fun at all.

There are multiplayer game modes, but they are half baked at best. There's capture the flag, trick rush, and tag. If you are tagged/flag holder your L1/LB standing jump is just lost and replaced with a tag, and there's an annoying push mechanic that is very inconsistent (again, contextual prompts would help). You cant even change map or communicate in the lobby before hand, and winning the matches gives no reward. The maps are way too big for the game modes of 4 players. I feel like the taggers name should be invisible and move faster or have faster filling adrenaline or something. There's a free play multiplayer mode that is nice if you don't have toxic players. 

The inputs are very tight, and the feet landing has to be perfect, there were so many times it looked like the character would land the move, just to trip (even mashing roll). I often felt more frustration than fun getting gold on the challenges.

Part of the negative review is that the game just isn't for me, doing the same time trial for 30 mins because I held jump a millisecond before I landed to prep my next long jump just to unlock a new shoe isn't my cup of tea. There's a lot of skill for this game, but also some luck and jank. And I know it's an Idie dev, and I would have recommended this if it was early access and cheaper, but it just feels and looks unpolished. Game has a ton of potential and is really fun at times. The soundtrack is great and you can tell a lot of love and passion went into this game, but ultimately it still needs some work. I hope the game continues to be improved.

review_text:
Hakuoki Demon of the Fleeting blossoms was my very first and all time favourite Visual Novel, so when I saw that they had added new characters and changed it up, I just HAD to get it. Kyoto Winds is the first part of two games, the other being Edo Blossoms. It is essentially the same story as Fleeting Blossoms but now there are twelve guys to romance instead of just the main guys from the first one. I can't tell you how excited I was to see Shinpachi was now available to romance because he was always my favourite next to Saito. 

It was nostalgic to read through the story again and there were pleasant surprises with the additions of new characters introduced in certain routes. Hachiro Iba and his story was definitely a surprise and I am really glad they included him. I have played nearly 20 hours so far, and I haven't even done Yamazaki, Sanan, Chikage or Sakamoto's routes yet, and I skipped a lot of the reading I had already read (especially after playing back to back characters) so that should give you an idea of just how long the game is. 

The Cg's are beautiful and there is definitely tension in a lot of them, but don't expect to see any romance (barring one CG that I won't spoil) because this game is just the getting to know the characters before getting into the real nitty gritty of the relationships in Edo Blossom. But don't let that stop you from buying it as the getting to know the characters is one of the best parts of the game and the CG's you get as Yukimura and each character get closer are worth it.

If you love amazing story, romantic tension, beautiful CG's and history, then you should definitely give this game a go. Don't forget to get Edo Blossom as well (grab the bundle!) and you'll go on a rollercoaster that will leave you emotionally wrecked (hopefully in a good way) by the end.

With hundreds of hours in the game from 2017-current, this is the best form the game has been in and it continues on an upward trajectory.  The lead devs have been very active in both public discord and private conversations.  Through my interactions with them, I fully trust that they can move RHL from early access to full launch without straying from their mission and with Gearbox behind them as the publisher, I am not concerned about them wavering on their ethical monetization principles.

Gameplay is fun, builds are diverse, grind is relaxing.  That being said, if you aren't a fan of warframe or destiny-esque grinds, then skip this title.  Movement is snappy, the systems are simple enough to be broadly approachable, but deep enough to keep you coming back to further tailor your build.

Overall, would recommend -- if not now, then definitely on full release.

name: After the Fall®

review_text:
I'm a fan of the dot hack series (be it games, animes or light novels) and I still have the PS2 version of those games but let's be honest, this remaster is a joke ... potentially a scam.

Let's skip the fact that a playstation controller isn't supported despite the game being originally from PS2 and now only on playstation 4, and that the game hasn't an option for playstation overlay buttons. It's a inconvenience (most of all for the tightly timed QTE when disarming traps) but can be worked around with mods.

No the real problem is the lack of work this port ... or should I say ... this emulation has receive.
- saves that disappear magically after some random period of time (edit : they are actually still there but you need to restart Steam -not just the game- to see them again) (edit2 : launching the game with administrator's rights seem to prevent that to happen ... seriously bad port).
- Many visual glitches (edit: most -but not all- can be worked around by setting the shadows to low).
- Lack of proper PC options, and some of them aren't properly implemented, like for vsync where enabling it locks the game at 30 fps ... but with the game being slow down since the speed is tied to the framerate, or disabling vsync which locks at 60 fps but with a tearing fest like you probably never seen. (edit: the vsync 30fps lock only seems to apply when using full screen mode. You can use borderless windows to work around that but have to use the same resolution as your desktop).
- PC options not even accessible in-game. You have to return to the title screen (the one where you can select which game to load) but you can't even quit the game unless you spend 30 minutes in the 1st part of the tutorial (but you usually want to test the settings right of the bat).
- Same (very short) draw distance as on PS2.
- Textures barely upgraded on the background (it's ok on the characters) which is very (very) blurry. (edit: texture filtering is indeed doing more harm than anything, disabling it got you less blurry textures).
- And so on.

Add to that, that the game isn't an especially good Action RPG if you're not into dot hack storyline. The gameplay is quite limited, the game ask the player to "return IRL" quite frequently ("guess I will log out and check my emails" will be the sentence you will hear the most), the ctuscene using the game engine are strange since there is a delay before each character started talking which results in something quite funny when the conversation heating up but is plagued with silence between each sentence), which would be unthinkable nowadays, but since they didn't even port the game correctly, it's no use to expect they would refine the game itself.

Frankly I really hesitated to ask for a refund right away. The only reason I didn't was because, as I said, I'm a fan and having already finished that game on PS2, I want to know what is the 4th story/game they added.

For those that are still interested in the game, I would strongly recommend to get it on console.

review_text:
Amazing visuals!!! I really love the character design. Lighting, fluids and other effects are great, the sound is well defined.

For the gameplay, I don't compare it to "Metroidvania" style or anything, I look at it independently and I really like it.
You will have enough gold when you will realize that you can sell a lot of found items. 
Yeah sure not getting exp when killing monster can seem frustrating but I barely noticed it as it is the same for a lot of other games. And I don't feel the need for it, evolution through better equipment is cool too...
For the combat system, as for any games which are not "assisted" you will just have to "git gud" and that's it. Personaly I think it is quite good, you have to calculate your moves because it is not fast paced. You will feel personal improvements.
I like the arrows that bounce back on your shield (yes it is important)
I like the variety of items/weapons/artifacts and their effects, there is a lot of ways to handle new areas and enemies.
In fact, new areas/enemies will force you to change your gear and gameplay, it is refreshing.

name: GTTOD: Get To The Orange Door

review_text:
Ironically the extreme amount of time it took to release this episode of the story both affords it leniency and deprives it of leniency. But regardless of either, it is a lukewarm and heavily disappointing iteration of the story.


This took an utterly ridiculous amount of time to release, especially considering how overly funded it was. A variety of problems seemingly hindered its release but in the end; this simple point and click game took three years to produce. With over two million dollars in funding that is completely unacceptable behaviour. In nearly every sense, a failure.

The game itself has a very distinct arch of quality. To start the scene transitions are extremely abrupt, multiple beginning areas feel shallow and clearly exist as a desperate reference to Friendsim, characters lack a variety of idle expressions needed to actually telegraph their mood in conversation, the inventory is overly cluttered and full of uninteresting objects that aren't very compelling to use on anything; there is also an asinine delay between when a conversation begin and actual dialogue starts being typed out. This game took three years to make.

Despite all this the start of the game does gradually build a solid atmosphere with nice pacing and decently interesting item puzzles. It really does start to replicate the quality set forth by the first act.

Then the [spoiler]trial[/spoiler] sequence begins. It is extremely long, probably over an hour long if not more, and has no direct relevance to the main story at all. From a writing perspective it is an entire derailment of the story because for probably over an hour players are basically stuck in what is practically an entirely different game with an entirely different plot; for no reason. It's like the developers randomly got bored of working on a point and click adventure game and instead decided to make this spinoff game instead. But instead of it being a spinoff they just forcibly adapted it into being a sequence in this game. 

Beyond that, from a gameplay point of view this section of the game is abhorrently unfun. The game takes what is a relatively dynamic, complicated situation and forcibly converts it into a very linear choose-the-right-dialogue-or-item-option-to-progress trial and error gauntlet that makes almost no sense over half the time. The entire sequence is meant to be about deduction and logic but it often operates under information that players simply do not know, and then the game acts like the player made a mistake for not choosing the right option. In a situation where the necessary information is either being withheld from them or buried beneath unintuitive allusions. It's like playing connect the dots with invisible dots, make a connection between two random points and hope it's correct.

This sequence is so extremely out of place, overly long, mechanically ramshackle, and entirely irrelevant to the story that it completely sapped my will to even keep playing. Because after all that, all of that, players may not even be able to select the proper conclusion in-game even if they know the final answer because the player didn't have the right items. Apparently the items that players got up until that point, from their random choices in previous parts of the game and possibly even in the first game too since the save files do transfer over; these items actually determine the players ability to reach the successful conclusion in this completely different bit of the game.

Even more absurd; the game has the audacity to give players a summary of all the things they did wrong that led to them not canonically reaching the correct conclusion. After this totally incoherent, trial and error, over an hour long sequence of badly telegraphed information driven gameplay the game lectures the player about their so-called mistakes. All this really accomplishes is further alienating players from the game by exposing how totally asinine and wasted this time was, because the conclusion was determined entirely by picking random options without proper information and or having specific random items already beforehand; not actual genuine player input. So not only was this whole thing irrelevant to the story but it also bashes whatever investment the player may have in this sequence by proving that the whole thing was out of the players control from the start.

It seems that after finishing this section of the game the developers themselves were tired too, as after that sequence the game immediately devolves into fetch quests. Over, and over, the game demands players walk back and forth along a very long horizontal map talking to characters to perform multiple fetch quests. Talk to character, walk down one side of the map, pick up item, go back, talk to character, progress, talk to new character, repeat. The game does this perhaps seven times in a row; this is the entire remainder of the experience before the final puzzle. The game even acknowledges that it's giving players fetch quests in a funny bit of dialogue as some kind of twisted irony that it is self aware of its own lazy, shallow design. They took three years with this and still skimped out on the entire second half of the game after also skimping out on multiple starting areas.

The final puzzle is a complete mess of asinine, random trial and error use-random-items-on-random-things over and over until something happens gauntlet as well. Players can also be game over'd by certain decisions and forced to go through the whole process again for no reason. Players aren't even allowed to save during this part, the game literally stops acknowledging saves, completely forcing players to be reset if they get a spontaneous game over from a random item interaction.

And as nice as it is to see all the trolls from the Friendsim game in this one, it also is extremely awkward that somehow they all magically ended up appearing in the story. Not even spread out, they almost all show up in this act in one massive reference dump inexplicably. And players almost exclusively only interact with them, all the other new trolls are just background decoration. Except for maybe three. I believe at least one of them is the troll that some one paid the creator large amounts of money to be able to design their own troll and have it put in the game. Because apparently the creator has no respect for their own work and is willing to sell canonical access to money hoarders who can afford to dump thousands if not tens of thousands of dollars into an indie game kickstarter to reach exclusive backer tiers. Ironic corruption considering that the story of Alternia is all about corruption and inequality.


In spite of all the aforementioned smaller problems the game has, which are especially disturbing considering how long the developers had to work on it and smooth these things out for a proper release, the first couple hours of the game are genuinely fun and live fairly well up to the quality the first game set. But the mid game sequence was draining, erroneous to the plot, frustrating, confusing and ultimately invalidates itself by revealing that from the start the player was doomed to the conclusion they'll reach by not having the right items already or picking the right random dialogue options. Then after that huge exhausting waste of time, the story resumes to now suddenly just be a bunch of awful fetch quests purposely stringing the player along pointless distances for zero reason besides desperate padding. And to top it all off; the final puzzle is an incoherent trial and error gauntlet of absolutely asinine item usages. 

A strong, promising start and ascent; followed by a baffling, absurd intermission; then by a shallow decline straight into a frustrating and unsatisfying conclusion.

If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38950844-Anoemalous/] here [/url].

review_text:
I wish steam had a "Meh" option

This game has no identity, it feels like a formulaic combination of Dead Space, Silent Hill and Resident Evil. Sometimes it works, most of the time it doesn't.

Sound design. Music:

+ No complains here, music is easily the best part. I liked it. Gave me Stranger Things vibe
+ Sound design is nice, every howl, growl, ambient sound, floorstep, etc. Everything sounds good, definitely play it in headphones only.


Enemy:

- Only few enemy "variety" and really it comes down to: a fast one, a normal one, ranged, armored, big and bosses.
- Boss fights = you literally run in one circle and shoot, maybe set things on fire. That's it. Also the game even gives you the same boss THREE FUCKING TIMES
- All these spores, sprouts, cliché looking appendages... come on, you can do better than that.


Locations:

+- Two good locations: some parts of snowy town and a hospital, the rest is boring, not memorable, empty and plain


Controls:

- You are VERY slow. Even in DS you moved much faster and felt agile and ready to any fight. Here you can't dodge at all, so most fights are just clunky, awkward and exausting
- You can ealisy get stuck on objects and textures, especially if you are trying to do anything fast (I got stuck on a ladder, because I interacted with it too fast lol)
- You are shooting NOT from your gun but from a camera behind you. So if your character is behind an object, your bullet WILL HIT THAT OBJECT even if your gun is not in it's way. First time I see shit like this
+- Shooting feels punchy and fun at first, but you HAVE to charge every. fucking. shot. to do damage, otherwise you are just wasting bullets.


Gameplay mechanics:

- You need to start the tram TWO TIMES doing exactly the same, the location is a copypaste too. Even your character says that she is tired of it (lol)
- Probably the worst inventory management existed. You never have enough space so you have to always come back to your safe room and storage stuff.
- Upgrades are meaningless, you'll basically spend everything on inventory space anyway
- You have enough money to upgrade only ONE, maybe 1.5 FUCKING WEAPON TO MAX (but there is achievement to get every weapon, and it's about 7) thank God, you can just collect enough for one, upgrade it, reload the save, upgrade another one and etc. it works
+- You'll only use two, maybe three guns: a pistol, a shotgun and maybe BFG. Weapons with carabine ammo basically useless. Game is about saving ammo and knowing when to use and you give us automatic rifles that does low dmg?
- You have only 1 fire bomb, 2 max if you upgrade it. So once again, you will need to run back a lot to your safe room to get more. Sure, you'll get a mine later on, but it will also take another slot in your inventory
-+ NG+ sometimes give way too much HP to enemies (Abyss boss is pain), but on a positive side in NG+ you already know every door code necessary, so it helps


Story. Voice acting:

- Story is the worst part, I honestly couldn't care less after the hospital location and just wanted it to end. It doesn't bring anything new while being confusing even when you read notes and listen to conversations
- Voice acting and animations are waaaay over the top, they show emotions that are too extreme, cartoony and don't feel real
- Goal is to save humanity, but if you extract 3 humans, in order to extract more you need to DELETE the previous one (????) and you can even delete PLOT CHARACTERS. WHAT'S THE FUCKING POINT THEN?
- Ending is underwelming, all I thought was: "... wait what?"
- Your choices mean ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. Why give it to us? Even if you choose a different option, you'll get maybe ONE additional line, that's it. Usually characters react exactly the same to your response. Lame and lazy.


Settings:

- No FOV slider in a 2025 game (...)
- You can't skip most cutscenes and they are very boring, people just slowly talk words that mean nothing
-+ Optimization sucks, but on low plays ok


tldr:

Overall, feels like a downgrade from Silent Hill 2 Remake devs in terms of story, animations, locations and even gameplay. I didn't mind finishing it once, but it's not worth the full price. Get it on 50-75%

6/10 for me, but I really wanted to play a Dead Space clone, so I can see a lower score here.

A "Very positive" rating on Steam feels wrong though.

review_text:
One of the most fantastic but frustrating games I have ever played.

To start off, the game is fantastic in the sense that 2K & Irrational games have created a game that is truly unique and vastly different than any other game at the time.  Almost 10 years later, Bioshock has aged very well and can easily be played for many more years to come.  The weapons & combat system offer great variety and satisfaction.  Shooting an enemy with a pistol to taking photos of hideous splicers for damage buffs, each weapon offers something unique for every combat situation as well as enjoyability.  

Visually, Bioshock is beautiful; considering it's age, the graphic design really is ground breaking compared to many other games that were made of the same year.  There are many small details that Irrational games added to give a strong emotional feel towards Rapture - the environment and atmosphere in particular.  The water and fire effects are pleasing to look at.  I believe the graphics in Bioshock will withstand the test of time.

The story is very well done.  From beginning to end you will most definitely be engaged,  I don't want to put any spoilers on this review so I will keep this part short; the game's story is very good.

Now,  this is the kicker for this game - not the game in particular, but, STEAM's version of the game.  There are MAJOR MAJOR MAJOR bug issues with this game on STEAM.  First of all, you cannot play this game without a microphone plugged in; don't even bother starting it up because you're game is just going to crash before you even hit the main menu.  

The next part is where Bioshock on STEAM will make you drop to your knees and cry.  The game WILL CRASH ON YOU.  I have tried everything in my power to make this game fully operational but nothing worked.  I had to save this game EVERY 30 seconds to a minute.  Since Bioshock does NOT have autosave you have to do it yourself; guess what happens when you forget to save the game? That's correct! You lose all your progress! YAY!

I somehow managed to finish this game, considering how much I enjoyed it while it managed to run for 10-15 minutes at a time before I had to reboot it.  If you can withstand this kind of frustration and headache then you will love this game - otherwise, just buy an XBOX 360 and play this game on the console.

5/5 Gameplay, Graphics and Story

0/100 for STEAM's horrendous port version of this game.

review_text:
Scorn is a mixed bag.

PROS
+The game is beautiful in a disgusting way.
+The game is disturbing, just like it wants to be.


MIDDLE
- No dialogue and almost no text. This isn't something that breaks the game, but they didn't compensate for these limits elsewhere. Detailed below.



CONS
-The visual design for puzzles is terrible. It's hard to distinguish what is an interactable element or not. The worst is an egg puzzle early on that really, really doesn't explain itself. With no text or dialogue, visual design was even more important for a game with puzzles, but it feels like they made this part bad on purpose, to spite the player. The corridors also all look the same and it's very easy to get lost, especially during the puzzle underneath the big guy about 2/3 through.

-The storytelling is pretty mixed.

-The art-book is essential for understanding plot elements, but the digital version got downgraded after people had purchased it, which is one of the most consumer unfriendly decisions I've heard in a while.

-The save-points system is abysmal. Dying can send you way back and you have to go through a lot of nonsense to get back there.

-If you get behind on resources, like bullets or healing items, you are behind for the rest of the game. Missing a few shots is enough for this to happen.

-There is a lot of audio clutter, especially around the parasite that is on your back. Every hour or so, it screams at you, you look down and the parasite punches your guts. Also, this is unavoidable damage that can kill you, which is a terrible design choice and forced me to restart a chapter because healing is very limited.

-The boss fight takes way too long and is very repetitive, which is extra frustrating because of the previously mentioned check points garbage.


OVERALL
Scorn is a game that makes almost every decision against the player. It's a game that wants you to feel as much torment as the character you're playing as and expects you to like it. Scorn is a game that hates that it's a game and wants to watch the world burn.

review_text:
Long rant. I had fun playing this game, most of the time. It's flashy, the sniping is fun, but the game hardly ever gives you an incentive to do so. As others have mentioned, most objectives are things you have to interact with, so why use a sniper and risk alerting everyone when I can sneak in undetected? I have to be in there anyways. In fact, the most fun I had in this game was NOT sniping, it was sneaking with a close range weapon.

This game has the bones of a game from 2012. Some examples:
- Enemies will immediately shoot if they see you, no surprise animation or window. If you try to rush around a corner to take someone by surprise, the enemy will most of the time immediately shoot, alerting everyone. This happened once while falling towards an enemy to do a death-from-above, in the time it took me to fall on top of him, he had turned around, seen me, and drew his weapon.
- There are no [i] meaningful [/i] stealth detection mechanics, just what level of crouched are you, and are you "concealed" in some foliage. One of the best moments I experienced in this game was being prone in some foliage with two enemies stopping to have a conversation almost right on top of me. Only to be immediately spotted a few seconds later by an enemy almost 70 meters away. Splinter Cell had dynamic light based sneaking figured out in 2002. Snake Eater had an in depth concealment system in 2004.
- It plays very much like Far Cry 3. Most of my gameplay loop was throwing a rock to distract an enemy, sneaking behind him, watching the kill animation, and hiding the body. Enemies don't care if patrols go missing, they don't react if their friend goes to check something out around a corner and doesn't come back. Enemy outposts don't communicate with each other if one comes under attack. It's very dry, and I constantly found it hard to believe that I was playing a stealth game that came out 4 years after MGSV, and 7 years after Dishonored and Far Cry 3.

What ultimately turned me off from this game was the glitches. Over my few hours I experienced:
- Multiple instances of getting stuck on an object and entering a free fall where I'm unable to move or shoot, causing me to reload
- Multiple instances of Autosave working inconsistently, especially on hidden paths. Autosaves only seemed to trigger on the main paths, so approaching an objective from a hidden path was often met with a 15-20 minute reload if you failed.
- Two instances of me being in stealth, and an entire outpost becoming alerted for seemingly no reason and immediately converging on my position. Maybe they saw one of my placed gadgets OUTSIDE of the base, but this then caused 25+ enemies to know my exact location.
- Multiple instances of reloading a save putting me not at all where it was supposed to. One instance reloaded me along a path I had been on 10 minutes prior, in the middle of the enemy camp. Another instance loaded me into somewhere on the map I hadn't been at all yet.
- Foliage being wildly inconsistent at concealing you. Standing still, my concealment icon would sometimes flash repeatedly when trying to hide in a bush, like it couldn't decide if I was concealed or not.
- More than one occasion of enemies spotting me through solid objects.
- Two occasions of the map menu ceasing to work, requiring a full game restart.
- I'm not sure if this is a bug or a feature, but occasionally, after dying to an enemy and reloading the checkpoint, that enemy would be missing from their spot, gone entirely. 

TL;DR: I had fun, there are some good moments in here. But it feels like a game which came out a decade before it did. It doesn't do anything new, and is lacking features from games released 20 years ago. It doesn't do anything interesting, besides the fun sniping mechanics, which it's constantly discouraging you from doing. Even after paying $3 for it on sale, when asked if I would recommend this game, the answer is no.

review_text:
The story itself is largely a ripoff of Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, except that film was so brilliantly written and delivered that it's completely unfair to compare them. Go and see that film if you haven't, it's genius.

To The Moon's writing is just painful, as it tries desperately hard but fails to be funny around what is ultimately supposed to be emotional and touching material, but the emotional aspects themselves just come across as trying too hard and are not really that engaging, to be honest I found myself literally wincing inside. It's also [i]so slow[/i] getting through dialogue, if this was simply written as a book I could've read through the conversations about five times as quickly, but the game just makes you wait for each and every painful and not particularly well-written line. 

Finally there is actually no game here, each scene is just go and find the same five or so objects that are identical to the objects you found in the previous scene, none of them are even hidden in any interesting ways or require any puzzle solving ability.

Definitely not my cuppa tea.

review_text:
Firm suggestion: REMAP YOUR KEYS. The default control scheme is... odd, to say the least. Somebody here on Steam helpfully wrote a guide for a more comfortable control scheme that you can utilize, or at least springboard off of, for your own comfort, so why not use it?

If you're bad at stealth games, like I am, then this is a game you want to play in small doses - maps are large and take time to complete, and even the easier missions can range into an hour or longer depending on how badly you do (in my case, it routinely takes me an hour or longer, because as I said, I'm bad at stealth games). This is also not a game where you can simply charge through and kill everything in sight - your characters are squishy, and even the strongest among you will quickly be torn apart; you will routinely be outnumbered, and if an alarm gets raised, reinforcements get called in to make things even worse; and you have to toggle your combat abilities every single time you want to attack anything, which takes precious seconds that will cost you your life.

However, the game has proven to be very engaging otherwise, and the diversity of each character's moveset strongly urges you to strategize on the fly, aided as well by the Shadow system which allows you to coordinate multiple characters' actions simultaneously. The game urges liberal use of quicksaves, and in fact has a built in function to remind you when you haven't quicksaved in a while. You can load quicksaves at the push of a button, even in the middle of being spotted by patrols, so don't worry about it if you get caught and start dying, just hit your quickload button and it magically never happened!

Mind the voice acting - it's British actors trying to affect Japanese accents. It, uh, it can be a bit touch-and-go in places.

review_text:
Yakuza 5 is called Yakuza 5 because you get to play 5 characters. Seriously though what the actual hell, as if the Devs thought Y4 did not have enough things to do for each playable character, they MADE SURE you had an obscene amount of things to do with each individual character. They looked at the previous game and just said "lets beef this thing up to the max and try to make the ultimate Yakuza game thus far".  

Dont play this game if you haven't played the Previous entries blah blah blah.

Yakuza 5 is an incredibly big improvement from Yakuza 4 in gameplay, minigames, side stories, substories (they are different!) and just about almost anything else in between. As a person who started playing the series from 0, I would say this game is the closest thing feeling wise to that one (0 is still by far the better game and still my favorite). So you might of noticed that I mentioned a few things that this game improved on, but I left out the main story from that category. The reason for that is because I Feel like the story in this game, although not terrible and honestly pretty ok, wasn't as hard-hitting or as cohesive as I would of liked it to be and felt like it was all over the place. To be honest, it was a little bit of a let-down compared to all the other games that I played in the franchise, and I feel like this happened because the devs were probably so focused on adding so many damn things to do in the game that they probably didn't have enough time or energy to develop the story just a little more to make it manageable and easy to follow. The main story overall just felt like a second thought and was predictable on certain occasions instead of it being a priority. It didn't help that each playable character took place in a completely different city so the story overall felt very split as they would explain the character first and what they are going through before getting back into the main story of the game. The main villain was also not that great, we've had much better.

The game has you starting off with Kiryu in Fukuoka which I think was a good choice from the previous game where you played him last. At the beginning of the game however, they make you do all these different things while teaching and showing you all the different stuff you can do to the point where if you dive deep into the side stories and sub-stories, you might forget completely that something is going on in the main quest. Kiryus gameplay was fun as he is such a solid fighter with the addition of new moves you can pull such as grabbing enemies when you finish a combo and overall the most balanced character. His side stories were pretty fun too as it has you driving a taxi and I really enjoyed the ones that had you racing against other opponents. The normal taxi missions though could have gone with having less of them as most of them were just you doing multiple choice questions from dialogue, so it got repetitive. If anything they should of cut the number of Taxi missions by half.

Right after you're done with Kiryu you go to Saejima which starts exactly the same as it did with the last game, and then the same cycle repeats with him as it did with Kiryu. Saejima combat wise is improved, he is still a heavy hitter that does a ton of damage with a wider range of move sets to your disposal, especially if you level him up and learn new abilities from your master trainer. His side story was one of the most enjoyable to me as you get to go out and hunt animals by being strategic as you need to be quiet when approaching a deer or with Bears being able to dodge your bullet which adds tension and forces you to land the perfect shot. My only complaint is that walking was pretty slow and the animation to set up traps and take them off got annoying as it dragged. Saejima was also the only character where you had 2 different places to travel to as the hunting side stories took place in a small village while everything else took place in the main City of Sapporo.

After you're done with Saejima you get to play... Get this... HARUKA! Which was completely different from all the other characters gameplay-wise. Haruka Does not fight but instead engages in dance battles which has you playing a rhythm game similar to karaoke. All of her side stories events are about the same thing with the exception of some where it does the same multiple choice questions you had to do with Kiryu and another one where you shake hands and answer questions while timing how long to hold the hand. As much as I appreciated Harukas part of the game, I think it dragged on for far too long because all the side stories were the same thing repeated 5 times over to the point where trying to complete it just felt like a menial task more than a fun quirky gimmick. I'm not sure why they gave Haruka the most side stories, but the game would of benefited if they just slashed that number by half just like Kiryus.

Akiyama Starts in the middle of Harukas chapter and I was actually relieved that he was the only character that didn't get side stories, you still have sub stories though and those were fine. Akiyama to me was probably the most fun character to play. He's quick, snappy with his kicks and they gave him a new ability where you can throw people in the air and whale on them. Akiyama felt like the closest thing to Dante from DMC being in this game. Him and Haruka also take place in Dotonbori so no new city for him which was honestly a relief as well.

Finally, the last character you play is a washed out Baseball Pro named Shinada. Out of all of the character's story and even the main Story of the game, I enjoyed his the most. I felt like he was relatable and felt bad for him a lot of the times because of his past and what he had to go through, there was also other times where I just felt like he was a complete idiot that doesn't have any common sense. His combat style was my least favorite, I did not like playing him and I did not like going through his section of the game because I just really did not enjoy how he fought. They advertise the character as a Weapon user but he's actually more of a Grappler and his way of fighting is just very odd. His Side stories were pretty enjoyable though as all it has you do is play in the batting cages, so if you like baseball you will like his Side stories. With his Part of the game they also introduced the best Character in all of the Franchise, Koichi Takasugi. I love that guy, he made me laugh a couple of times.

After you're done with everyone's story, the game throws you back in Kamurocho (Finally!) for the final chapter, and man do I love Kamurocho, I wish the game would just let you play there from the start instead of having you go on this wild goose chase collecting members. So besides the combat for each individual Character, I feel like This game also suffered from the same thing that Yakuza 3 suffered where enemies would just constantly block all the time, Blockuza was very apparent and alive in this entry. Normal Enemies wouldn't block as often but it still happened enough for me to notice and Boss fights... They all just blocked almost always. I don't understand what happened, Not sure if its a remaster issue or what but it was incredibly annoying fighting bosses at times, all I could do most of the time was just grab and throw them. Speaking of bosses, a lot of them were very poorly designed as some that I would fight would Spam the same move constantly without having any sort of variety. Enemies across the city would also spawn on top of each other and there were too many all over the place as I would often get into an encounter, finish it and somehow get right into another one because the enemy would be right on me. I realized that this had something to do with a text you get daily about your luck being bad or good, and if it was bad, enemies would spawn more often across the city.

Overall Was the game fun? Yeah, it was pretty fun, just too many things to do.

might forget completely that something is going on in the main quest. kiryus gameplay was fun as he is such a solid fighter with the addition of new moves you can pull such as grabbing enemies when you finish a combo and overall the most balanced character. his side stories were pretty fun too as it has you driving a taxi and i really enjoyed the ones that had you racing against other opponents. the normal taxi missions though could have gone with having less of them as most of them were just you doing multiple choice questions from dialogue, so it got repetitive. if anything they should of cut the number of taxi missions by half. right after you're done with kiryu you go to saejima which starts exactly the same as it did with the last game, and then the same cycle repeats with him as it did with kiryu. saejima combat wise is improved, he is still a heavy hitter that does a ton of damage with a wider range of move sets to your disposal, especially if you level him up and learn new abilities from your master trainer. his side story was one of the most enjoyable to me as you get to go out and hunt animals by being strategic as you need to be quiet when approaching a deer or with bears being able to dodge your bullet which adds tension and forces you to land the perfect shot. my only complaint is that walking was pretty slow and the animation to set up traps and take them off got annoying as it dragged. saejima was also the only character where you had 2 different places to travel to as the hunting side stories took place in a small village while everything else took place in the main city of sapporo. after you're done with saejima you get to play... get this... haruka! which was completely different from all the other characters gameplay-wise. haruka does not fight but instead engages in dance battles which has you playing a rhythm game similar to karaoke. all of her side stories events are about the same thing with the exception of some where it does the same multiple choice questions you had to do with kiryu and another one where you shake hands and answer questions while timing how long to hold the hand. as much as i appreciated harukas part of the game, i think it dragged on for far too long because all the side stories were the same thing repeated 5 times over to the point where trying to complete it just felt like a menial task more than a fun quirky gimmick. i'm not sure why they gave haruka the most side stories, but the game would of benefited if they just slashed that number by half just like kiryus. akiyama starts in the middle of harukas chapter and i was actually relieved that he was the only character that didn't get side stories, you still have sub stories though and those were fine. akiyama to me was probably the most fun character to play. he's quick, snappy with his kicks and they gave him a new ability where you can throw people in the air and whale on them. akiyama felt like the closest thing to dante from dmc being in this game. him and haruka also take place in dotonbori so no new city for him which was honestly a relief as well. finally, the last character you play is a washed out baseball pro named shinada. out of all of the character's story and even the main story of the game, i enjoyed his the most. i felt like he was relatable and felt bad for him a lot of the times because of his past and what he had to go through, there was also other times where i just felt like he was a complete idiot that doesn't have any common sense. his combat style was my least favorite, i did not like playing his way of fighting is just very odd. his side stories were pretty enjoyable though as all it has you do is play in the batting cages, so if you like baseball you will like his side stories. with his part of the game they also introduced the best character in all of the franchise, koichi takasugi. i love that guy, he made me laugh a couple of times. after you're done with everyone's story, the game throws you back in kamurocho finally! for the final chapter, and man do i love kamurocho, i wish the game would just let you play there from the start instead of having you go on this wild goose chase collecting members. so besides the combat for each individual character, i feel like this game also suffered from the same thing that yakuza 3 suffered where enemies would just constantly block all the time, blockuza was very apparent and alive in this entry. normal enemies wouldn't block as often but it still happened enough for me to notice and boss fights... they all just blocked almost review_text:
On first impressions it feels like someone sat down and said "what makes games fun? Well, we'll have absolutely none of that 'fun' nonsense in it" !

The tutorial didn't really explain anything useful about bullet drop and wind effects. The tutorial, if you wish to do it, should walk you through *in great detail* about everything. I still don't understand the dotted line thing, exactly what the Q/E modifications to your scope do, how to get the little soldier guy on the scope to line up relating to distance. I want to learn but the game didn't help me enough.

Then, onto the first mission. Oh what fun as literally seconds into the mission I try to grab the rope. Over and over I try to grab the rope. Restart and it takes me through a load of inescapable chatter with my mission handler again. Finally I realise I need to grab the ledge. Ok .. onwards.

Then the next part I sneak up and kill a guy with a knife. Fair enough, did that bit.

Next up, I'm supposed to throw a stone to distract some enemies. Very vague idea of where the stone is going to go. Throw it anyhow, one guy has a bit of a look, other two don't move. Tried another stone somewhere else, about the same result. A couple more with no luck and I get shot.

That'll do me for now, I'll come back another day and try with some more patience. Oh wait, how do I quit the game? They even managed to make quitting the game a chore! I mean, come on, ESC ESC ESC should get you out back to the main menu on every game on earth! Not here it doesn't, seems to be "F" in the game (of course!).

I really hesitate to give a thumbs down to games. It's just pretty poorly thought out, not *awful* and a patch or two could no doubt help things along. If the devs read this, one thing to take away is make the tutorial mission more explanatory. Thanks!

review_text:
Pretty decent game!

The graphics and visuals are super detailed and pretty, especially if you like body horror and gore. The environments in the game create an absolutely stunning atmosphere that makes you feel unsafe and on your toes at all times. The sound design is also great, especially with a good pair of headphones on.

However, the story is kind of weak, with no notes or dialogue that explain what is going on. The story leaves everything up to your own understanding and fantasy. The game is pretty short, and I wish that the developers would have taken more time to include at least some kind of backstory. I also wish the game had more endings instead of the depressing ending that makes you feel like, "Huh, was that it?"

The combat absolutely sucks and is slow and sluggish. The weapons are weak, and ammo is scarce. The enemies have literal aimbot and almost always hit you, making you die a lot, which can be brutal, especially because the run back can be kind of long, tedious, and annoying.

I give the game a good 6/10 because I really, really like the theme, design, and atmosphere the game offers, which really saves the game from falling below average. It’s kind of a bummer because I feel like it has so much potential to be great had the story been more fleshed out and explained better, along with a complete combat overhaul.

If you have 7 hours to burn, this game is pretty good, but 40€ is way too high of a price for a game like this. I’d say get it on sale for something like 20€/25€ and sit down with a movie-like game that’s got super pretty visuals!

review_text:
✅ Positive Features :

1-The game offers a strong focus on authentic sniper experiences, including bullet drop, wind direction, breathing control, and distance calculation. It’s satisfying for fans of precision shooting.
2-Each mission takes place in a semi-open world map, allowing players to approach objectives from multiple angles. You can plan your route, use vantage points, and choose your method—stealth or aggression.
3-Missions have optional challenges, collectibles, encouraging players to replay contracts and improve their performance.
4-The AR Mask high-tech helmet with augmented reality features, helping the player gather intelligence and navigate the environment more effectively . like Enemy Detection , Object Scanning , Tagging System , Environmental Analysis & Displays information like bullet trajectory predictions, distances to targets, and wind direction when sniping (when upgraded).
5-The game includes various high-tech tools and gadgets, like drone, remotely-controlled snipe turret , Decoy Trap , Warning Device , grenades and mines
6-the Interrogate System allows players to gather valuable information from enemy soldiers during missions
7-The Bounty System optional high-value targets that players can eliminate for bonus rewards.
8-Completing contracts earns money and tokens that can be used to unlock new weapons, customize gear, and upgrade your character’s abilities.


❌ Negative Features :

1-Weak and Uninspired Story
2-Enemy AI sometimes overly alert and other times completely unaware.
3-The stealth system is serviceable but not as refined or flexible as in other stealth-based games like Hitman or Metal Gear Solid.
4-useless tools like C4 & Mines
5-Many contracts follow similar patterns, reducing variety
6-Multiplayer is currently disabled and cannot be accessed or reactivated.


Differences Between SGWC1 and Earlier games in the Series:

1-Gameplay :
SGWC1 uses a mission-based structure with semi-open sandbox maps. Each mission (called a "contract") is set in a separate, detailed area.
Earlier games (like Sniper Ghost Warrior 3) featured a fully open world, but were criticized for being too empty or buggy.

2-Stealth and Strategy:
SGWC1 focuses more heavily on stealth, careful planning, and tactical decision-making.
Previous titles were more linear or tried to mix open-world elements with traditional shooter gameplay.

3-Customization and Tools:
SGWC1 introduced more customizable gear like masks with special abilities, drones, and advanced gadgets.
Earlier games had more limited equipment and fewer strategic tools.

4-Map Design:
The levels in SGWC1 are dense, replayable, and encourage exploration.
Earlier entries often had more linear paths or less detailed open worlds.

review_text:
Overall, my experience with this game was very positive. The first story I chose to begin with was the "Trapmaker" series at it appeared to be captivating and interesting based off of the description of the first EP as well as the visual art covers for the 3 separate acts. As expected, it did not let me down and had me on a wild journey that had me glued to the edge of my seat with each puzzle I solved in order to progress the story along. It was a creative take on the who-done-it genera in EP 1. Following that act, it was a complex chase after trapmaker in acts 2 and 3. Many of the puzzles in this story was exciting and thrilling to solve, being very reminiscent of Jigsaw and the "Saw" franchise. The light sprinkles of humor, mixed with the right music in the background made these puzzles very interactive and captivating through and through. The same can be said for the other story I played. The pirate themed story had a great premise and did not rely too heavily on the movie cliches. This story felt like a great mix of various elements from the "Indian of Jones" series and "Pirates of the Caribbean" into one package. This story was not long, but also not too short. The music fit the story very well and helped to further immerse into this world of pirates and scallywags.

Despite this, there are a few huge critiques that makes me feel like this game format was also aimed to copy games that was more focused on revenue instead of overall satisfaction and enjoyment. What I am referring to is the difficulty of many of the puzzles both in the "Trapmaker" and "Pirate Cove" stories. Various of the puzzles from both stories is too complex for someone to just figure out without hints or help. You are given in-game currency to help when you need, but when you run out of this currency you must buy more. This also is the same for unlocking EPs in the game. You have a max of 3 keys over a very long time. Each key to unlock an EP is set at a timer of 2 hours, which in my opinion is way too long of a wait, unless they were thinking that is how long it would take to solve and complete each EP. Although I get the incentive for there being some form of payment in a free-to-play puzzle game, these types of forced payments makes it very difficult to completely defend the enjoyability of the game. I really do enjoy the conepts and stories they went for, but this form of money making is very frustrating. I will give them props for not being as overlydependant as current free-to-play games on mobile devices, but still is quite annoying.

Taken as a whole, I still would recommend play this game if you want to challenge yourself, and have quite a lot of time to spare inbetween life. If I were to give stars to rate the game overall, I would give this game a 3/5 stars overall.
