review_text:
Not here to try and convince anybody that TGR isn't worth their time.. doubt with a Steam population as low as it has, barely anyone will even see this. Still, I left couple lengthier feedback posts on TGR discord for the devs past season, and wanted to see if Season 2 brings any welcome changes - not seeing any, so I'll lay down the truth here as well.

This should not have been an online requirement live service game. I think the devs thought this would be some big hit to take on bigger giants in the market, and instead it just dwindles in its very low playerbase, making the online part of the game (one that earns all the fancy cosmetics) a real chore - long and ridiculously unfair matchmaking (whilst not even filling up most spots in a match) ; brutally grindy season track (exponential curve, so first 10 levels is like one last) ; and a lot of cores and every single cosmetic tied to online progression only, so if you want to have fun by yourself trying to do better on some tracks solo (whilst looking fly), then be willing to invest a bunch of time into playing with others just to get bombarded by missles every 5 seconds, trying to finish some dumb daily missions like a good little sucker. 

Can't just have a fun game, no no no - got to have that seasonal track and daily logins, to keep the player retention like every other BS live service game, right?!

First season took me approx 50 hours to finish, and I had a winrate of over 50% over 327 matches (games should fill up with 8 players, but most of the matches it was me vs 1-5 other players, making 6-8 player lobbies very rare, and I did try both NA/EU servers at all kinds of different times.. after a few weeks into the season the waiting time (matchmaking > loading players/levels > flyby cam > potg) takes up as much time as actually going through the 3 maps in one match, so by that conclusion a single season will waste tens of hours of your time, just by mindlessly waiting around.

As mentioned, the player count is kind of low (not screaming the game is dying.. but expect some queue times go upwards of 2-5 minutes further into the season). Steamdb shows around ~20 people playing (it was around 60-100 when the first season launched), so most of the players come from this game being a freebie on Game Pass, so if that contract ever ends (which they usually eventually do), expect the player count to totally plummet. To make things worse, there are 6-7 regions to play in (good for latency, but terrible for a very low population in online games, forcing segregation).

Also this game is centered around online-only, so if TGR crew doesn't have a end-of-life plan for this game, it can just shut down over the next year or so with the usual "oh well we tried, but we're so glad to have people come along on this journey (but this aint profitable for us anymore so we're shutting down)" type of bs as usual. I hope I'm very wrong about this, but TGR does not have any client-saves, nor can this be played in offline mode, even if you're just interested in solo-ing some tracks for better times or to have simple casual fun. And to top it all off, this will be another one of those infinitely in Early Access type of games, to justify whatever is wrong with it - and all the diehard fans can always make excuses "oh well its still beta" or "oh, this is planned to be implemented sometime / soon / who knows" like any of it matters if the game is already in full motion with selling itself and pumping out seasons.

To touch on cosmetics, this game goes hard on exclusivity, so hey.. if you didn't play in Beta / Season 1 / Season X, then feel ready to see others with stuff you'll never own, because clearly you're not worthy to be with the cool crowd. As far as other games doing seasonal track better, Minecraft Dungeons has a way to let people progress whatever season pass they choose for those rewards, but I guess 'fear of missing out' is better to keep people active from season to season. 

Also the store, for no good reason at all, rotates out items daily (and some smaller stuff every 6 hours).. So, why does that matter? Again, purely for suckering people into logging in daily, so if you're after an item to come back into rotation that you weren't able to afford (or missed out) when it was last in, be ready to log in daily for 2-3 months with your fingers crossed (quite literally that was the time for something I wanted in Season 1 to come back) - all of the cosmetics governed by 'you playing vs others' (something that this game doesn't even feel to mention on its store page).. if you buy the game, you get no cosmetics apart from one base car. More stuff added in these little rotations also mean less likelyhood of you ever seeing them again.

Still no cosmetic presets either, and there's already a decent amount of items in the game that this should have been long implemented (should've simply done one loadout for each car body), but its not like anybody plays this game for the cosmetics anyway, right? RIGHT?!

There are a bunch of other smaller issues as well, but I doubt the devs decided to consider my feedback on their discord (which is actually nicely done for this game), and I doubt they will consider anything mentioned here either. I don't hate the game, but I do despise the GaaS model they decided to tie this game onto and then sink it. It plays fine and was fun at first, but personally I'd suggest investing your time into Rocket League instead, if hitting balls with cars is your thing - as terrible and toxic as that game can be, at least you can still get better at it after playing over 10 hours, and it will probably be around in the coming years - something I can't see TGR have a future for (and I do hope I'm wrong).

Sadly, if/once I'll be back to complete S2, I won't care for player competition in it, and will just have to idle-macro my PC for those cosmetic rewards for 3-4 days straight, whilst I play some other game that is fun and values my time. 

Everything I mentioned here, can be fixed, even if not entirely, then surely for much better, hence the negative review until they do.

review_text: I got the game to run at above 40 FPS with frame gen on. Playing about an hour I decided to refund the game. This is not a Dead Space clone, this is a horror game that tries to sell itself as such; but ratchets up the difficulty so much it is better to run than fight anything. The combat is just clunky, you move slow, there is no parry or dodge, and your main attack requires you to charge your gun up to do any damage. Enemies barely flinch, so they keep coming at you with ranged melee attacks and take several charge shots to kill. Resources are very scarce and your inventory is super tiny (6 slots!) while needing to collect crafting resources, hold ammo, healing items, and keys to doors. The devs have said they want the game to be hard. This game is hard alright, but in the most clunky, unfair, and tedious ways. Dead Space and Resident Evil can be difficult, but they at least had a better balance and design than Chronos. My rating = 5/10 Only play if you like super hard horror games and can deal with clunky, slow controls.

review_text:
Updated review at the bottom:

This will be a fairly honest and direct review.

The game is very good in concept and very poor in execution.  I have a pretty heavy machine and I get constant FPS drops for no apparent reason while my machine is not even at 25% load on processor, RAM, and graphics card.  And when I say FPS drops, I mean like 5 FPS and my inputs don't work at all.  Like, I can move with WASD, but no matter how often I push fire, I don't fire.  If I pull out my grenade, I keep it in my hand and don't throw it.  It's like any kind of fire button is disabled during frame stuttering.  Like, Valve should probably pull this off Steam until the devs actually make the game playable.  At this point, it is probably stealing and could feasibly be argued in court.

I picked up this game in early access and it was really solid.  It was an easy "shut your brain off" PvE game and those roots are still secure in foundation.  You get standard classes with a role that nobody actually uses the class for at all (medics not reviving, assaulters staying on defense, engineers not doing any engineering at all).  Somehow you can still usually win on normal this way, but you can still lose as well.

The weapons need heavy revisions because they don't do their intended job well, but it's still a bit charming with how unbalanced it is (and not in your favor).  The classes all have their own unique skills, perks, and equipment.  The Demolisher, for instance, can become a suicide bomber with a fully automatic shotgun and a melee attack that shatters dead bugs, and an arm one of those football people would envy.  The engineer can build stuff like turrets outside of base.  The assaulter can get a little boost towards the opponent and lay new spawn points for the team.  That kind of stuff.

Every time they release an update, the game gets worse.  Not in concept, but technically.  More bugs are introduced, others aren't fixed, the optimization gets worse (somehow).  Nobody seems to have an answer as to why and the development team seemingly has chosen to just not acknowledge the problem, let alone fix it.  Been a while since I could even complete a single mission.

Speaking of this.  The game crashes all the time.  I realize this is a problem with UE5 in general, but I can't make it through missions anymore it seems.  Crash to desktop and once it caused an entire BSOD on crash.  And in the rare case your game doesn't crash, the server you're playing on does.  

There are other flaws with game play, but most of those are what I would consider part of the game's charm.  Like occasionally just running hundreds more at you than it should even though your map has no mutations or anything.  Or accidentally spawning in like 10 tigers at once for you to mow down.  Or overwhelming you so much you can't leave the starting area.

But the technical "achievements" of this game seem more like proof of concept than even a beta, let alone official release.  If you buy this I would consider setting an alarm at one and a half hours before considering to refund it.  I really hope they fix it because it has immense potential and console players don't seem to have nearly as many issues.  But right now, for PC, I would genuinely consider skipping this one until optimization issues have been fixed.  But I could easily see them abandoning PC all together and only focusing on console with how much console players seem to like it.

-------

Update: Game has massively improved in stability and updates since my review.  I can not recommend the game to anyone who wants a near-mindless bug killing experience.  Most of my negative experience for the last several months has been because of players, not the developers.  They'll just choose a support class like medic or engineer and then just never do the job for that class.  I suspect some people choose medic for the auto-revive - but that medic just sucks at outputting damage so they're a waste of resources.  They don't revive anyone, they don't really contribute.  That just exist and are a burden on everyone.  And since nobody chooses that class if there are three medics, it's fairly common to just have three medics who absolutely refuse to be a medic for some reason.

If you like to shut your brain off and slaughter bugs, you'll enjoy this so long as they don't create more problems with the game.

review_text:
I love turn-based strategy, so when I saw this title on Steam, I thought: "Hey, this looks neat! I'll give it a shot!" 

Well... it's basically the PC equivalent of a Facebook or Android game. Normally I'm forgiving of certain quirks if the game came from a different platform, but the one thing I can't get past is the fact it has micro-transactions. Not just a few, but a LOT of them and it badgers you to purchase them. 

Now, I don't doubt this game is playable without ever paying a cent, but it seems like that would require a huge grind. 

The problem is you need special items to increase the speed of building, healing or doing whatever with your troops and buildings. You can decide to forgo that, but you'll have to wait in real-time. So if something takes five minutes, it's five minutes off your real day. 

Five minutes wouldn't be so bad if that was the extent of it, but the more advanced options can take hours or days. So unless you pay, the game's essentially stalled. 

It's not a terrible game and I've certainly played worse. Even so, that's hardly a ringing endorsement. 

That said, it's free, so if you don't believe me or think I'm full of crap, try it yourself. Maybe you'll love it, and if you do, that's great. However, I have a feeling most PC gamers won't spend a whole lot of time with this game.

review_text:
I typed up a long review covering my various criticisms and annoyances cause by JC4 but steam helpfully deleted it before I could post it after I clicked away to check my hours in JC3.

In short. It's not just "JC3 but slightly worse and only like $5 on sale, so still worth playing" which is what I thought going into it. It's annoying and frustrating in ways that JC3 just wasn't and overall feels like a massive step backwards. 

The combat gets samey quickly, you can't so much as fire off a shot without having an infinite and oppressive army sent for you which gets old quickly. They've added so many bells and whistles that it becomes annoying to navigate and everything seems to not work as well as it did in 3 (please get rid of these stupid balloons and grapple thrusters and just give me back my old grapple and booster system). I appreciate the jet powered wing suit isn't locked behind DLC but it's a less manoeuvrable shell of its former self. I also appreciate the rebel drop system not having the same degree of annoying cool down + beacons (before you max out everything) but other than that it's just a downgrade from 3. While the map is cool, and feels like they fully filled it out vs leaving the top 1/3rd more or less unfinished like in JC3, the whole game looks on par if not worse than the previous one, especially the characters weird beard hair which kinda looks like they wiped a hedgehog across their face rather than facial hair.

Overall, definitely feels like after putting their A team on JC3, they passed their golden goose over to the B team, possibly even C team based on the lack of play testing the devs obviously did.

If you haven't played JC3, go play it + the DLC instead. If you have played JC3 and just want more, give it a hard think and only buy it if it's on sale.

Just a phenomenal game and a reminder of the great games Western game devs used to make. Graphics still hold up very well. Playing at 4K and you'd think it came out more recently. It's more open ended than Arkham Asylum, but it still has a lot of the great more closed environments with stealth moments and exploration as well. Music and voice acting is great, and the story has a lot going on to keep you interested in it and the game world. Combat is just right, not too hard and not too easy, and it's fun to rack up combos and mix it up as you go. It's also a pretty long game on a blind play, and it's fun to replay and collect everything. Huge amount of value on sale.

The only cons if any is the cutscenes actually look worse than the game itself and then also the controls are a bit wonky and take some getting used to at first. 

Overall, even in 2025, this is still a fantastic game and must play for Batman or action/adventure game fans. You simply can't go wrong.

I think that the price drop was a last ditch effort due to the dwindling community. Not really any reason to play anymore. Would not recommend, even at the lower price. I myself am a big starship troopers fan, but this is... Not what it use to be.

review_text:
I honestly can not recommend this game to fans of the series, RPGs, and or MMOs enjoyers.  A little backstory first so everyone is on the same page, when this game was first released to the Western audience in the US, EU, etc. Back in 2020 on the Xbox One/Series the game was phenomenal, PC players through the Microsoft store and later Steam were introduced later that year. The game had some stability problems but it was quickly resolved. Xbox players and PC players enjoyed each cooperation through the content of this game. And in some cases, we were very competitive with one another.  The game had so much stuff packed into it. We had an amazing story with fleshed-out characters, the game was divided into six chapters, and through the chapters you see introductions of new characters or old characters with a good backstory yet some tragic, and some goofy it was an enjoyable experience. 

We had a large variety of unique events some crazy. We had hunting parties, boss rushes, dance-offs, Persona 3 and 5 dance-offs. Elizabeth can't dance to save her life. We had some unique ones where we got to ride in gundam like robots to fight a massive Japanese Navy, ride futuristic bikes at mark speed to do drivebys and run over a global celebrity on the moon. My favorite is beating up the God of marijuana who lives in Las Vegas and blows up part of the moon.  Do you see what I mean by variety and crazy? The gear that we can obtain from events, special feats a player would do, or even super rare drops had unique features to them.  So no matter what update or new best gear that came out you always had other options, sometimes even more fun than the best gear for that particular update or even better in some cases. Basically, you had a lot of options as a player.

We had premium membership that was a feature you spend real money with. It can last for 30 days, 60 days, or 90 days prices change on which pack you're getting of course.  As a premium member, you would log on and get daily gifts, then you would have a special monthly daily reward which gives you some quality life items like a high-quality fishing rod, pickaxe, some boosters etc, every day was a different item.  Then when it came to the player's living quarters it would drastically improve, so instead of having a five item limit you can have a full apartment complex and go wild and crazy with your apartment. I've seen some premium complexes that have a full summer resort,  a Gothic vibe, Japanese theme hotel service, one player I've seen had an actual Baseball stadium with a Go Go dance Cage. Premium players were able to use the auction to buy and sell items and gear.  You could even get 3-day shop passes super easily by trading in FUN points which were easily acquired by playing the game, doing small tasks, or reviving a dead player.

The game was not perfect, it had some flaws in it, and the biggest complaints were. The graphics looked bad like PlayStation 2 or PlayStation 3. Content was being pushed out at a rapid pace, and improving equipment was super tedious and felt like you needed a college degree just to min max (This means having the best possible outcome for your equipment) The worst you would see in the community was jerk elitist alliance, a drive-by disagreement, or some random player undercutting you in the auction. That was basically it, to be honest. 

The backstory is over. When the New Genesis update was released in June 2021. This game was went from hype to a complete storm of trash. Let me explain the changes.  With New Genesis players were allowed to keep all their outfits and cosmetics they had from PSO2 along with their weapons even though through the transition they became incredibly weak.  Players are now able to change their gender and race at will using a salon ticket, this couldn't be done before, you would have to make a new character if you wanted X race and X gender.  Now you can be whatever you want.  They completely removed anyway for players to obtain free 3 day shop passes,  Trading can not be done on NGS with or without Premium,  Premium didn't have any player quaters/home until to 2023 June update. So no effect on player homes since there was none back there and the items that players received from dailies were useless. There was lag, disconnections,  and server drops for months.

The community was bombarded with AC scratch banners ( Use real money to gamble to win a chance of an item 11 tries for $22)  There was always AC scratch banners in the previous game. They had a good selection of male outfits, female outfits and Casts (Robots/Androids) parts. Since New Genesis release this game been super heavily focused on female outfits and accessories. They also added in stupid stuff like eyebrows, nose hair,  and barely noticeable makeups in those packs. So now players rolling on these AC scratch banners can end up getting eyebrows and stuff and yes they have the highest chance of appearing often. We was getting like 4 AC scratches per week and fans that played this game with NGS released was hit with the survey no one can forget.  

SURVEY QUESTIONS : Did you buy AC? If so How much? If not? WHY NOT!? BUY AC. What is your reason for not buying AC? Are you going to buy AC? Have you previously purchased AC before NGS? Do you know how to purchase AC?  Is the instructions  to purchase AC not clear or easy to understand?(I can't make this up)

The story bad, The characters are just very boring and bland, the music is great, the character customization is the strongest feature in this game. I don't believe there is a game that can top PSO2 NGS in character customization. The combat been very stale since it came out. Instead of getting some good quality content like we received in the past everything comes at a snail's pace which players call drip content. So we see big updates every six months to give you a  clear idea.  The events in this game is the worst offender and it pisses me off. How on earth do you have a copy and paste event since 2021 release to current? Every single event is all about points, same type of shop items, rinse and repeat.

The weapon variety took a nose dive through the ground into underground subways. We basically only have best gear and event gear. The Best gear drop rate is so bad, you are better off not wasting your time hunting, farming, searching for them. Get a second job or do something else with your time. Its been proven if a X content creator/'s complain they would see a drop. Fishy isn't it?  It happened a few times over the years.  In New Genesis I will admit they made gear improvement mechanics much easier than the previous game.  Its very straightforward and easy to understand and do. 

Community wise in NGS there is a complete divide. You have one side who are fed up with the game and make complaints that they want to see the game become better.   But any improvements come at a snail's pace I'm talking between 6 months to 2 years wait. And most of the improvements takes around  9 months+ With that in mind some people leave the game to pursue other things.  The other side just go on about there daily activities in NGS, either it grinding, socializing, making X rated content with one another (Yeah some players get down like that) 

Not really a lot of good things to say about NGS. It just sucks and I wish it was better. They removed a lot of features to make it more pay to win than anything else.  Sometimes I wonder who were the target audience for this game? It can't be the fans cause tons of them refuse to play this game since its so bad in many ways.  I haven't even gotten started with the playerbase being so sensitive if you hurt their feelings you can get your account banned. It happened a lot on ship 1 and ship 2 from 2021- to late 2022. So in this game you have to be careful who you talk to and if you decide to talk out loud in public about topics.  To be honest, there is way too much drama, I mean like highschool drama in this game.

review_text:
AVOID THIS GAME LIKE THE PLAGUE if you're not someone going for a nostalgia trip of a god awful piece of shovelware that you were young enough to enjoy.

I've bought this game for 75% off and still feel i got ripped off harder than someone buying Fallout 76 full price.

This game is so terrible in every single aspect that it's in a "shelf" named S h * t in my library. 

The good: none whatsoever. 

The bad: 
- The story, even 1 hour in is so awful, with so many plot holes and complete idiot plot that it makes Sword Art Online look like a masterpiece.
- The world is completely disconnected to what a MMORPG should look and feel like to the point where you think the makers have never played one even though it came out during the golden age of MMORPG.
- The dialogue and script is straight up sewer buckets. The characters talk like 10 year olds who role play, the timing between lines in the english dub is mind numbingly bad. The lines themselves have errors and are at best high school dissertation paper level of depth.
- The gameplay is almost non-existant, hidden between tons of cringy cutscenes and text reading (such as emails and forum posts (yes it's as bad as it sounds)), yet they still managed to f*** the combat up and make it the most boring trash I've ever seen from a JRPG and also the most boring part of this game. 
- The controls are cancerous even with a controller. It's so badly done it feels incredibly unresponsive during combat (looking at you skill button), and moving to the sides also brings the camera angle with it, with no setting to turn that off (shoutouts to the Mario cam in Mario 64) You can't even jump or dodge or anything fun.
- The maps/areas/dungeons are just massive empty spaces with the same 8 types of enemies throughout the whole world. The map layout is the laziest garbage you find in mobile games with just super long corridors with strings of rooms in a straight line with no puzzle or even jumping or anything that could be fun.
- The game has a big history of crashing, which I didn't get (yet) because it seems I haven't reached the chapter where it allegedly starts doing so, but I still got massive frame drops for no reason whatsoever as I have a high end PC. 
- The characters and cinematography are all out from the imagination of a 10 year old who thinks doing a motion blur close up of a new character should be enough to convince players that they're badass. The characters do some of the dumbest looking movements for no reason whatsoever to "look cool" yet they only look extremely foolish. No character in this game seems to have anywhere close to an average IQ.

There is no semblance of realism or of any in-universe consistency. 

This is the first game where I will say that the best thing about it is its voice acting (if we ignore the original JP VAs because they're always higher quality than english), not because they were good, they almost never are for anime-related stuff, but because the rest is just that much worse.

Some people might say that this game is old so I shouldn't be so harsh, well there are tons of EVEN OLDER games that did literally everything better than this piece of garbage. 

I cannot understand how anyone would enjoy this game without being single digit age, or so blinded by their nostalgia that they're able to not be affected by the thousands of completely stupid plot holes and story defects and by the complete trash gameplay and world.

If you think you want to play this game even after all of that, then please watch a let's play of the first couple hours of gameplay AND make sure you try the game before your 2 weeks from purchase of refund trial time are up. If you still think you'll enjoy the game, then I wish you the best of fun!

This game is now in my top 1 of worst game I've ever bought for over $10 on Steam. 

Even if you could get it for free I would still recommend never adding it to your library.

1/10

review_text:
I'm not going to preface this with how long I've been a fan. The fact of the matter is SEGA has been sabotaging this game for years. Every launch of this game has been severely botched. Deleted or missing files, unstable servers, limited activities, random ban waves with very little transparency. It's been nonstop.

Now in 2023, when the game should be in a much better place in terms of content and player experience, we seem to be at an all time low. Recycled enemies and quest types, severe gear bottle-necking with no content to justify the effort, no direction for story or future updates. This latest major update that was touted as the evolution of the game ended up being an empty promise.

The new Creative Space feature didn't disappoint, it delivered in ways many players weren't expecting when you consider how poorly they've handled combat and gear progression. However, it seems as though SEGA was expecting this to take the place of all other content. Rather than postpone the update so that it would include combat based content, they pushed through with it and we're left with another empty promise for August. The reality is this new update will not meet the expectations of the player base.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone. Many of the friends that I've made in the few thousand hours I've spent in this virtual space have left because they've gotten tired of waiting for what comes next as every new update just delivers either more of the same or disappointment.

SEGA refuses to learn anything from each update they push. They refuse to course correct. Hundreds of complaints about poorly implemented features will be presented to them with solutions included. If they fix the issue in one update, the following one will include the same mistake. (Impossibly low drop rates. content specific upgrades, quests with drops that don't reflect the effort involved etc.) They run on an outdated business model and are unwilling to adapt with the times.

PSO2 NGS could be the best anime MMO on the market. There's plenty of potential here, but success isn't measured in what ifs. review_text:
What a fall for a studio that has been truly brilliant until now. The basic concept of the game is good and has some really appealing ideas, nothing less is expected from Stress Level Zero after all... but the execution... this time it didn't cut it for me.

The storytelling is quite disjointed, and although I didn't get very far into the main story, I had a constant sense of emptiness that would have been ignorable if it weren't for the technical aspects of the game (spoiler alert): it switches from moments of "rail-shooting" (literally sitting in a mining cart shooting fixed targets like an amusement park), to first-person go-kart tracks with a steering wheel that is so sensitive that it gave me motion sickness even though I am extremely used to VR, don't suffer from motion sickness, and have played numerous VR simulators of various types, including flight sims), to what was really the last straw for me: some sequences where you change "avatars" and find yourself in bodies that have proportions different from the human body, particularly in the length of the limbs, which makes even interacting with simple objects extremely strange, not to mention sheathing weapons and objects, which is already more complicated than in many other titles due to how the object anchor points have been calibrated.

I also found the movement and parkour much more "awkward", and I don't particularly like the fact that essentially every "level" is a timed course that is supposed to encourage you to climb the leaderboards.

I'm sorry but this time it didn't work for me, there are now much better titles out there and if you really want to do something in VR, I'll tell you: replay BoneWorks or jump into IntoTheRadius, personally I feel that depending on what you're looking for, you'll benefit in both cases.

I'll be keeping an eye out for any future updates

review_text:
[h1]Soulless low effort cashgrab made without love[/h1]

I have to put this out. This is probably the worst game i've played this year. It's supposed to be a Dead Space successor but it fails in every area possile.

You end up in a space prison and then chaos erupts, genetically engineered monsters swarm the prison and you must escape it. Usual story which was done so many times by Resident Evil but better.

So what's the gameplay? It's tedious hell. The main character is so slow that he can barely move. The game consists of corridors and mazes. That's the “level design”. And there's no map, no UI for some reason so you don't even know where to go, which maze path is the main one or optional.
Do you like crawl and squeeze through walls every 5 minutes? Then this is the game for you. You walk a bit, the crawl, then fight couple of zombies, then squeeze through walls, run until next gap in the wall, squeeze through then climb into the vent to crawl. That's the gameplay.
Oh wait that's not it. Running is so slow that it feels like you're in slow motion. And you can't run all the time, most of the time the game only lets you to slowly walk. There are some spots on the ground where you start running for 2 seconds and then back to walking. Buggy mess.
Combat is an absolute joke. This extremely slow character swings his bat to kill the zombies. You have to dodge their attacks by holding the stick left or right. So dodge, dodge hit, rinse repeat million times.
You have weapons but very limited ammo and it need more ammo than melee hits. Makes no sense.
Inventory space is so limited that you will always struggle to have ammo, healing items or items to sell to make money. Sop for the entirety of the game you must choose between HP, money or ammo. You can't have them all.
Switching weapons is a pain. You must press right, then up or down and then A to confirm. In the heat of the fight it's impossible to do quickly because for some reason each button press is extremely slow and takes around 1s to react.
You can't dodge ranged attacks or jump which makes the last boss a real pain. Worst boss design ever. A pain, tedious, annoying fight where the Resident Evil copy pasta last boss is quick and has an insane reach, shoots at you and send minions after you which explode and damage you when you can barely move and must use both hands to switch weapons which takes 5 seconds because you can't stand still or you die.
Bugs? Oh yea. Running ability just disappears randomly, when you pick up an item sometimes you start crouching which is “really helpful” when you're in combat. Switching weapons doesn't always work, sometimes game doesn't react to your inputs if you press the buttons too fast. You MUST wait for a second or so for them to register. Basically stand still to switch weapons.
You think when you get the suit you'll take less damage? Nope. You start taking more damage with armor. Who even designed this mess?

Horror? The only horror this game offers is tedious and clunky controls, crawling, squeezing and walking without any UI or waypoints.

Graphics are decent, game runs great without issues and loading times are almost non-existent. Also native ultrawide support. At least something is good.

Sound is messed up. Sound scares play way before the enemies appear or jump you so you hear the sound scare and see nothing and after 5 seconds you see zombies coming at you.

Overall a terrible game where every gameplay aspect is tedious and clunky, boring repetitive combat which doesn't evolve for the entirety of the game, crawling simulator. Which tried to copy Dead Space and a bit of Resident Evil, has no soul and zero creativity. Avoid.

[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Looks pretty good
[*]Ultrawide support and good performance
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]Buggy mess
[*]Has no soul and just copies other games
[*]Level design is no level design
[*]Clunky, unresponsive controls
[*]More walking, crawling and squeezing than actual gameplay
[*]Boring repetitive combat
[*]Story for the sake of story
[*]No UI
[/list]

I found myself thinking back about the time I spent on this game alone, my account here on Steam says I have roughly 2.6k hours, but I've played this game on the JP servers starting 2016, then moved to global on the XBOX and finally on PC in the last couple of years, so collectively I have around 8k hours or so.

I can confidently say that, despite all it's flaws (That will eventually come up as you run out of story and things to do except endless grinding) this is a really enjoyable experience overall, and really one of the only few games like this that allow you full freedom to customize your character however you like, and that is one of the best things this game has to offer.

Otherwise, the game is populated enough where you can play without any issues, but for completely F2P players, it is a slight challenge to buy fashion items off the market, as a decent hairstyle can go for up to 20m+ in-game currency, so usually a single item is enough to drain all your savings. But instead if you're the kind of person that has plenty of money to toss at SEGA, you won't have any issues looking fashionable. Although it is probably better not to play this game around your family, as a good chunk of the players likes to use that freedom of the character creation to make pretty NSFW stuff, hahaha.

In conclusion, I've met some of the most wonderful people here over the years that have changed my life for the better, that I wouldn't have found otherwise if I didn't play NGS, so give it a shot and see if you can come out of it with something nice.

TL:DR: Instance based "MMO" with decent gameplay, can go back to the 2012 version of it if you download the data for it, lots of story and good characters to entertain you enough, for free.

review_text:
TLDR: Witchfire is a very good game. Its well optimized. Feels great to play. And has a fair bit of content in it for early access. The price is a bit high (I'm not mr. moneybags, I shudder when buying anything above 10 bucks) but it's definitely worth it if you're willing to grind levels. That doesn't make it exempt from any criticisms of which I have quite a few. But overall the game is pretty worth it as is.

I have played through witchfire to it's entirety. Gotten all the achievements and conquered the current witch mountain. I am only missing a handful of items in witch mountain because the progression kind of falls off the rails in there. I've done all of the timed dungeons at least once and killed every boss. My character as it stands is level 75. My criticisms mainly revolve around pacing and leveling which are the two biggest offenders that I can think of. Nonetheless, these criticisms clearly aren't dealbreakers for me as you could probably tell from my completion status.

On the topic of pacing. The Gnosis levels are a topic that I'd like to address. Once you hit around Gnosis 3-4. There's no new content in the form of weapons, spells, relics etc. The weapons system in this game hit struck such a chord within me that I was practically salivating at the thought of leveling up. I wanted to explore more and see what secrets the mirror was hiding. Only to realize the harsh truth that this game metaphorically blows its load with weapons too soon. There's no shortage of guns in this game. But you will have about 85% of them by Gnosis 3 with the rest being unlocked from miscellaneous things and exploration, not research anymore. There are 6 total Gnosis levels. My enthusiasm for leveling Gnosis quickly waned as the rewards became a very slow trickle. Only a small boost in witchfire earned along with new 'secrets'. Leveling up to 5 and 6 only lets you open a single odd door or two and nets you access to witch mountain. I don't consider those concrete rewards. Not in the slightest. The rewards for the lower levels of Gnosis are staggering compared to the higher levels and open the game up a lot more.

Next, on the topic of leveling. I have some gripes with how fast levels come. To begin, lets talk about witchfire. The leveling currency like souls would be in the dark souls franchise. Of course, when leveling. The amount of witchfire you need per level increases ever so slightly. The problem is not the increase in required witchfire to level up. The problem is acquiring witchfire. As mentioned before with Gnosis, you get small boosts in obtained witchfire as your Gnosis level increases. Each map you travel to also boosts its given witchfire with it's increasing difficulty level. Makes sense, harder content gives greater rewards. But as you play, you will notice that even if you clear out an entire map including killing it's boss at the very end. You will only have enough witchfire for a 1-2 levels maximum. I understand that there's a way to get millions of witchfire from a single run. Even the devs have championed these people showing "LOOK HE GOT 1 MILLION AT THE END OF A SINGLE RUN, THE LEVELING SYSTEM IS FINE." But that's simply not an accessible way to actually progress due to the huge drawbacks of using the items that give you more witchfire. Namely the foul stimulant item which heavily reduces your maximum health and stamina. At anything less than 40 flesh you will get 1-2 shotted. At anything less than 40 blood you will only have 1-2 dodges. To demand near perfection from players just to obtain levels in a reasonable amount of time is absurd. Especially when if you die after using the foul stimulant. You lose everything. This hardcore leveling system predominently benefits the already extremely strong player. The players who have enough to take the huge HP and Stamina hit and shrug it off. As well as nearly instantly clear any encounters they come across. That is where the millions of witchfire come from. if you don't believe me. The person who posted their million witchfire run claimed to already be around level 440-480. At that point, you don't need levels at all compared to players like me at not even level 100. But in order to comfortably grind I'm expected to do what they do? I expect anyone reading this to understand how absurd that is.

There are two aspects in this game. 

A) The game is exactly the first game all over again. It has all the merits AND THE ISSUES that plagued the first one, minus the bugs. This is a totally bug free experience, with the occasionally clipping. But the learning curve, the bad combat, the nonsensical hit detection, the calibration of combat, the auto-locking system, the way you must cheat your way to play and to prevail, is there. Mind you there are tons of more combat here, so what was just an inconvenience back then, becomes a real problem now. 

b) The game hates you. It throws you into the most ludicrous and outrageous senarios you can think of. Those who suffered the "tortured" debuff know what I mean. The game sets you up to FAIL every time you make a moral decision because "war is bad", but by the end you end up being a bad person just because you HATE EVERYONE. I know that it is a subversion of the "audentes fortuna iuvat" theme, but GOD BY THE END I WANTED TO DROP A NUCLEAR BOMB ON TOP OF KUTTENBERG.

Totally a hateable game. But it is universally praised so they won't mind my thumbs down.

review_text:
It is worth noting that all servers but one are inactive so if you hoped for an immersive experience with a variety of different servers with various play styles, this isnt the game.

The only good thing about this game is that it can be fun with friends, but quite literally any game can be.

The map design is lacking, with uneven and square terrain that appears rushed. Additionally, the excessive amount of hills makes navigation difficult and it is incredibly hard for newer players. 

The animations are janky and limbs seem to merge with one another, especially when you fall, the legs sprawl out.

The only active server follows a realism style of play which causes rule-breakers to join because it is the only server you can play on with others. If you have ever played 'The Cenozoic Era', this game is similar but with more animals and instead of the product being free, its overpriced.

In terms of quality, the early access price is not worth it. £5 would have been a fair price for the quality of this game in this stage. Roblox games are performing better than this.

review_text:
The first Samorost game is free, browser-based and available on the Amanita Design website - http://amanita-design.net/samorost-1/ - whether you enjoy this or not should be a reasonable (though not watertight) indicator of how you'll feel about 2.

In Samorost 2 you guide a space gnome on an adventure through various environments/scences, solving puzzles, all in hopes of rescuing his dog. And that's more-or-less all there is to it.

Samorost 2 is a short game and I have criticised other games for being too short/simplistic to be worth it.. but I can't bring myself to do that here. Everything about this game is just too damn charming to me. The artwork is gorgeous, the music is relaxing and I enjoy the quirky atmosphere, creatures and puzzles enough to justify it.

Another valid point, though, is that there's very little guidance - this will appeal to some and not to others. For the most part, I quite like working out what it is I have to do in a scene (even if that involves mousing over everything to find out what I can interact with first ;), but I appreciate that not everyone feels the same way - preferring a clear objective.

So while I do definitely recommend Samorost 2, it's worth keeping in mind that it's a short game with little direction in each scene, making it not worth it for some.

From memory, I first played World of Goo in early 2009. I remember because it was only slightly before the time I played Plants vs Zombies for like 40 hours in high school. Plants vs Zombies pretty much took my undivided attention for a while there, and World of Goo got kinda left by the wayside. About 9 years later I give it another chance and I just can't see whatever magic there undoubtedly was for an indie physics puzzle game all that time ago. I certainly don't hate World of Goo; it's got charm and quality for sure. But it's also not particularly compelling or awe inspiring. 

If you love casual games or physics puzzle games then I'm sure you won't find much wrong with World of Goo. Since Steam reviews are about whether you would "recommend" the game, and not if you can recognize that some people would love the game - it's unfortunately a no from me.

review_text:
I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Was it up to the level of the SH2 remake? No, but I feel like those a big shoes to fill in the survival horror space. There are things that this game does exceptionally well. The combat is very fun and engaging, the world design is immaculate and off putting, the sound design amplifies the horror elements of this game nicely, the item economy is tuned very well to where you feel the stress of your limited inventory but at the same time you dont get hard locked on a run from not having enough. I also liked the character designs the Travelers walk really reminds me of Judge Dred or Robocop walking down a hallway XD. With just those aspects alone I would give this game an 7/10.

If there is a weak point in this game is that the story is serviceable, but not all that memorable. It worked to make a nice spooky story, and I enjoyed it overall, but the big pivotal moments just felt *alright* they didnt leave me excited and reading fan theories and obsessing about what it all means. All of that being said I dont think you have to have a story like that for it to still be a fun game and I hope that Bloober team expands on what they made here.

Cronos: The New Dawn is a great survival horror game. This may be the single best game I have seen accomplish resource management flawlessly. You are always able to get by unless you miss too many times, but there always seems to be just enough ammo around the corner. The story is interesting, with intriguing audio logs and texts to read. Pros:
- Excellent resource management
- Fine tuned difficulty with good balance
- Great environments filled with a believable history in them
- Solid combat for a survival horror game 

Cons:
- The game should have some sort of dodge mechanic to move a little more suddenly
- The beginning is a bit slow
- The story starts off feeling a little generic

review_text:
Hakuoki: Kyoto Winds is a first part of the story, continuation is held within Edo Blossoms.

Wow, what a wild ride has it been. The story revolves around a girl named Chizuru Yukimura, who's headed to Kyoto in search of her father, but unfortunately (or not) she stumbled upon something she wasn't supposed to witness and it led her to being captured by the Shinsengumi for further questioning, which later allowed her to stay in their headquarters. With time she learns more about the Shinsengumi, their life as samurai and her own life details, which she wasn't previously aware of. I didn't know about the Shinsengumi before this game, so I was pleasantly surprised that this game has historical accuracy, it's always nice to learn about something new through games.

I can hardly consider this part of the game an otome title, as all romance is kept for the second part, Edo Blossoms, but it's a very enjoyable read anyway. You're presented with the ability to build up bonds with one out of 12 available men, so that's still something! 

- The story is awesome, even if it lacks the proper romance in this part.
- Historical setting sprinkled with a bit of fantasy.
- LOTS of different endings since you're presented with 12 men to pick from.
- All characters are very different and it's interesting to see how they open up once they get closer to you.
- Beautiful art.
- Soundtrack is really enjoyable.

Overall, I can say this is a great read, definitely worth a pick together with Edo Blossoms for the full experience.

review_text:
I'm likely going to revisit this review once I finish the game, however, it has been suggested that I split up the game because of how long it can be if you listen to all the voiced dialogue and go through every route, both of which I (intend to) do. So, here I am, 5 endings out of 30, and 55 hours with only two men romanced, though I wouldn't really call it romancing. Even put mildly, even considering the time period, this specific game (Kyoto Winds) is more of friendship building than romance building, and you have to have an appreciation for the story more than looking to romance some hot guys. I came into the game understanding this, after reading reviews that said the romance is in Edo Blossoms, I can completely confirm this.

Kyoto Winds is, in essence, the very long common route to Edo Blossoms, where sometimes the MC might figure out she has some sort of feelings towards a LI, but she's not entirely sure what those feelings are, if they exist at all, and then the ending practically says: To Be Continued. Does that make the game bad? No. I don't think so. Unless your aim is simply to kiss the dude, then you're going to be sorely out of luck in that regard.

What's good, bad, and in-between about this game?

Good: Several branching stories and paths. I feel like my choices actually matter. Different options lead to different revelations so repeated play throughs (and there will be many since there are 12 LIs) doesn't (yet) feel like a chore. Skip feature for read text, so when you do eventually know everything, you don't have to slog through 10 hours of the same story that you didn't find interesting. Saying that, there isn't much that I didn't find interesting. I reread every bit. Service Record section in the main menu, allowing you to pick up at a specific chapter instead of starting all over. Lovely art. Music I didn't get tired of hearing. Even considering the mystical aspects of this historical fiction, the stories were realistic and people were seriously injured or even died. I tend to enjoy when mortality is not only possible, but likely and the heroes (whether it be MC or LIs) don't have plot armor.

Bad: It really bothered me the amount of the game where there was no BGM. I understand stopping it for dramatic purposes, but sometimes it was simply gone for no reason, and for an extended period of time. And the scenes where they looped the same 2 seconds of background chatter to give the impression of busy areas, super annoying. MC is predominantly helpless. If you want a damsel in distress, this is perfect. Flimsy excuses for the MC's personality, both for flaws and strengths; it simply makes little sense for why she is the way she is and instead of just saying that's the character they input illogical correlations for causation. MC doesn't grow, really. The game takes place over 4 years and she's practically the same person from beginning to end.

In-between: MC is self-aware enough to acknowledge how useless, unintelligent, and inexperienced she is without dwelling on it, so it doesn't turn into a pity-party, nor spur any sort of fervent tasks to be a better person. Translation. It isn't that it is poorly translated, it's that the language is extremely modernized and Americanized, so certain ideas aren't expressed in a clear manner unless you know about Japanese culture and the Japanese vocabulary associated with those ideas that you so happen to pick up on through the verbal dialogue and not the written text. I don't see how it would be possible to get the route you're aiming for without a guide, if you are the type to aim for certain LIs. I tend to play and see where it takes me, but eventually I'll want to go down everyone's path, and I'm not sure I'll be able to without much trial and error due to the amount of choices that are either removed or changed based on previous choices.

TL;DR: It's really not a bad game, and I dare even say it is a GOOD game as long as you don't go in with expectations of steamy, romantic stories, light-hearted fluff, or men solely interested in the MC, since they all have their own agenda and MC is pretty much along for the ride.

review_text: I would say this is a great example of a very specific kind of game genre: the 'time-killer' game. It's a really fun experience for a 10-15 minute reprieve while doing something boring or mundane, like writing college essays, working in excel sheets, or doing taxes. In this way, it fills the kind of niche that games like Loop Hero fill: it's a fire-and-forget roguelike, but the outcomes matter, and the game has a nice sense of humor (I really liked all the pop-culture references). It's got style, the graphics look nice, and it's easy to learn while a bit more challenging to master. review_text:
This game is wasted potential. Yes, the game looks as cool as it does in screenshots. But that's where the praise ends. There is very little narrative; I get the idea of environmental storytelling, but I was hoping it would be something like Super Metroid or Oddworld where you get decent context even without any dialogue. This game's environments are simply too alien to deduce anything from them, and as a result you get nothing from them. They start to just blur into each other if none of them have any point or meaning; the whole game is just a Giger painting come to life, there is no feeling of originality that makes you remember the locations. 

The gameplay is dreadful. The combat is bad, and the puzzles are just put item A into socket B with the occasional pointless slide puzzle. It feels too "gamey" if you will, instead of the puzzles being a natural extension of the environment, it's just interacting with random panels that are strewn about the environment and trying to figure out which panel the devs want you to interact with first. In fact most of the challenge of the environments is trying to even figure out what you can interact with in the first place. There are UI indicators, but good game designers know how to separate interactables from the rest of the environment using visual clues. If you have to put a big white button next to them, you have failed.

It's like someone wanted to make a graphical showcase of Giger's work but stopped short of trying to figure out how gameplay and story would fit in. They clearly weren't sure whether to make it a puzzle game, a horror game, or a Doom clone, so what you get is some weird attempt at all 3 at various points, but with none of them done well. Simply put, there is not much to be gained by playing this. It's not an outright bad time, but it's not living up to its potential at all.

[h3]
[/h3]
As a fan of Sword Art Online, I was drawn to Fractured Daydream by the promise of 20 party raids and an engaging RPG experience. Unfortunately, the game failed to deliver in several critical areas.


[h3][b]Pros:[/b][/h3]
[list]
	[*][b]Mechanics:[/b] While it's probably one of the better SAO titles on the market, that's not really saying much.
	[*][b]Earnable Cosmetics:[/b] Some cosmetics can be earned, but at an extremely low drop rate, or through story quests by defeating a random named monster.
[/list]


[h3][b]Cons:[/b][/h3]
[list]
	[*][b]Unpolished Gameplay:[/b] The gameplay isn’t buggy but is far from polished, feeling more like an unfinished beta.
	[*][b]Poor Storyline:[/b] Shallow and not engaging for those unfamiliar with the previous titles or anime/novels.
	[*][b]Stamina System:[/b] The stamina system for flight feels more like a penalty than a fun experience.
	[*][b]Repetitive Quests:[/b] Most quests are tedious and repetitive, offering little variety or challenge.
	[*][b]Microtransactions:[/b] Mostly cosmetic skins that aren’t heavily pushed, but still a factor.
	[*][b]Performance Issues:[/b] Even on high-end systems, the game struggles with performance issues and long load times.
[/list]


[b]Overall:[/b] Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream fails to live up to its potential. The grind to reward ratio is astronomically low, making it a frustrating experience. I would recommend picking up Granblue Fantasy: Relink if you’re seeking a fun action RPG co-op or single-player experience. Save your money and your time—this game isn’t worth it.

It really sucks to have to say I don't recommend this game, but it's just not very good. The campaign is a complete mess with what feels like the majority of it being a series of forgettable mini-games. What little that has actual care and effort put into it is surprisingly good, but those moments are few and far between. The first hour of this game sets expectations very high but the rest simply does not deliver.

The developer's excuse is that Bonelab is supposed to be more of a modding platform or pseudo-engine like Garry's Mod or Little Big Planet, but those games give players full access to the ultimate tools for creating anything and everything. They can be excused for having a lack of built-in content because the ease in which players can create their own has resulted in an overflowing cornucopia of free to download addons. Bonelab lacks built-in content and its mod tools suck, as they lack functionality and are not intuitive or fun to mess around with. This has caused a content drought, which is a death sentence for any game attempting to survive off community creations.

At the end of the day what we have here is a game without enough valuable content to warrant the price tag, and that's pretty much the end of it.

I will say while the sound design, overall is good, the volume off the sounds is a little low and I do recommend increasing your audio device's audio until you can hear your footsteps while "sprinting."

Enjoy looking at 4000 hour lore breakdowns of the game on YouTube to "understand™" the game. I truly think this game will only people who want to deliberately spend their money without worrying about the value to time ratio and or the quality of gameplay mechanics.

review_text:
I really wanted to like this game but I just couldn't. I was always interested in it since it released on Epic Store, but am not going to buy something there so I let it bake. Periodically I would see an article from a gaming journal how it had a significant update or how good the atmosphere and mechanics of this game were. 

But in my opinion it falls flat on it's face. I love roguelite/like games. I love Noita, Risk of Rain, Gunfire Reborn, Dead Cells, Returnal, Hades, ect. A high octane shooter that incorporates these mechanics (much like Returnal) sounds like a great concept.

But none of my 5 runs felt different than any of the others. Unless I brought a different weapon they were the same. And I cleared 2 out of 3 of the maps.

Maybe it gets better later, but the pacing is terrible. The first two maps are complete snoozefests and the difficulty is not so much hard as it is tedious because you simply run out of ammo versus die to a powerfully enemy because you are too weak / or not skilled enough / or too much going on that you don't react to the enemies attack in time. So you run across the map to get ammo then go back. 

The graphics are good, the gunplay seems nice, and the gameplay (when there is some) is decent but could be better. But the pacing: God awful.

There are huge gaps in doing well - anything. You run around the island clearing points on the map and if you clear them all you leave to do it again. You cannot go everywhere as you are gatekept by certain upgrades initially. You grind essentially for souls to level up at the main hub. The magic aspect of it seems like a sidepiece gameplay mechanic stapled on afterwards. 

Truth be told, playing this game just made me want to play Returnal if I want an atmospheric roguelite shooter. 

Maybe it gets better, but I don't want to gamble $30 on whether it does. I have a big enough backlog to play. I want to like it, but I'm amazed at how bad the starting experience is.

review_text:
[b]A whole new breed of survival horror emerges with Cronos: The New Dawn.[/b] LOL

From a Galaxy far-far away. Your dreams are becoming true. You’re about to touch them… just with a bit of money spent. Ah, those marketing divisions, if they learned anything about the gaming industry it’s how to sell the expectations. And it’s disgusting.

Cronos could have been taking the best parts of Dead Space and Callisto Protocol and advancing them further. But it didn’t.

No matter what people are saying about Callisto, it has very good things: animations and fluidity in their execution and blending, no stutter when moving and transitioning in between different states, no “stick in the ass” feeling like Dead Space has, but still a very good feeling of heavy armor, and also very good approach opening a road to a very good melee combat system with evade moves that make sense - you don't roll in an armor, you sidestep and you keep the control of your space.

Drawbacks of Callisto are (1) its textures which are a bit generic (and it’s my biggest reproach to the game) - Dead Space has a better atmosphere because in that game textures are organic, you can feel them, they’re alien, scary; (2) its UI which tries to mimic the one from Dead Space, but it’s not doing well enough; and (3) AI restrictions (due to animations processing and queuing) - only one enemy can attack you, others are waiting (I was against this initially, but I learned to like this approach).

In Cronos when you touch something your character is not using his hands, there’s no animation for grabbing. It’s AA, but you don’t need to be AAA to make good animations nowadays with UE5, so those kinds of excuses are just bullshit talks. Cronos UI doesn’t take example from Dead Space, devs probably looked at all the similar games and took the one from Alien Isolation as something easy to implement. But while that UI fits well into the world of Alien, in Cronos it’s disconnected, it makes no sense, there’s no coherence.

Cronos is supposed to be a horror, but it’s not scary at all: scripted sequences when you know exactly which of your actions will trigger enemy spawns, simplistic AI which can’t follow the player through passages in walls (though from their looks and animations it’s clear they could) and either stands still or runs in circles like crazy headless chicken when pathfinding fails. It’s hilarious, but not scary. It negates the difficulty making the game very easy (and it’s also happening with elevations, not just passages).

The best part is the traversal. Because it’s made in the easiest way for devs to implement. If you think you’ve got freedom of movement, it’s false. You won’t do a free jump, it’s a predefined sequence and a non-fluid one (opposite to Callisto). For example, you won’t be able to jump down the floor even if it looks like you can - you need to find a predefined interaction point to do it. And the same mechanic is everywhere. Temporal anomalies (a bit of Stalker here or Quantum Break) - you need to find a premade interaction point to create a passage. And then finally like in Dead Space - you’ve got gravity boots. But you won’t be able to move freely with them - it’s one point to another, premade travel from A to B. So traversal is a fully scripted movement. And here we are - stutters  [b] -- processing... AI bloober team investigating....[/b] Bah ... Probably because Bloober Team did not manage the async loading of resources the right way.

So what’s left for the player? A combat system which is not good: push your trigger to use your weapon, but before that you need to collect resources to upgrade your damage to a comfortable level, because the progression is all about numbers.

Now why I stopped playing and refunded the game: when I got outside into the city I saw a big road with a small fence in between, so small you could step over it… but in this game you can’t. The same way as you can destroy a wooden crate with your stomp, but you can’t destroy a small wooden chair blocking a door. No logic. Sorry, but it’s not possible.

So now make yourself a favor if you did not play those games yet, go and grab them instead of Cronos :

Dead Space 1 . 2 . 3
Alien Isolation
Returnal (eager to see the upcoming Saros) 
Lost Planet 3
SOMA
Callisto Protocol

* NOTE :  I was puzzled by the music of the steam main video trailer. It's Polish-Ukrainian band Zazula ? right. But I was betting hard on Siouxie & the Banshees ... bah ... strange days.

review_text:
bought the game hoping for decent action game, didn't get that.

stayed for 300hrs to figure out whats good, what works, how it works etc.

in the end, the experience is layer 1 shallow, there is virtually no skill expression, and the gearing/content loop is absurd, although they're *attempting* to address some of it in *season 2* they are still not fixing the fundamental errors that make this game absurdly unfun.

>progression is complete dogshit

you will spend the first 70-80hrs of your game experience just trying to reach rank 100, post season 2, the grind to 50 will be reduced, but the worst part of it (85-100) will be untouched. there is also no-one playing the content of the lower ranks/world-tiers. CPU/bot lobbies are dreadfully slow and teach you nothing of the game, even worse, is that the content you're doing is Co-Op quests, which by r100 you will find out all the knowledge you have accrued is absolutely worthless as r100+ content is exclusively boss raids

>the enemies don't fight you

you either roll the enemies to death in half a second, or you find arbitrary ways to avoid or mitigate them entirely. this includes bosses, but with how bad the ping is, you essentially just smack a big wall until it kills you (you're only dying in EX) for an action game with perfect guards/dodges, you almost never use them (also a DPS loss.)

>the gearing is abysmal

in endgame, you will need to setup your build with a specific set of equipment with desirable traits. getting a legendary item, is pretty fucking rare (1 in 10 on average iirc) then getting the item for your class-type (1 in 6) AND then getting the correct legendary trait (1 in about 5 or so depending on the item) AND then you need to farm several legendary and epic items to take stat lines for to create a desirable item. for every character. for every build.

weapons are almost entirely worse as for most characters, 75% of legendary effect options are ass, and one is locked to a specific element. even then, you require a weapon of every element that character has access to, with desirable traits, desirable legendary effect, then its RNG whether or not its EX (objective 10% dps increase) and if its lv.98-100 (average loss of 1.2% per level iirc)

in my 300hrs, with what i consider to be extremely lucky (and i was always 4-stacking in one of, if not, THE fastest party on the entire game) i was only able to fully gear up 2 characters. (silica/eiji) most players will never get fully optimised gear unless they're 500hrs deep.

i won't even go into how some of the BiS traits like crit have like a sub 2% chance of even appearing on gear, or the fact blue rarity and below cannot be used to take traits from, as i'd be writing a 50k word international crisis report.

>combat is very bland and expressionless

all characters share the same attack sequence profile, there are no jumpcancels to take advantage of, guard/dodge cancels are often suboptimal and have an arbitrary cooldown between uses and are very clunky. every character essentially boils down to "find optimal normal attack chain, find optimal skill, use off cooldown and repeat" with absolutely no exceptions. a lot of the top-tier characters have basic skills that can be indefinitely looped for easy, free damage.

as expected, there are no hard execution characters, one resource heavy character who is bugged as fuck, a couple of gimmicks that are mostly shared amongst several cast members at the same time etc. combined with a lack of response from the enemies, there is just nothing satisfying or fun. again, basic overview, but i only really have negative things to add.

>balancing (not just character balancing)

the roster is horrendously balanced, from characters having easy damage that infinitely tracks and has no weaknesses to characters who carry every utility, to characters who literally do the exact same thing BETTER than another character because "lol", and some characters who are incapable of doing virtually anything. the balancing is an absolute mess.

element damage fundamentally in my opinion upsets the game balance entirely, and makes balancing the game impossible from a developer standpoint. element adds a flat 20% additional damage boost to any damage done on an enemy, provided you hit them with the element they are weak to. (relink anyone?)

where the issues comes in, is that all (besides 3) characters are missing at least one element from their weapon roster. and mobs, where present in boss raids, might have a different elemental weakness than the boss, and finally, the BIGGEST problem, is that all characters have at least one elementally-locked skill.

the issue here, is that certain characters now have certain parts of their moveset completely made redundant or useful based on ONE select piece of content. sometimes an ENITRE CHARACTER becomes completely unplayable if their missing element is the weakness of the boss in current rotation. even worse yet, characters can have legendary effects on their weapons to change their elementally locked skill into a new element, which is also fixed to one type only, and grants a FURTHER 20% damage boost vs. that element. making gearing and character power even more matchup dependant.

review_text:
This game likes to present you with gameplay taxes in the guise of gameplay mechanics. Difficulty is inflated by meaningless comedy dialogue exchanges which generally result in unpredictable penalties. Flexibility in building teams is mixed, as both the singular healer units and the singular tank units are obligatory picks due to the combination of zero sources of consistent healing, tiny unit health pools, and high enemy damage. Cross your fingers that you get the opportunity to fill your army with these units. DPS units are your only flexibility source, and they're largely interchangeable in effectiveness.

Above all, the food mechanic presents nothing of enjoyment and is perhaps the fastest tax clock I've ever encountered. Extremely frustrating as the game is a room-tile exploration type game, and if you somehow ended up at the wrong side of the grid from the boss, you are going to be taxed for every room backtracked.

The auto chess style is there, but held back by key factors. The food system discourages you from building up your strategy/army. The loss of items on unit death means you may have your synergies strangled in the crib, or your army crippled permanently after a hard battle. Before battle, you can see where enemies will be, but not what kind of unit they will be. This means there's little to no point in adjusting your formation, as you simply cannot strategize meaningfully against what you will face. Perhaps most importantly, the effects of stacking units in a class just aren't that interesting. Extremely simple base effects, with equally simple raw number increases.

The game is gorgeous and I like everything about the concept, but the experience just doesn't spark joy. I'm a roguelike player by far and above every other genre I play, I'm no stranger to randomization, rough starts, and playing by what the RNG graces me with. This game just doesn't give you enough to work with.

review_text:
Samorost 2, originally released in 2005 and remastered in 2020, is a short point-and-click adventure with absurd art, quirky humor, and a surreal alien world. While it has nostalgic charm and appeals to a niche audience, its gameplay might not hold up for everyone.

Pros:

Unique art style: The absurd, alien-inspired visuals stand out, though some textures in the remaster are inconsistent in resolution.

Achievement-friendly: Completing all achievements is straightforward—all you need to do is finish the game.

Affordable and short: It’s a cheap game that you can finish in under an hour.

Runs well on Steam Deck: The touchscreen-like controls make pointing and clicking intuitive and enhance the experience.

Helpful Steam community guide: Steam’s  guide section is incredibly useful, helping you avoid getting stuck and making the game more enjoyable.

Cons:

Puzzles lack clarity: The game doesn’t teach its mechanics well, like needing multiple clicks to interact with some objects, which might leave new players stuck.

No clear objectives: Upon entering a stage, the game doesn’t always provide a clear goal. You only realize the objective after solving the puzzle, which makes figuring out the logic more challenging. While this might be a hallmark of older point-and-click games, it doesn’t make the experience more enjoyable.

Alien logic: The puzzles can feel unintuitive due to the surreal setting, often requiring trial-and-error.

Progression bug:

[spoiler] After completing a puzzle, there’s a button on a recliner that may not work unless you restart the game. If you encounter this issue, simply reload the game, and the button should be functional. [/spoiler]

Overall:
Samorost 2 is best suited for fans of absurd art and humor or seasoned point-and-click players familiar with the genre’s quirks. For newcomers or those seeking a polished experience, it may feel more frustrating than enjoyable. While it offers nostalgic charm and a quick, inexpensive playthrough, its lack of modern quality-of-life features might not resonate with everyone.

review_text:
Witchfire, on the surface, seems like it should be a lot of fun. The idea of a PvE extraction shooter with the grit of a souls-like sounds really appealing! But in reality, this game just doesn't deliver a FUN experience, and ultimately, doesn't respect the time of the player.

This game has a serious issue with how it handles it's progressions, taking way to long to feel worthwhile, especially in the early game. There's no reason why I should be playing this single player game with the same starting loadout for 3 hours. It takes AGES to unlock anything new, being tied to 'Real Time' timers, which I'm sure is fine if you like to drown all your time into a single game, but for someone like me, it's frustratingly slow and unsatisfying. If any game that you play has the caveat that it gets better after "x" amount of hours, then it's just not a good game.

Witchfire also feels like it missing a core mechanic that all the souls games have (and the vast majority of extraction shooter for that matter), which is online gameplay. It's a lot easier to get lost in a game for hours on end when you've got a friend to play through with, but instead your slogging through the first couple areas by yourself while you wait for things to unlock. It just feels like a gaping hole in the gameplay, and with the developers staunchly against it, it feels like they're gimping themselves. Much like the souls games, I don't necessarily think it needs to be primarily a multiplayer game, but having the option of co-op would do the game a lot of good in the long run.

On a positive note, I think the visuals and atmosphere of this game are awesome. Artistically this game does everything right, from visuals to sound design. It's obvious they had a lot of skilled artists on their team. It's a cool premise with a lot of SICK visuals, and everything works together to really sell the vibe this game is going for 100%. It has the exact kind of dark gothic vibe that you would want from anything that carries the souls-like tag. Hell, even the shooting feels satisfying and fun! And thats coming from someone who RARELY plays shooters. But that polish starts to fall away when the gameplay begins to feel stale, using the exact same loadout for the first few hours with no change, praying that whatever you unlock next is something you'll actually enjoy using.

Theres a real gem of a game here, it's just buried under layers of unfortunate, un-fun decisions, and quite a few timers.

Edit:: Since it was pointed out, it's worth saying that I actually played a handful of hours at a friends house before playing my own copy, so I have netted around 3 or so hours of gameplay. Take that how you will!
