The game has so many levels that you get to clear and get completion tag as a acheivement. The levels are not very hard and dont demand your impulses and compulses to get 100%... still there is challenge and your time as well as some stress can be handled. 

Graphics

The game is 2D game which has good details on game objects, there are translucant game object and game effect which blends with backgound nicely. The colors on these game objects as well as background can convay good amount of situation as well as atmosphere of level. The textures on objects of certain gameplay feature are indicative such that you can get a idea, for example black goo balls are simple entity where gray when picked by mouse shows effect of pull on certain other gray ball, green shows similar effect towards black, gray or other green balls of removable attachment. pink is also passive where red ones are explosive. chain-reaction with combination of these balls of goo is also convayed nicely. Wind efect is also nice with indication on direction.

Physics 

It has realistic physics on goo balls such that it falls, rolls and bounces with deform on certain surfaces. Structure that we build to clear level has bridge building characteristic and we need to understand atleast a basic knowledge on whether certain iteration of user's imagination of bridge, overpass or platform structure is stable or not. then level can get cleared very easily. structure deforms as well on certain levels with enviornmental effects. The pulls that is programmed on goo balls with physics engine is very similar to springs... and visible to great extent when there is a level of hanged figure, item or puzzle that require building a hanging structure. Tower building is also involved to reach a certain height and goal destination.

Gameplay

Goo balls can be picked, thrown and moved with mouse. The 2D physics engines Laws greatly provide realistice behavior on these items. The drag and drop moves is used to build, solve these physics puzzles. There are bugs-Entities on game level which when used, undo's a previous move and error can be corrected with flashy quick screen effect. Timing is also taken in notice to give 100% completion Tag but always it is not neccessory to progess and experience the story of this game. The levels are populated with sign-boards that provide Hints, messages, story quotes and statements to smartguys then level can get cleared with good focus and game experience...

Sound
The sound on these game is addictive and can provide you focus to solve a puzzle... Atleast i have not experinced a situation where i need to mute the sound track to clear the clutter and noice to be on puzzle solving... still some times backgound enviornment's clutter is more satisfying than actual sound track. once i liked no sound track, peace-full scenario to solve a challenge.

Overall It is a Great game with physics to experience and dosent need great hardware configuration to play...

review_text:
43 Hours | 100% Achievements (The True Dawn)

Let me be clear: Cronos: The New Dawn is a superb survival horror experience, but it’s one that demands mastery and respect for its core mechanics. Hitting the 100% achievement mark felt like earning a degree in resource management and strategic combat, and if you’re looking for a title that rewards deep commitment, this is it.

The Atmosphere and World (10/10)
Bloober Team knocked the atmosphere out of the park. The grim, brutalist architecture of 1980s post-apocalypse Poland combined with the unsettling sci-fi aesthetic is truly unique. Exploring the ravaged wasteland as the Traveler, jumping between time periods to unravel the mystery of "The Change," is constantly intriguing. I spent hours hunting down every audio log and text file, and the lore here is dense, disturbing, and genuinely compelling.

Strategic Combat and the Merging Mechanic
This is where the game earns its survival horror stripes, and why the "Mixed" reviews don't understand the depth. Cronos isn't a fast-paced action game; it’s a constant tactical exercise.

    Charged Shots are King: Learning to prioritize charged blasts and headshots for ammo efficiency is essential. Normal shots are a waste of precious resources.

    The Merging Mechanic: This is the genius layer of difficulty. Every encounter is a puzzle: Do I spend my precious Pyre fuel to burn the corpse now, or risk a nearby Orphan merging with it to become a heavily armored, acid-spitting abomination? When you get deep into the game, failing to burn a body quickly means an immediate, terrifying difficulty spike, which is what made the hardest encounters so satisfying to overcome.

The 100% Journey
My 43 hours weren't just running through the story. Achieving all the cores, finding every collectible, and unlocking all the suit upgrades is a massive undertaking. The 37 Cores are expertly hidden, forcing you to use the time manipulation puzzles and Gravity Boots to fully explore every corner. If you are an achievement hunter, this game is perfectly paced to push you to the brink of your resources while rewarding your exploration with meaningful power progression.

Final Verdict
If you love strategic survival horror games like the modern Resident Evil remakes and Dead Space, and appreciate a punishing difficulty that you can eventually conquer through mastery and resourcefulness, buy this game. It is a slow, tense, and incredibly rewarding journey to the "New Dawn."

TL;DR: Strategic survival horror masterclass with fantastic atmosphere and lore. The merging mechanic ensures every fight is tense, and the collectibles/upgrades are essential for the full experience. A must-buy for genre fans.

review_text:
Where do we begin with this? PSO2 (aka New Genesis) is an online ARPG (not MMO as some may be misled to believe) that follows the trials and tribulations of the ARKS military squadron --a special group that harness supernatural abilities known as photons that provide them supernatural strength and finesse-- that defends humanity from the Dark Falz threat. Dark Falz being an entity that transcended from dark matter into a physical form. The protagonist (who is named Ash by default but is never referenced as such) is dragged into an occurrence that swings destiny into another direction when he meets a young woman named Matoi, whom of which requests to be killed. I won't be speaking of the story itself to avoid spoilers, but needless to say it starts off very slow. Anime filler slow. You're basically tasked on running through preset areas cleaning up threats, and occasionally fighting bosses (that get recycled as you go along) while also getting story beats that unveil more of the solar system you're fighting for.

PSO2 has a class system that utilizes different skilsets and weapons. Hunter is your mainstream melee class, Ranger focuses on long range, and Force is a go-between that focuses on techs (or basically magic). There's also Summoner which is one of the most interesting classes with its pet system, but also requires a lot of learning and commitment to get the most out of it. Not a beginner friendly class but one I would suggest trying.

PSO2 is a great game that unfortunately got put on life support to make way for NGS.
NGS is a bad expansion that really needed another year, at least, to make it seem like it's a solid contender to keep the franchise on par with other online RPGs. The story is so dreadfully weak in contrast to PSO2. There are hundreds of mangaka that write compelling stories which put whatever NGS has done to shame. SEGA really dropped the ball hard when they also removed planet based seed exploration for an open world that is mostly empty space and large cliffsides. 

NGS introduced FOMO to appease shareholders, as SEGA had to devise a setup that would keep the population numbers at a "fine" incline. The community has dried up tenfold and it's quite disappointing that only those with Stockholm syndrome are sticking around. I'd say that I'm part of the issue, yet I'm also self aware enough to know that I despise this gameplay design. If you're seeing people idle in the city hubs, then that alone is proof that the game has no merit or worth. It has now turned into a glorified social hub.

Speaking of which, NGS has a high level of degenerates (far more than I ever saw in PSO2) that try to make their characters look as inhumanly erotic as they can go. SEGA are at fault for making clothing that is quite clearly crossing the line, but the players who partake in that are setting a very bad example. There's also open communication in these hubs where groups would get together and either have childish arguments over in-game meta, spam R18 illustrations (known as symbol arts), and engage in erotic roleplay. Thankfully, you can disable such unsightly behavior by blacklisting such players. This has no impact on matchmaking with them.

My play time on Steam isn't reflective of the 5000 hours I have through Xbox One (where I started with the closed beta). Seeing a game that I had so much passion for decline into a deteriorated mess leaves me wondering what happened.

Oh, that's right. Hamazaki.

review_text:
I've played the previous sniper games and I have to say this one has a lot of very glaring and almost game breaking issues that I find to just be frustrating. Let me first start of by saying visually this game looks fantastic though sound design is a little odd if not jarring at times but it can be looked past. Now for some of the issues I have with the game.

1. The AI of the enemy units/cameras/etc.

I found this being that it is what you deal with majority of the time to be able to have super human senses due to the fact that I found myself at times being spotted by cameras behind walls. Or being spotted when an enemy is on a platform right above me when there is no way i would've been in the view of the enemy to begin with. Or when you go to throw a rock to distract the enemy, instead of them going to investigate the sound they walk right up to you instead even though no sound was made by your character at all. This nearly defeats the point of stealth or trying to be stealth as I just found myself killing guards because it seemed like sneaking around they would spot me anyways. There were even times I was laying in the tall grass behind a group and was spotted even though their backs were turned to me. I feel that this issue destroys the idea of being stealthy and sneaking past pointless fights as it just lead to me killing groups just to progress anyways.

2. The combat.

 Yes I know the game is primarily a stealth sniper game but there are times you're forced or dropped into a fire fight that you have to use your secondary weapons to handle it. I found the secondary weapons clunky and just about as useless as the sniper rifle at times. Weapons either had a sudden and uncontrollable kick or just felt completely ineffective at doing anything to an enemy while they could dispatch you just by looking at you. Combat in itself feels clunky and awkward as you feel like you're moving around in a big heavy suit and you have to make deliberate actions in order to move or fire back in combat. It feels more like an after thought than something that was intended in the game. It also seems like hit boxes are not matched up with the character models when you shoot at them. There are times my shots though looked dead on would pass through a target's head or right through them leading to me getting spotted and killed.

3. Key mapping.

   Isn't much to really say but a serious lack of being able to remap keys and functions just are something I don't like and I find myself hitting the wrong keys for certain functions just because I know for other games it's how I would've had them set for.

4. Frame drops


  Now I don't know if this is just me or anyone else is dealing with this but I do get times where I will be at about 60 or so fps and then it will spike down to 5 at random times. It has caused me to screw up shots or over step out of cover and get spotted. Not sure though but this could just be something on my end that could be an issue and not the game itself but I felt it was worth noting.


  Now I'm not saying I would not recommend because I want to blast this game but I know for many this isn't going to be the game for them. And with glaring issues I've dealt with while playing I know many are going to be frustrated through playing it. Finding myself going through missions with a lot of trail and error due to AI spotting me in areas that they couldn't have seen me in etc. As for the level design, visuals, voice acting, and the like I have no issue with it. Just the gameplay with dealing with enemies and the like are well... they need work and I do know the dev team is working on it and i hope as time goes on it gets its kinks worked out. But as for what it stands right now I can't recommend this game to others at it's current state. Perhaps later down the line that will change but for now I really can't do that.

review_text:
Just finished the first playthrough.

Generally, another positive addition to Bloopers catalogue. How I am viewing Blooper atm is the younger CDPR of survival horror that has so much potential but needs more time. Of course, they absolutely smashed the remake of Silent Hill 2 and for them to even try that and pull that off goes to show how far they can go in the future.

Overall I would give this game a solid 7/10, maybe a weak 8/10. 

Gameplay is pretty nice and punchy with a great balance between resources/enemies and pacing.
Story has great pacing with so many questions rather than answers which does add to the want to push on (imo).
Level design is also pretty appropriate and nice throughout, not too difficult in regards to puzzles/fights but not too difficult. 
Enemy variance is also nice and in my opinion has an almost perfect curve in game progression and difficulty.
The story left me feeling as if it could have done with something more, but not too disappointed. It is hard to describe without spoiling it.

Overall this game was a blast to play and did not feel bored at any point. Takes a lot of inspiration from other franchises but successfully adds its own identity which I appreciate, especially in todays age. This is a Solid AA-esque game. Saying that as well, I got this game for just under 30 GBP which I feel is the right price for it. For 50 GBP I would say that is quite a bit too steep for what is on offer here (Whereas SH2R is totally worth 50GBP imo ha).

I would totally recommend and will probably play through this again to get the other achievements and just enjoy what is on offer in the harder difficulty at some point. Something in which I rarely do nowadays.

I look forward to that next game from this gem of a studio! Recommended!

I don't want to give this game a thumbs down, but Steam doesn't give me a neutral button, so...

Best game in the trilogy in terms of gameplay, but it’s not my favourite game in terms of atmosphere and story. The main story, while good, is VERY short and is quite fragmented – it’s like the writers were trying to stuff the story with all supervillains they could think of without explaining why. The majority of the gameplay is made up of side missions, riddles, collectibles. Oh, and to get 100% completion, you are forced to complete the extra “Riddler’s Revenge” Mode as well, which I ABSOLUTELY LOATHED. It consists of mini games that have nothing to do with the main story. I tried to force myself to do the challenges, but I did not enjoy them at all, so in the end, I just gave up.

I applaud Rocksteady for trying something new in the sequel, but I’m sorry to say that it just isn’t as good as Arkham Asylum. Open-world system isn’t suitable for most story-driven games and this is a textbook example of that, especially for a dark and atmospheric story like Batman. 

That said, it isn’t a bad game at all, it’s just that I wish they made the story longer and make the game less bloated (with fillers). 

7.5/10

review_text:
Have you ever consumed a piece of media that was just okay? You watched it, your opinion wasn't one direction or another? Realistically, that is my experience with Callisto Protocol. 

The game is fine. The story is generic, the setting is generic, the combat is repetitive; however, it still holds a charm that many games miss. I will not advocate you to buy this full price. This is not a game worth more than maybe ten dollars at best, but if the setting/plot interests you, I'm sure you'll get value from it.

Many of the original complaints for this game regarding performance and lack of "dead space-y" vibes have been addressed with content patches and actual development time. For people craving the DS experience, there is dismemberment mode now, and that more or less, makes enemies lose limbs whenever you shoot them or hit them hard. It's satisfying and certainly more interesting than the combat of the main game which most revolves around you holding directional keys to avoid attacks then counter. 

This isn't a huge thumbs up review, this is however, a review that is middle ground. It is not absolute dogshit like some may make you think. The game functions, there were no crashes, there were no huge audio/visual/control bugs. 

If you want space horror and are okay with a bit of slop, you'll get a nice 6-8 hour playthrough from this.

review_text:
Samorost 2 is a pretty exercise in frustration.  Graphical layering glitch hid the inside of one location (snail's house) and I was unable to control the main character to move anywhere in hopes of retriggering the view.  Fortunately the clickable things remained clickable even while hidden...  My cursor kept disappearing on entering the conveyor belt tunnel and I had to keep clicking randomly to cause it to reappear.  I used a walkthrough in basically every location as certain things like dials and strings and labels on dials were often too small for me to recognize as interactive and significant against the incredibly detailed background.

Some puzzles were entertaining, but often things happened with little explanation of what was going on.  Also, the bad guys' plot is something out of Team Rocket from Pokemon - They attack with opportunity this one animal with a caring owner even though there are potentially many abandoned ones out there who might be better off with them...

This is a great game studio and they improved the interface in later entries.  Probably better off in general buying some of those and checking out the art in motion of this game through video clips.  If you do play this and have similar problems navigating, might be a good idea to have that option for the computer system to magnify everything around the cursor handy.

review_text:
Haunting and phantasmagoric, Scorn is a convulsing nightmare of an experience. The game showcases some of the most stunning visuals and sound design the medium has to offer. I frequently found myself stopping just to absorb the striking level of detail in the environments. There is a strange and alien story unraveling before you, solely communicated through Scorn's immaculate environments. Strange whispers echo the halls while gurgling, fleshy masses comingle with machinery. The atmosphere is laid on thick and refuses to let you go until the game's final striking and thought-provoking moments.

Scorn is less of a game and more of a visual and auditory experience. In fact, Scorn is at it's best when it's not trying to be a game. I found that the pacing was disrupted by the gameplay and puzzle elements and would have much preferred exploring the world uninterrupted. What sparse mechanics Scorn does present are never explained. For example, I found myself in a section where I only had one bar of health and copious amounts of enemies. I kept dying in one hit and couldn't understand how I was supposed to complete the area when I die so easily. I only discovered that I could heal myself by accident when I stumbled upon the key to do so in the menus. I don't need or want weapons and combat when the world and the story it tells is this engaging. Scorn really would have benefited from embracing more of a "walking simulator" design principal and forgone the tedious combat though I will say the deliberate obfuscation of all of it's mechanics does lend itself to a sense of this space being truly alien.

Scorn, while rough around it's edges mechanically, is a one-of-a-kind and unforgettable journey through a demented alien landscape that I will be thinking about long after I've uninstalled it from my machine. It's not for everyone but no great piece of art is. Giger and Beksiński would be proud.

review_text:
Starship Troopers: Extermination is an OKAY game at best and is the poor man's Helldivers 2. Right off the bat you notice a big problem when you join a random match. There are 15 other random people and at least 13 people have no idea what they are doing. Most missions have objectives that aren't killing bugs and unfortunately killing bugs is the only thing those 13 other players do. So missions take twice as long as they should or the mission fails because you get overrun. Imagine Helldivers 2 chaos, but with even more DUMBA** players. 

The game is also very buggy, expect to get stuck on things. Expect the bugs to have bugs, it's really interesting watching the enemy bugs stand around like they are lost on what to do. It's even more interesting to watch the bugs glitch through walls and buildings. This doesn't look good, and it doesn't seem to be a high priority for the devs to get it fixed. I've read a lot of people complain about how the game runs on their machines, I noticed lag for a moment maybe once in 4 matches but overall optimization didn't seem like it was a problem for me. 

Also there are solo missions that teach you the various mission types as well as show you the ins and outs of the bug killing community. However, the problem with that is, the AI in your squad are piss poor teammates. It makes the solo missions so awful that you'll just want to skip them and most probably do. Which also explains why random players in your matches have no idea what to do but point and shoot bugs.  

One positive if you like this kind of thing, ST:E is quite a bit more chaotic than Helldivers 2, only because I think there's more going on. You have the ability to build in this game in certain parts of missions. Mostly you are building defenses but that can get quite crazy with 16 people building wildly. You'll then be tasked with protecting your base by killing bugs and repairing defenses. It'll be nonstop explosions. You'll have smoke, fire and bug guts all messing with your vision to make it even more insane. Overall the experience is very intense in those parts of each mission.

My thoughts for an overall grade on my review is a positive IF you are are getting it on sale. I don't believe it is worth $29.99 USD in it's current state. If you don't have friends to play with, you probably won't enjoy playing with randoms. You'll likely be stuck doing the boring parts of the mission if you even want a chance to pass the mission. It has too many glitches and things that simply aren't getting fixed. I don't believe the the developers (Offworld) truly are going to take the time to improve the game in the ways it needs it most. I suggest 9 times out of 10, you should pass on ST:E and go play or buy Helldivers 2 instead.

Let me tell you about my wild ride with The Callisto Protocol - the game that made me scream, hide under my blanket, and... buy it twice! First on Xbox, then on Steam, because sometimes you just need to relive that terrifying magic. 


🌌 The Setting: Space Prison Gone Very Wrong
Imagine you're Jacob Lee (who's quite handsome even when covered in blood 💕), a space trucker stuck in Black Iron Prison on Jupiter's moon. Sounds fun? Well, not when your cellmates are mutating into horrible monsters!  

- So dark, so scary, so pretty!🔦 The graphics are amazing - every bloody corridor looks so real you'll want to touch it (but don't)  
- The sounds... oh the sounds! 🔊 Footsteps behind you, metal creaking, growls in the dark... My heart was beating so loud!  

---  

⚔️ Combat: Up Close and Personal  
You can't just shoot everything here - you'll need to learn melee combat! And you know what? It feels great once you get it.  

- Dodge, hit, repeat! 🎮 Every swing feels powerful, especially when enemies go splat
- Guns 🔫 are rare but satisfying. That shotgun? Pure monster-blending goodness!  

---  

👻 Horror Moments: Blanket Required 
If you like scary games that make you jump, this one delivers!  

- The monsters 👹 are disgustingly cool. Those Two-Heads? NOPE. Just nope.  
-  1️⃣ The Grunt (Your Basic Nightmare)
- The standard model, but "standard" here means "flesh melting off bones"  
- Comes in fun variants like Exploders (💥 surprise boom!) and Spitters (🤢 acid attack, ew)  
- Pro tip: Always check ceilings - they love to drop on you like terrible meat 

2️⃣ Two-Head (The Stuff of Nightmares)
- My personal sleep paralysis demon 👹  
- Basically two angry dudes fused together (relationship goals?)  
- That *scream* when it charges? I had to mute my TV twice  
- Funny story: First encounter made me throw my controller at my poor cat (she forgave me... eventually)  

3️⃣ The Blind (Sneaky Scary Boi) 
- No eyes, but HEARS EVERYTHING 👂  
- Tip-toe sections had me holding my breath IRL  
- Pro strat: Throw objects to distract them... unless you enjoy being gutted  

4️⃣ The Final Boss 
- Let's just say it involves creative use of human anatomy  

---  

💻 PC Version: Pretty But Demanding
I played first on console but the Steam version works great!  

- Graphics 🖥️ are gorgeous on max settings  
- Controls 🎮 feel better with a gamepad for dodging  

---  

The Not-So-Good Stuff  
- A bit short ⏳ (10-13 hours) but has replay value  
- Story 📖 is good but not amazing  

---  

💖 Final Verdict: Absolutely Play This! 
If you love horror with amazing atmosphere and visuals, this is a must-play. Even if you get scared easily like me!  

Score: 9/10 🌟 (for making me feel ALL the emotions)  

---  

Happy screaming, everyone! 👻

The base or "meat" of the game seems okay so far - environments look great, world is compelling, UI is polished. But it's got the worst combat of any of the big budget survival horror games. 

There is no dodge button, movement is too clunky/inertial to get away in combat, you have to charge shots to do damage, and some of the encounters are structured to where you can not kill/stagger an enemy before it reaches you. This leaves your defense option to be "strafe to the side of a pillar and hopefully their tentacle extension misses me."

Layer on to that other issues - ammo is more scarce than other survival horrors (RE, Dead Space, Callisto, Alan Wake 2) unless you spend upgrade currency on it which incentivizes save scumming, raised black levels/extreme fog (can be fixed with mods), way too zoomed in FOV with no toggle (can be fixed with mods), and traversal stutter, and it's hard to justify spending time with this game.

This game has suffered such a continual decline in content and quality in the last five years that it's really shameful. These current devs only seem to know how to use a microscope to squeeze players more and more where it isn't needed while adding nothing of value in the game. We used to get thoughtful and fun ships in the zen store regularly, now we get 3 gatcha box ships a month that are only worth a trait and 1 zen ship every 2 months that is completely worthless compared to the gatcha ships. We used to have events that gave rewards that excited you, now we get 10 year old queues shoved on us to get some crappy ground gear for a space game. 

I wish this game would die really but my idiot self started a fleet nine years ago and I have dozens of people that count on me to run it.  This game is a rotting corpse with a team that have shown they have neither the skills to move this game on or the vision. They would rather go play fantasy board games than do their jobs. They never fix anything and the list of complied glitches they refuse to or are incapable of fixing is pages long now. Recently, they decided the way to save money was increase instance size to use less servers....which has doubled load times. I mean it's just bad in so many ways when you see how it has went. They treat this game as nothing more than a place to collect stuff from Star Trek and that is what killed the game, not the power creep. review_text:
Scorn looks and sounds like nothing I’ve ever played before.

It’s a linear horror puzzle game, most reminiscent of a walking simulator but with combat sequences. 
Still, the gameplay isn’t what will stick with you after finishing this game (which you absolutely should).

Everywhere you look, you’re met with a hauntingly beautiful void, open yet claustrophobic. 
Every corridor oozes atmosphere, every room hums with its own distinct noise, and every surface feels grossly alive.

Its biggest flaw is the sluggish combat system, made worse by a frustrating one-slot autosave mechanic. 
Scorn flirts with survival horror but ultimately feels too slow and meditative to succeed in that genre.
Just keep in mind to pick off lone enemies with melee attacks, and stand still when firing to reduce spread.

I highly recommend playing this slow, taking your time to soak the environment in.

It's a just cause game in name and setting, and in that you blow things up. Beyond that, it feels rather hollow and unfinished.

It's got the region capture system of JC3, but instead of knocking over bases you just do a single mission and the region is up for grabs. Somehow has less map content then 3, and what feels like a smaller map then both 2 and 3. At least it has the different biomes like 2 did, but unlike 2 or 3 there was no reason to explore any of the map. 

The story was somehow lighter then in 2 or 3, with the main bad dude showing up I think a total of three entire times throughout the story.

There's no different heat levels, beyond if they'll send a helicopter or tank or something, but it's not like it means anything when most of the game is the same loop of go to base, kill bad dudes, complete one of three objectives. 

Honestly it's more of a JC1 remake with what seems futuristic in current year then it is a standalone game. I think it would have been better if that's actually what it was instead of what it ended up as. Compared to JC2 and JC3 it's just lacking over all.

It's not a functionally bad game nor an ugly one. The setting is nice to look at, the guns are pretty neat. The bases are more complex then any of the other games. Just a little disappointing that beyond the one mission at a base you need to do in order to get the region they aren't used for much else.

Over all Just Cause 4 is just bland, and doesn't hold up to the older entries in the series.

Atmospherically, visually and sound-wise, Scorn really does everything right. A strong stomach would be recommended, because the character goes through a lot in the course of the game that can only be described as sadistic torture in the real world.

I had a hard time evaluating the technical aspects of the game, because there are some weaknesses here. For example, it was very often difficult for me to solve the puzzles without help from the Internet. Absolutely nothing is explained to you in the game, you are faced with a puzzle and have to find out what you have to do in the first place. There is also a lack of variety in the number of enemy types in the game. There are only 5 different enemy types (with the final boss) in the whole game (4 of them are similar in appearance and behavior almost like one egg to the other). review_text:
Many game-breaking bugs and in-game incentives that ruin the fun. Gameplay loop involves running the same 5 missions repeatedly, trying to get weapon attachments or challenge skins. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there are too many reasons why their gameplay loop is not enjoyable.

Here are the primary reasons for not recommending. Note that most of the pros listed below are barely positive:
[h1] Pros [/h1]
- Gunplay feels okay, defo not the best but decent for a zombie shooter.
- Upgrade system is [b] mostly [/b] for convenience, which means new players would not be at a massive disadvantage due to missing attachments.
- Harvest is easy to come by, so it's easy to tinker with and try out different weapons.
- Voice acting is not awful.
- Music is pretty good.

[h1] Cons [/h1]
- Shooting while strafing with smg is too strong, means that as long as you can kite the zombies (snowbreed, whatever) near ammo, you do not need to strategize. At that point, killing them isn't a challenge, just time consuming.
- Many high-value challenges, especially the Nightmare challenges disincentivize teamwork, because it means you are fighting against your teammates to get enough kills in a given run if you want the skins.
- Quick reload is an inherent advantage over Advanced reload, and the Harvest bonus for Advanced reload does not mean anything since it does not make the mission easier. Most players using Quick reload will end up getting more Harvest anyways due to their advantages with up-time/DPS and versatility.
- Weapon attachment rewards being completely randomized, whether a duplicate or not, is frustrating and artificial padding to keep end-game people playing longer.
- AI pathing is frequently laughable. It is common to see zombies zig-zagging back and forth, slowly inching forward. This is especially noticeable on higher difficulties, which means they are moving faster, messing with their pathing even more.
- Peeker's advantage in the PvP mode is absolutely horrendous. Basically unplayable. Not an issue in harvest runs since the zombies don't have the same problem, though there is still plenty of desync, connection issues, and other issues in online runs.

[h1] Bugs/Bad Features [/h1]
- Using Index controllers, you are unable to hold weapons while simultaneously grabbing items or reloading. This puts players using Index controllers at an inherent disadvantage compared to Quest players.
- Door clipping still nullifies final stands, can skip them entirely and just finish the missions without fighting the last hordes of enemies. Obviously you don't need to, but when the alternative is mindlessly running in circles with your smg and unlimited ammo, you don't really feel like you're missing out on anything.
- You can still sequence break, as in if someone stays near the beginning of a checkpoint and there are gaps or jumps, you can never fail because most zombies will kill themselves (Including elites/bosses) when they realize they cannot get to where you are. Other sequence breaks where the zombies can still path to you mean that you can hold out in more advantageous positions than you otherwise would be able to. Takes more time, but guarantees success, which means it is currently one of the easiest Nightmare strategies.
- You still cannot reload your missile launcher at safe rooms.

This does not include inventory-wiping bugs and other network related issues. I also never addressed issues with bots since they did not massively impact my experience.

Needs a LOT of work to make the experience remotely engaging and cooperative. Even without the bugs and pathing issues, elements such as weapon balance, circle-strafing, and end-game rewards are still huge problems that would need to get addressed.

review_text:
This game is tedious.  There is exactly ONE solution to every level.  You job is die an extraordinary number of times trying to discover the one, single way that the developers want you to solve the puzzle.  There is absolutely zero room for creativity or spontaneity.  If you step out of the correct path for even a split second, you die.

Ultimately, this game tests your willingness to commit time.  If you are willing to sit through enough deaths to finally stumble upon the only right way to finish a level, then you will get to repeat the whole stupid exercise over again in a new map.  There is really no skill or learning, just grinding through death after death.  

If you dont mind this type of game (i.e. you like Sudoku puzzles), then this game is for you.  But if you like creative, emergent stealth games, then give this one a pass.

review_text:
2000+ hours 50/50 main.
TLDR: The meta is super trash right now with Survivors using sprint burst with the exhaustion cooldown perks and hard gen rushing. Killers are tunneling a lot (Generators are completed so quick they feel like they need a least one kill for the entire match. 

I don't blame the players on either side, they are just playing the game the way it is right now, the problem is with the game balance and direction that the developers are allowing it to go in. Any sense of proper matchmaking is just a facade, coop survivors are ultra unbalanced, and to play killer is just a sweaty stress fest if you are trying to compete in matches against SWFs, Meta-builds, and Gen Rushing (which these are all you get once you have enough time in the game).

Don't get me wrong, I still enjoy this game for the most part under the right circumstances, but when the bad parts of the game come out, it's really bad and makes me okay with taking extended breaks from the game until I feel like checking up on it again. I have been limiting my time and money that I am willing to spend on this game.

I really hope one day enough of our player criticism is heard and BHVR actually cares and does something truly meaningful to mend these issues, I know i'm not the only one and that there are plenty of players you feel the same way.

Additional perspective: From a Killers perspective, you are just here to "chase" the survivors around as the loop you across the map, complete Generators at high speed, you are here just to give them a sense of challenge, some hooks, maybe a kill or two at best, but just to allow them to have their power fantasy, especially against higher level survivors/teams. And if you happen to get to a good start and frustrate a survivor or two, expect them to immediately disconnect/throw the game.  If the matchmaking decides to swing too far in the other direction, you'll feel bad for dominating players who are obviously below average and probably just them go if you're nice. The Devs have even stated that they want this type of matchmaking ratio, which is obvious cope for an inability to actually balance the game and matchmaking. 

From survivors perspective, if you are in a sweaty gen-rushing meta perk pre-running tryhard squad then see above; for everyone else, expect to play against the most desperate bitter traumatized killers ever! Whoever gets the first hook is going to get tunneled out of the game ASAP, they will be so desperate for that early kill to slow down the probable gen-rushing. If you are teamed up with randoms, they'll just be running around the map like chickens with their heads cut off, leaving you to be the last survivor alive if you are competent and not tunneled... but what is your reward? To get slugged, left crawling on the floor while the Killer moves back and forth behind you in a humping motion insinuating Rape, until you bleed out, yes this happens a lot!

review_text:
The core of the game is fantastic, fun classes, fun base building, fun to shoot stuff. I really like this game a lot. It is a great experience with friends and it can be fun even "solo" with random players. My only complain is the party system or better to say in-match squad system when you can't guarantee playing with friends in a squad. But that is not the reason I'm labeling this as negative review.

If it was possible I would give this game a "neutral" review, it is playable but 1.0 introduced some stuff that rustles my jimmies.
1) Solo campaign
Who the hell thought this is a good experience.
I get it, at the end you get fully leveled class that you can hop in a real match without the feeling of being useless, right?
Except it won't explain anything to you, not even how your class works. 25 missions (~2,5h to finish it) and not a single base being built, only deconstruct for reasons unknown. Oh and the teammate AI? that gets literally stuck at the spawn teleporting like crazy so you can't even fix him by stay/follow command. Not that you need them for the most part, they are nice to have to revive you in the last 5 missions to rush through.. Who in the QC team thought this is fine? Who in the QC team thought...
I'm sorry for any newcomer that is going to go throught this and think this is what the game is all about.
The only good thing is slower introduction to [strike]all[/strike] most of the bugs. You are better off to play the basic bulding tutorial (that takes like 2 minutes) and have actual fun in PvE game.

2) Galactic Map - is fixed, nice

[strike]Or war, or front, whatever they call it. Thing I was most excited about is.. broken.
Only Company can join this and there is virtually no way to get in one for reasons mentioned many much times. You can make your own and play solo, but that is not what I want to do. I want to have company with my friends and play with friends. I wanna contribute to the war and earn the rewards.[/strike]

3) Skins
No, I don't mind the paid DLCs, even tho I expected the "first wave" being that, not orange hazard suit literally called "1st wave" but whatever, silly me. I am jelaous of PS5 players getting unique space tiger stripes for the galactic boogaloo. Yes, I got the game for free so can't really say I pre-ordered but we carried the development and all we got was this lousy orange skin.


[strike]Devs, don't waste your time doing nothing and fix the Company system asap at very least. Don't be another Payday 3, please.[/strike] I still stand behind the "neutral review" but props for fixing Companies.

review_text:
Star Trek Online (STO) is worth a try. [i]If[/i] you're a Trekkie. Otherwise, it's just outdated graphics and stale gameplay. It's entertaining, but quickly becomes repetitive.

There's a lot I could say about the game. Instead, I'd like to focus on the one aspect that led me to leave a negative review: the monetization.

The game is f2p. So, I expected microtransactions, and such. I was totally unprepared. Their in-game store contains [i]thousands[/i] of dollars of merchandise. This is not a game in which you are going to own everything. (Unless you are crazy-rich.)

The pricing is truly truly truly outrageous. Oh ho ho yeah. $30 for ONE ship. $5.50 for a costume. $12.50 to make your ship's bridge look like the Enterprise-D. Everything is just a little more expensive than you would expect.

Fans on the forums will tell you, "Yeah, but you can just grind and buy the stuff for free." This is true. You absolutely [i]can[/i] work to get the items for free. However, the time investment is hardly worth it.

The system is complicated. Try to follow me. 

Tier 6 ships (the highest tier, I believe) cost 3000 zen. 3000 zen costs $30. You can earn dilithium ore in-game by completing daily missions and repeating "Task Force Operations". (Which are equivalent to dungeons in most mmos.) You can refine up to 8000 dilithium ore per day. The refined version can be exchanged for zen. However, the exchange rate is roughly 500 dilithium for 1 zen.

So to obtain a $30 ship for "free", you would need nearly 1.5 million units of refined ore. At a rate of 8k per day, this requires around 180 days. 

Assuming you login and gain the 8k every single day. Which is estimated to take a little under 4 hours. That's 720 hours of your life you are never getting back. For a $30 ship. That's like working for $0.04 per hour. No way [i]I'm[/i] doing that! That's not even remotely reasonable.

(Edit: [b]To be fair,[/b] there's an easier way to obtain a free T6 ship. It's simply a matter of waiting for one of several yearly events. Then completing dailies until you get the required number of points.)

Oh, and loot boxes. With variable rarities. In other words, gambling. Because spending $3 on a box, $1.25 on a key to open it, and then getting a mundane item you could have acquired anywhere isn't at all exploitative.

STO isn't against twisting your arm. They hook me up with 4 bridge officers. Then 2 more, but they won't let me use the new ones. Why? Because I don't have enough "bridge officer slots". The only way to obtain more is to delete one I already have. OR spend money to unlock the slots.

Why even bother? Because my ship has 7 positions for bridge officers. Not being able to fill all the positions puts me at a disadvantage. In particular, my science station is empty. Due to this, I am denied an extra ability in space combat.

So, I need to buy 3 slots. However, the game only sells slots 2 at a time for $3 each. But the game will only sell me zen in amounts of $5 or $10. Which means I need $6 worth of zen for my ship to be fully-functional. So, I'm forced to buy $10, and then have 400 zen left I don't intend to use. Worse, I'm pretty sure you have to spend this with every character you make. (If you want to fill those positions.)

I really wanted to talk about the gameplay. Particularly, the space combat. However, none of it is worth it.

This game wants your money, and everything is centered around getting you to spend. I can't support a game like that. At least, not financially.

I will, however, still play for free. I'd like to see if the game has any more to offer that might change my mind.

Update: Playing more [i]did[/i] change my mind. Started to really enjoy it. Learned about more f2p options. Gonna go ahead and leave this a negative review. Since they arbitrarily decided to make the game cease to function on Windows 7. Despite the game having FULL capability of running on even a Vista. A game with graphics this dated (running on Dx9, no less.) has no reason to do this. No flaws of Win7 are a threat to STO in any way.

review_text:
A game that is brutal for all of the wrong reasons.

There is no in game tutorial or help files. There is nothing on their website beyond forums. You have to pause the game and Google to find how anything works.

You get messages/warnings about stuff going on but you can't click on them and go to the location. A monster is attacking a building but to find out which one you have to scroll across the whole screen to find it. A person is starving but there is no way to know where or who it is.

You can't tell the monsters from your people. The pixel art is too low quality to tell the vast majority of monsters from your people and there is nothing in the UI to help. If you hover over a monster it get's a red circle but this isn't always there. Monsters get lost in the art of the buildings and you aren't able to pick them out. Add to this if you cast a spell or a fire elemental sets something on fire and it's just a screen full of nonsense where you can't tell your people from the monsters.

The sourcing of materials is horrific. A piece of wood can be on the ground next to something that needs 1 piece of wood but the colonist will go across the map to get wood from where else. I built a wood storage area near where I was going to build other stuff, the settlers still went to the other side of the map to get stuff and ignored the storage. 

Pausing the game covers the screen and doesn't let you look for stuff. You know the stuff like who is hungry, what building is getting destroyed, and where or where could those monsters be.

They mention RimWorld on the store page, buy that instead of this. It's brutal and fun. Plus it has support for mods so if there is something that annoys you chances are someone has already fixed it.

review_text:
Interesting game mechanics.
6 chapters each with 5 objectives.
Played through on normal and was somewhat challenging.

Here is why I can't recommend the game.
Many times in each chapter I got stuck on the environment and couldn't get loose. I was force to load from last save.
Saves are few and far between.
Looting bodies requires you to be in a certain space between the enemies legs. Only when you get the ability to loot while melee killing is looting fast.

If the game is in the bargain bin its worth checking out, but I wouldn't pay a premium for this title. Maybe the second game has better game mechanics.
